one_line_positioning: "Build something Lovable" — a full-stack AI app platform (not a website builder) that turns one prompt into a production app with database, auth, payments, hosting, domains and enterprise governance, sold by credits rather than seats.
summary:
Lovable (Stockholm; $400M Series C at $13.3B announced 12 Aug 2026) positions itself as "One platform. Endless possibilities." — explicitly NOT a site builder. The homepage headline is "Build something Lovable" with the subhead "Bring a new product, internal tool, or entire company to life." Targets are stacked deliberately: solo founders at the top of the funnel, then "For Work" personas (Founders, Product Managers, Designers, Marketers, Sales, Ops, People), then Enterprise governance buyers. Logos shown: Adidas, Asana, ElevenLabs, Zendesk, Workday, Nvidia. Scale claims on-page: 1.2M new projects/week, 60M projects built, 900M monthly visits to Lovable-built projects.

END-TO-END FLOW. The landing page is a single centred composer floating on an animated mesh gradient — a 608×97px card, 28px radius, white at 80% alpha with `backdrop-filter: blur(4px)`, a 0.5px hairline border and a two-layer soft shadow. Inside: a "+" button (aria-label "Additional actions"), a ProseMirror contenteditable (aria-label "Chat input"), a "Build ⌄" mode chip, and a mic ("Start voice recording"). The placeholder animates as a typewriter — "Ask Lovable to create a landing page for my…" — fading with `transition-opacity duration-500 ease-out`. There is NO template chooser, NO style picker, NO questionnaire before the wall. You type, you hit send, and THAT submit is the signup wall. The prompt is preserved through signup (email, Google, GitHub, Apple), and you land in the dashboard/editor with the build already starting. Docs say "The first version takes a few minutes, and you can watch it take shape as Lovable works"; third-party reviews report a clickable app in under 10 minutes. Design quality is not left to chance: when a prompt is visually open-ended, Lovable generates THREE parallel HTML/Tailwind "design directions" to compare side by side (up to six refinements), or runs "design questions" — font pairs by aesthetic category, colour swatches "grouped by mood", wireframe layout options — and compiles the answers into a design brief with named fonts and hex colours. It skips this entirely for dashboards, admin tools, cloned URLs, or when a design template/system is attached.

BUILDER SHELL. Two panes: chat left, preview right. Top-left is the Lovable logo (opens the dashboard sidebar) then the project-name menu (workspace, plan, credit bar, "Get free credits", "Remix this project", "Design system"). A History toggle and a sidebar collapse (Cmd+B) sit alongside. A horizontal project toolbar switches Preview / Files / Code / More — More holds Analytics, Cloud, Agent integrations, Payments, Connectors, Security, SEO & AI search. Top-right: preview-toolbar toggle, comments, collaborator avatars, Share, Publish. Cmd+K is the command palette. The preview bar carries Desktop/Tablet/Mobile view, a page selector with custom paths, and Refresh (Shift-click = full environment restart). Idle previews pause with "Still building?" and a "Keep building" button.

EDITING MODEL. Two modes toggled with Option+P: Build (default, usage-priced) and Plan (1 credit/message, never touches code). Plan renders a full-screen structured document you can edit as markdown, or select any passage to get a "Describe the change…" box, then review a strikethrough/highlight diff via "Show changes" / "Edit plan". Approval hands off to Build. During Build you watch activity cards naming each step and each file, with subagent rows ("Explore: How does the current authentication flow work?") that can be expanded to see files inspected and tools used. You can queue further prompts above the input and pause/reorder/edit/repeat them (up to 50x), and Stop mid-run keeps completed work and bills only what ran. A floating preview toolbar (draggable, corner-snapping, Auto/Light/Dark, position remembered) gives four modes with single-key shortcuts: Select elements (S), Edit text inline (T — first 100 daily edits free), Draw annotation (D — rough shapes auto-cleaned), Add a comment (C — free). Version history is automatic with a Bookmarks tab, a "Published" badge on the live version, per-version diff view, and Revert — which explicitly does NOT roll back database data.

PUBLISH & DOMAINS. Publish sits top-right next to Share; a small dot appears when live is stale; the dialog holds the editable Website URL, a visibility row, and a basic security scan. Default URL is `[name].lovable.app`; Business/Enterprise get `{app}.{workspace}.lovable.app`. Crucially — and this contradicts the brief's assumption — Lovable is now a full domain REGISTRAR: it sells domains in-flow, auto-configures A/TXT, auto-enables WHOIS privacy, supports transfer-in with EPP codes and transfer-out, and for external domains uses Entri one-click DNS (fallback: A → 185.158.133.1 plus `_lovable` TXT). It also sends DKIM/SPF/DMARC-authenticated mail from your domain (50,000/mo included) — but provides no mailboxes.

MONEY. Free $0 (5 daily build credits capped at 30/mo, 20 Cloud + 4 AI credits, 5 lovable.app domains, read-only code, no custom domain), Pro $25/mo for 100 credits, Business $50/mo for the same 100 credits, Enterprise custom; annual = "2 months free". Top-ups are $0.30/credit on Pro and $0.60 on Business.

findings.title: Signup wall fires on prompt submit, not on page load — and the prompt survives it
findings.detail: The homepage composer is fully interactive to anonymous visitors. Submitting the first prompt is what triggers the auth wall; docs state the system "preserves the prompt through the signup process". Options are email, Google, GitHub, Apple. Post-signup the user lands in the dashboard in a personal workspace on the Free plan with the build already kicking off. Net: 1 type + 1 send + 1 OAuth click to first generation.

findings.title: Zero pre-generation configuration: no template picker, no style chooser, no wizard
findings.detail: Docs are explicit that "no templates or style pickers exist in this flow. Users describe their vision directly." Design templates DO exist but are gated behind the '+' menu (Design → Use a template) and restricted to Business/Enterprise. This keeps the anonymous funnel to exactly one decision.

findings.title: Free tier requires no credit card and is stated on the pricing card
findings.detail: The Free plan card literally carries the line "No credit card needed" directly beneath its "Get started" button. Free is perpetual, not a timed trial — contrast with Remixer's 30-day trial. Free includes "Workspace-private projects", "Unlimited collaborators", "5 lovable.app domains", "Cloud" and "Community support".

findings.title: The composer is one component reused as marketing hero, dashboard entry and editor input
findings.detail: The same ProseMirror-based composer (data-testid="chat-composer", editor id "chatinput") appears on the marketing homepage, on the dashboard ("Type a description of what you want to build and click send"), and as the editor chat input. Identical affordances everywhere: '+' menu, mode chip, mic. The marketing page is therefore a live demo of the product's primary control, not a screenshot of it.

findings.title: Animated typewriter placeholder that teaches prompt shape
findings.detail: The placeholder span is aria-hidden, styled `text-primary-pulse/50` with `transition-opacity duration-500 ease-out`, and types out rotating suggestions such as "Ask Lovable to create a landing page for my…". It teaches the verb-first prompt grammar while the user hesitates, rather than showing a static grey string.

findings.title: Three parallel 'design directions' generated before any code is written
findings.detail: For visually open-ended prompts Lovable produces three lightweight HTML/Tailwind previews the user compares side by side, with an input plus suggested prompts to refine a chosen direction — capped at "up to six refinements total" while preserving the overall design language. This is the single strongest anti-generic-output mechanism found.

findings.title: 'Design questions' branch: font pairs, mood-grouped swatches, wireframe layouts
findings.detail: When a project needs a stronger visual identity, Lovable instead walks a guided chooser: typography (font pairs grouped by aesthetic category), colour palette ("curated swatches grouped by mood"), and layout (wireframes — grids, splits, masonry). Answers compile into "a detailed design brief with named fonts, hex colors, layout approach." It deliberately SKIPS all of this for dashboards, admin tools, URL clones, and template/design-system projects.

findings.title: Activity cards name the step, the files and the tool — not a spinner
findings.detail: Build mode shows "each step of execution, including progress and which files are being modified", plus which tools are in use (search, web fetching, image generation). Expandable Details view. Errors surface as an activity card with a "Try to fix" button, and Lovable's fix attempts are free within fair-use — the error state is a one-click recovery affordance, not a dead end.

findings.title: Subagent rows expose parallel read-only investigation live in the chat
findings.detail: Subagents render as an activity card with individual rows showing "what the subagents are investigating and their current status"; expanding reveals files inspected, searches run, tools used and findings returned. Titles are human-readable, e.g. "Explore: How does the current authentication flow work?" They cannot write files. Shipped 27 May 2026.

findings.title: Named loading keyframes reveal a purpose-built waiting vocabulary
findings.detail: The stylesheet defines dedicated keyframes rather than a generic spinner: `heartbeat` (scale 1 → 1.07 → 1.02 → 1.02 → 1.06 → 1, a literal double-beat on the heart logo), `loader-sweep` (opacity+translate 0→50%→100%→50%→0), `shimmer-gradient` (background-position 200%→0), `gradient-sweep` (blur(1px)+position sweep), `status-dot-ping` (scale 1→2.667, opacity 1→0), and `message-highlight`. Waiting is branded, not borrowed.

findings.title: Idle preview degrades to a friendly pause state instead of erroring
findings.detail: When the preview environment goes inactive it displays "Still building?" with a "Keep building" button that resumes the environment. Docs stress this does not affect the published app or project data — the scary-sounding pause is explicitly de-risked in copy.

findings.title: Exact top-bar inventory, left to right
findings.detail: Left: Lovable logo (opens dashboard sidebar for workspace/project switching) → project-name menu (workspace, plan, credit usage, then "Get free credits", "Settings", "Project connectors", "Remix this project", "Design system", "Rename project", "Star project", "Move to folder", "Details", "Appearance", "Help") → History toggle → Close sidebar toggle. Right (with Preview active): preview-toolbar button, Comments, collaborator avatars, Share, Publish.

findings.title: Four-tab project toolbar: Preview / Files / Code / More
findings.detail: Rather than a right icon rail (Remixer's model), Lovable uses a horizontal tab switcher. 'Files' holds generated documents and uploaded deliverables; 'More' nests Analytics, Cloud (→ AI, Emails, Supabase), Agent integrations, Payments, Connectors, Security, SEO & AI search, Sensitive data. Toolbar navigation was explicitly 'polished' with keyboard navigation on 26 May 2026.

findings.title: Keyboard shortcut set is IDE-grade, not toy-grade
findings.detail: Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette (search projects and settings); Cmd/Ctrl+B collapse chat panel to full-window preview (same shortcut collapses the dashboard sidebar — consistent); Option/Alt+V dictate; Option/Alt+P toggle Build↔Plan; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F project-wide code search; Cmd/Ctrl+F in-file; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+L reference exact code lines; single-key S/T/D/C for preview-toolbar modes. Desktop app adds Cmd+1–9 tab switching, Cmd+T new tab, Cmd+Shift+O browser preview.

findings.title: Panel proportions are not documented and could not be verified
findings.detail: No public doc or screenshot caption states the chat panel's pixel width or the split ratio, and the editor is behind auth so it could not be measured directly. Only the qualitative arrangement (chat left, preview right, collapsible via Cmd+B) is confirmed. Treat any specific px figure as unverified.

findings.title: Two named modes with asymmetric pricing as the core mental model
findings.detail: Build (default): "Lovable makes direct project changes", usage-based cost. Plan: "Lovable discusses and plans without modifying code", flat 1 credit/message. Toggled by a chip next to the send button or Option+P. The pricing asymmetry is the UX: thinking is cheap and predictable, doing is metered.

findings.title: Plan mode renders an editable document with highlight-to-revise and a real diff
findings.detail: Plans open in a dedicated full-screen "Plan view" containing overview, key decisions, components, data models, APIs, sequencing and optional diagrams. Users edit markdown directly, or select any passage to get a "Describe the change..." box (shipped 3 Aug 2026). Revisions render as a diff where "removed wording is struck through and new wording is highlighted", toggled via "Show changes" / "Edit plan". Approved plans are archived to `.lovable/plan/` with dated filenames.

findings.title: Message queue is a first-class, manipulable object above the input
findings.detail: Additional prompts sent while Lovable works enter "a visible queue above the chat input" where the user can pause/resume the whole queue, reorder, edit, copy, remove, and repeat a prompt up to 50 times. This converts the usual 'wait for the AI' dead time into productive batching.

findings.title: Per-message cost, duration and shareable permalink under a three-dot menu
findings.detail: Each completed response exposes "Undo latest edit", "Revert to this version", "Copy", "Rate" (helpful/not helpful), and a More menu showing message cost, duration and a shareable message link. Surfacing per-message credit cost at the point of consumption is the main mitigation against credit anxiety.

findings.title: '@' reference picker and '/' skills menu give the chat IDE-like precision
findings.detail: The '+' Chat actions menu opens attachments, references and project tools. '@' references code, files, connectors and other projects; clicking a line number inserts an exact line reference (`file.tsx:42`, shipped 10 Jun 2026). '/' opens the slash menu of Skills — workspace-level reusable playbooks that attach "as a tag at the start of your message", plus read-only "Skills Built by Lovable" for accessibility, SEO and design reviews.

findings.title: Attachment limits are a visible plan lever
findings.detail: Images, PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and audio via the '+' menu, drag-and-drop or paste. Size caps: 20 MB Free, 256 MB paid, 1 GB Enterprise; max 10 files per message and 15 MB total images. File thumbnails render as a gallery in chat (14 Jul 2026).

findings.title: Automatic versioning with a Bookmarks tab and a 'Published' badge on the live version
findings.detail: Every change creates a version with no manual save. The History panel (top-bar toggle, or '+' menu → History) has two tabs: History and Bookmarks. Per version: More actions (full-screen preview, code diff, jump to chat message), Revert, Bookmark toggle. The currently live version carries a "Published" badge — so version history doubles as the deploy ledger.

findings.title: Revert is honest about its limits, including a disabled-state tooltip
findings.detail: Reverting restores code and redeploys edge functions but explicitly "does not restore or roll back your database data." Revert is disabled when already viewing that version, when the project came from a Cloud remix, or when the version is too old — with the tooltip "Cannot revert this far back in history". Chat history and later edits survive a revert so changes can be reapplied.

findings.title: Draggable four-mode preview toolbar with single-key shortcuts
findings.detail: Modes: Select elements (S — click one or many, Cmd/Ctrl to multi-select, then describe the change; costs credits), Edit text inline (T — "the fastest way to fix a typo, change a headline, or update a label"), Draw annotation (D), Add a comment (C). The toolbar drags to any corner or the default bottom-centre, minimises to a tab, or hides; position and state persist across sessions; theme is Auto (adapts to background) / Light / Dark. Shipped 10 Jun 2026.

findings.title: First 100 inline text edits per user per day are FREE — credits never gate typo fixes
findings.detail: Inline text editing (T mode) is free for the first 100 edits per user per day; only beyond that does it consume credits. This surgically removes the most infuriating possible credit charge (fixing a typo) while keeping the metered model intact. Comments are entirely free to pin; only replying-to-Lovable or sending a thread for action costs credits.

findings.title: Freehand annotation with automatic shape cleanup
findings.detail: Draw mode (D) accepts freehand sketches and recognises lines, arrows, rectangles, circles and ovals — the system "cleans them up automatically, so a quickly drawn circle becomes a clean one." Sketches attach to a message describing the change. This is a designer-native input channel no competitor in the brief offers.

findings.title: Code tab is a real editor, but read-only on Free — a deliberate paywall placement
findings.detail: Code view has a file tree with Expand all / Collapse all (13 Jul 2026), a "Search code" box, right-click context menus, tabbed files, and a file toolbar with Preview markdown, Copy file content, Download, Format, Save, Discard. "Code editing is available on paid plans. On the Free plan the editor is read-only." Per-file Download is on all plans; "Download codebase" (.zip) is paid-only. Git sync to GitHub/GitLab is on ALL plans including Free.

findings.title: Device toggle, page selector with custom paths, and Shift-click hard restart
findings.detail: Preview bar carries a device toggle for "Desktop view", "Tablet view", "Mobile view"; a page selector showing current location with a find field to jump between pages or type an arbitrary path; Refresh, where holding Shift performs a full environment restart ("resolving most issues"); and Open in new tab for full-screen or side-by-side testing. A 6 Aug 2026 setting lets users turn OFF live preview and show the last completed build instead.

findings.title: Publish button placement, the stale-build dot, and the dialog contents
findings.detail: Publish sits top-right beside Share and "collapses to an icon without a label" on narrow windows. "When your published project has changes that are newer than the live version, a small dot appears on the Publish button." The dialog contains: editable Website URL field (first publish only), a visibility row, basic security scan results, and deployment status. Republishing is a second click on "Publish changes". Unpublish lives in Project settings or the dialog's ⋯ menu.

findings.title: Publishing is free on every plan and does not consume credits
findings.detail: "Publishing itself is free. Only backend activity — such as database operations and AI features — consumes Run credits. A live site with no backend activity incurs no credit charges." Plans do not cap visitors, requests or bandwidth. This is a direct strategic contrast with Remixer, where publishing changes burns credits.

findings.title: You can ship by talking: 'Publish my app' / 'Ship it'
findings.detail: Publishing from chat shipped 9 Jun 2026. The agent deploys while respecting workspace settings and runs security checks with an approval step. Docs give the literal example phrasings "Publish my app" and "Ship it".

findings.title: Snapshot deploy model, stated plainly to set expectations
findings.detail: "Publishing creates a snapshot of your project. Changes made afterward don't affect the live site until you republish." Combined with the Publish dot and the "Published" badge in version history, users get three consistent signals for the same state — a rare level of coherence on staging-vs-live.

findings.title: MAJOR CORRECTION TO BRIEF ASSUMPTION: Lovable is now a full domain registrar
findings.detail: The brief assumes Lovable "structurally cannot" sell/connect domains in-flow. That is no longer true. Lovable sells domains in-app (April 2026), registers domains without a project attached (4 Jun 2026), supports transfer-IN with EPP codes carrying over A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/TXT/CAA/NS records (8 Jun 2026), transfer-OUT with EPP (4 Jun 2026), and a WHOIS privacy toggle (5 Jun 2026). Docs state plainly: "Lovable becomes the registrar for that domain", managing renewals, registration details and DNS. Domains belong to the workspace, not the project. Purchases require workspace admin/owner.

findings.title: Entri one-click DNS for external domains — the exact capability DreamHost lacks
findings.detail: Connecting an existing domain offers automatic setup via Entri: Lovable auto-detects the DNS provider, the user signs in and authorises Entri to write the records. Manual fallback: A record → 185.158.133.1, plus a TXT at host `_lovable` with value beginning `lovable_verify=`. Prerequisite: no AAAA records present. Docs even note the host name "may need to be: @, left blank, or set to your domain name". Since DreamHost does not support Domain Connect, Lovable is currently AHEAD on external-domain UX.

findings.title: A named state machine for domain status with a recovery verb for every failure
findings.detail: Statuses: Pending, Live, Ready (configured but project unpublished), Removed. Failure states each have their own action: Verifying → "Click Check status to check the latest status"; Unable to verify → "DNS verification did not complete within one hour"; Stalled → "Click Retry"; Offline → "Click Recover. Review displayed DNS records"; Removed → "Click Reconnect". Branded workspace URLs progress "Provisioning DNS" → "Issuing SSL certificate" → "Active". Every dead end has a button.

findings.title: SSL is automatic with a stated 72-hour escalation SLA, and vendor-specific rescue copy
findings.detail: Certificates are generated and installed automatically; "if not issued after 72 hours, users should contact support." TLS 1.2 minimum, not user-modifiable. Docs include Cloudflare-specific triage: for errors 1001/1003, set records to DNS only (grey cloud) rather than Proxied (orange cloud). Only one domain can be primary; others 302-redirect (notably temporary, not 301).

findings.title: Lovable sends authenticated mail from your domain — but provides NO mailboxes
findings.detail: Cloud tab → Emails, with "Auth emails" and "App emails" tabs. Lovable runs its own delivery infrastructure (not SendGrid/Resend) and auto-manages SPF, DKIM and DMARC; setup needs NS records for zone delegation plus a TXT verification record. 50,000 transactional emails/month per workspace included, overages at 4 credits per 1,000. Requires a paid plan and Cloud enabled. Docs are explicit: Lovable does not provide mailboxes. DreamHost's real remaining email advantage is inbound mailboxes, not outbound sending.

findings.title: Exact 2026 plan cards, transcribed from the live pricing page
findings.detail: Free $0/month — "Discover what Lovable can do for you"; Free grants, Workspace-private projects, Unlimited collaborators, 5 lovable.app domains, Cloud, Community support. Pro $25/month, 100 monthly credits — adds Credit rollovers, On-demand credit top-ups, Unlimited lovable.app domains, Custom domains, User roles & permissions, Per-member credit limits, Remove the Lovable badge, Email support. Business $50/month, 100 monthly credits — adds Team workspace, Role-based access, Internal publish, Personal projects, SSO, Security center, Design templates, Priority support. Enterprise: "Platform fee", "Volume based pricing", Book a demo. Billing toggle: Monthly / Yearly with a "2 months free" badge.

findings.title: Business costs 2x Pro for the SAME 100 credits — governance is the product, not capacity
findings.detail: Both Pro and Business list "100 monthly credits" at $25 and $50 respectively; the pricing FAQ even carries the question "Why is the Business plan more expensive?". Docs confirm the ladder scales identically in shape: Pro runs 100→10,000 credits ($25→$2,250/mo), Business runs the same 100→10,000 at roughly double ($50→$4,300/mo). Credits are priced per credit, not per seat — "Workspaces support unlimited members on all plans, and plans are priced by the credits they include, not by seats."

findings.title: Unified credit pool spanning build, Cloud and app-AI, with published cost examples
findings.detail: Since 18 Jun 2026 one balance funds three categories: Build (agent messages), Cloud (database size, storage, bandwidth, compute, realtime), and AI Gateway (model calls made BY the published app). Published per-message examples: simple update 0.50, component removal 0.90, authentication setup 1.20, landing page with images 1.70–2.00. Plan mode is a flat 1.00. Users can literally ask Lovable in chat how credits were spent.

findings.title: Daily free grants make the free tier a genuine habit loop
findings.detail: All Free, Pro and Business plans get 5 daily build credits refreshing at 00:00 UTC (Free capped at 30/calendar month; Pro/Business uncapped), plus a monthly 20 Cloud credits and 4 AI credits. Unused daily grants do not roll over. Spend order is deterministic and documented: "Lovable always uses usage-specific grants before general credits", then general credits closest to expiry first.

findings.title: Paywall interrupts twice: a soft nudge above the input, then a blocking dialog at zero
findings.detail: Low-credit UX is staged — a nudge appears above the chat input when running low; a blocking dialog appears at zero and stops building; deployed-app AI features fail and "built-in backend services will pause" (data stays safe but inaccessible) while published static pages keep serving. Email alerts fire to owners/admins for failed auto top-ups, and an in-app banner shows when a monthly spend limit is hit. Top-ups: Pro $0.30/credit ($15 for 50), Business $0.60/credit ($30 for 50); auto top-up triggers at 25/50/100 credits, adding 50–1,000 per top-up with a 100–25,000 or unlimited monthly ceiling.

findings.title: Credit expiry rules are the most-complained-about part of the model
findings.detail: Monthly plan credits roll over but expire 2 months after issuance; annual-plan credits expire 1 month after the period ends; top-ups expire 12 months from purchase; Cloud/AI grants expire at cycle end; daily build credits expire same-day. The pricing FAQ carries "Do credits expire?", "What happens to my credits if my subscription ends?" and "Are credits refundable?" — three questions that exist because the answers are unpopular.

findings.title: The whole system is OKLCH semantic tokens — measured live from lovable.dev
findings.detail: Not hex, not HSL. Light: --bg-depth oklch(95.49% 0 107), --bg-base oklch(96.99% 0 107), --bg-primary oklch(98.51% 0 107), --bg-secondary/tertiary/quaternary oklch(99.99% 0 107). Foreground ramp is a clean 10/30/50/69% lightness ladder: --fg-primary oklch(10% 0 0), --fg-secondary oklch(30% .001 107), --fg-tertiary oklch(50% .001 107), --fg-quaternary oklch(69% .001 107). Semantic hues: accent oklch(52.43% .2396 264.41) [blue], destructive .2203 26.56 [red], special .2523 294.88 [violet], positive .1689 138.23 [green], attention .1819 40.04 [orange], highlight .2244 359.16 [pink]. Every semantic also ships -translucent (/.16) and -glow (hover /.08, pressed /.16) variants.

findings.title: Dark mode changes ONLY the neutral ramp — the six semantic hues are byte-identical
findings.detail: `.dark` redefines --bg-depth 20.42%, --bg-base 23%, --bg-primary 24.74%, --bg-secondary 27.2%, --bg-tertiary 30%, --bg-quaternary 32.8% (a ~2.5% lightness step per elevation level), and --fg-primary oklch(100% 0 0). But --bg-accent stays oklch(52.43% .2396 264.41) in BOTH themes; only translucency alpha shifts .16 → .2. This is why the product reads as one brand across themes. Note the asymmetry: light mode collapses secondary/tertiary/quaternary to a single 99.99% ceiling (3 usable elevation steps) while dark keeps 6 distinct ones — dark is the design-led theme.

findings.title: Proprietary variable typeface 'Camera Plain Variable', self-hosted, with Roboto Mono for code
findings.detail: @font-face: "Camera Plain Variable" 100–900 woff2 (plus a 400 italic cut), self-hosted at /assets/CameraPlainVariable-*.woff2, licensed to "Lovable Labs Incorporated". Code/mono is Roboto Mono Variable 100–700 with per-subset files (latin, latin-ext, cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, greek, vietnamese). A bespoke variable UI typeface is the single biggest reason the interface reads as expensive — nothing on the page is Inter.

findings.title: Display type: exactly 1.1 line-height and exactly -0.04em tracking at every size
findings.detail: Measured at 1280px: hero 48px/52.8px/-1.92px, section 36px/39.6px/-1.44px, sub-section 28px/30.8px/-1.12px, all weight 600. Every one is line-height = 1.100× and letter-spacing = -0.0400em. Body is 16px/24px (1.5) weight 400; secondary body 14px/24px. So the system has exactly two rhythms — a tight 1.1 display rhythm and a loose 1.5 (24px baseline) prose rhythm — and no drift between them.

findings.title: Variable-font weight 480 used for prices — intermediate weights the system actually exploits
findings.detail: The $25 price on the pricing page computes to font-weight 480, not 500. Using a non-standard axis value is only possible because Camera Plain is variable, and it is the kind of sub-perceptual tuning that separates a bespoke system from a Tailwind default. Body copy is 400, headings 600, price 480.

findings.title: Radius scale is 6/8/10/12/16/24/28/32 + full-round, with --radius base 0.5rem
findings.detail: Measured distribution across the DOM: 8px (28 uses) and 10px (28) dominate for controls, 9999px/full-round (26) for pills and icon buttons, 16px (17) for cards, 12px (10), 6px (8) for small chips, 24/28/32px for large surfaces. The hero composer is 28px; the pricing card is 16px; buttons are 8px. Root exposes --radius: .5rem.

findings.title: A physically-modelled shadow system: 6-step surface ramp plus per-semantic inset button shadows
findings.detail: --shadow-surface-xxs → xl compose a hairline ring plus geometrically doubling offsets: 1px/1px, 3px/3px −1.5px, 6px/6px −3px, 12px/12px −6px, 24px/24px −12px, every layer at #0000000a (4% black). Buttons get their own recipe: `inset 0 1px 0 0 #fff, inset 0 -1px 0 0 #fffc` on neutral (a top highlight and bottom shade simulating a lit bevel), with per-semantic ring colours — accent #11318c, destructive #8d0e13, special #53388c, positive #1d4e04. The pricing CTA measured a 5-layer stacked shadow. This layered micro-lighting is the main reason controls look injection-moulded rather than flat.

findings.title: Hero is a live 2400×2420 canvas mesh gradient, not a CSS gradient or an image
findings.detail: A single <canvas class="absolute inset-0 h-full w-full object-contain"> at 2400×2420 renders the animated blue→lavender→magenta→red mesh behind the hero. Sibling CSS gradients define the brand ramps: blue #4F88FF → #5185FF → #5885FF → #6289FF → #7491FF → #91A0FF → #B0ACFE → #CEAFFB, and the warm ramp #FF8F1B → #FE771D → #FC541F → #FB3D26 → #FA2733 → #FA1F41 → #FC1A58. Keyframes `background-enter`, `background-enter-skip` and `background-ambient` control its entry and idle drift.

findings.title: Marketing hero copy is deliberately dark-on-light with the gradient BELOW the fold line
findings.detail: The hero sits on --bg-base off-white oklch(96.99%) fading into the mesh gradient in the lower two-thirds, so "Build something Lovable" (rgb(28,28,28)) and the subhead sit on near-white while the composer floats at the gradient's edge as a translucent frosted card. The gradient never competes with type for contrast — a discipline most AI-builder landing pages break.

findings.title: A small, opinionated easing palette — four curves, durations 100–500ms
findings.detail: Measured in use: cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) at 150ms (opacity) and 200/300ms (transform/translate/scale/rotate) — Material standard; cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1) at 100/300/500ms — decelerate, used for opacity and for background-color/border-color/box-shadow; cubic-bezier(0.33,1,0.68,1) at 350ms — easeOutCubic on 'all'; cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) at 250ms — easeOutExpo on colour/border/outline/text-decoration; cubic-bezier(0.215,0.61,0.355,1) at 225–300ms for SVG stroke-dashoffset. Nothing bounces or overshoots; every curve decelerates into rest.

findings.title: Scroll reveal is a single restrained gesture: translateY(12px) + opacity 0→1
findings.detail: Sections below the fold render at opacity 0 with transform matrix(1,0,0,1,0,12) — a 12px rise, not 40px, not a scale, not a blur. Programmatic instant scrolling to y=1500 produced a blank viewport, confirming reveals are IntersectionObserver-gated rather than scroll-linked. Stat counters ('Discord members', 'Projects built with Lovable') animate from 0 on entry.

findings.title: Component-level named keyframes reveal a deep interaction library
findings.detail: Beyond loaders: `view-switcher-label-enter/exit/option-enter/label-swap-enter/option-swap-enter` (a five-keyframe choreography just for the Preview/Files/Code/More switcher), `mention-pill-shift` (the @-mention pill), `checkbox-draw-check` and `checkbox-draw-minus` (checkmarks are DRAWN via stroke-dashoffset, not faded in), `radio-dot-enter`, `star-pop` and `star-spray` (starring a project emits particles), `message-highlight`, `shake`, `lol-foil`, `shine`, `sonner-fade-in/out/spin` (toasts), `swipe-out-left/right/up/down` (mobile), `ProseMirror-cursor-blink`. Roughly 39 distinct keyframes ship on the marketing bundle alone.

findings.title: Glow tokens encode hover and pressed as separate alpha steps for every semantic
findings.detail: --glow-{neutral|accent|destructive|special|positive|attention|highlight}-{hover|pressed} are defined as the semantic hue at 8% and 16% alpha respectively (neutral uses black at 4%/8%). Because hover/pressed are tokens rather than ad-hoc CSS, every interactive surface in the product responds with exactly the same weight — this consistency is a large part of the 'expensive' feel.

findings.title: Recovery is free by policy, and the policy is stated in the UI's docs
findings.detail: "Try to fix" appears on error activity cards and Lovable's fix attempts are free within fair use. Security findings likewise: "Fixing security issues is free within our fair use policy", with "Try to fix all" for batch remediation. Basic and Deep security scans both cost zero credits. Design-system verification turns are "billed at zero credits". Lovable systematically refuses to charge for cleaning up its own mess — the single most effective antidote to credit resentment.

findings.title: Findings use a four-level icon language, not just red/green
findings.detail: SEO and security findings render as: green check = passing, blue lightbulb = low impact, amber warning triangle = medium impact, red X = high impact (blocks indexing). Security severities are labelled with plain-language definitions — Error: "Critical problems that need your attention right away"; Warning: "Issues you should review and fix if necessary"; Info: "Suggestions to consider implementing". Groupings: "Failing", "Passing", "Fixed", "Ignored issues", with "Restore" to un-ignore.

findings.title: Scan-state microcopy is a three-word status vocabulary reused everywhere
findings.detail: "Up to date" / "Out of date" / "Scanning your project…" appears identically in the Security view and the SEO & AI search tab, with buttons "Scan project" (first run) and "Scan again" (subsequent). Reusing one status vocabulary across unrelated subsystems is why the product feels like one thing rather than a bundle of features.

findings.title: Marketing section headers use a consistent two-word comma construction
findings.detail: "Hosting, handled" / "Your app stack, connected" / "Payments, processed" / "Safe and secure, as standard" / "Works wherever, whenever". Paired with "Depend on Lovable, from end to end", "The proof is in production", "Millions count on Lovable" and "One platform. Endless possibilities." The rhythm is deliberate: noun, comma, past-participle. Highly copyable pattern.

findings.title: Native iOS and Android apps, free on all plans, with swipe between chat and preview
findings.detail: iOS 15+ (iPhone/iPad), Android 9+ (phone/tablet), free in both stores. Users "start something new, continue an existing project, prompt with voice or images, and get notified when a build is ready to review". Mobile-optimised layout with swipe gestures between chat and preview panels, edge-swipe back, and native system sign-in dialogs rather than browser redirects. Account, projects and credits sync across devices.

findings.title: What is explicitly cut on mobile — and an iOS billing tax
findings.detail: Desktop-only: OAuth integration setup, account creation, detailed code review, preview-toolbar interactions, some billing functions, inline comments and the full mention picker. No offline mode. Billing splits by platform: iOS purchases go through Apple IAP, Android users must buy via web browser on Stripe — both sync status back. A separate Electron-style Desktop app (macOS + Windows, all plans incl. Free) adds LOCAL MCP servers (Figma Desktop, Paper, custom) and Cmd+1–9 project tabs.

findings.title: Three link types with different, explicitly-stated expiry windows
findings.detail: Invite links expire after 5 days, only one active at a time, and changing the access level regenerates the URL invalidating the old one. Preview links are public view-only, valid 7 days, show "the app exactly as it runs; they do not see the Lovable editor, chat, or source code." Direct email invites put the project in the recipient's "Shared with me" section. Roles: Admin (Business/Enterprise), Editor (default), Viewer (paid only).

findings.title: Guests can comment on a preview with no account — and the owner gets an inbox ping
findings.detail: Guest comments are ON by default; visitors comment on previews without logging in and "the project owner receives an inbox notification in Lovable when a guest comments" (shipped 26 Jun 2026). Collaborator avatars show live presence in the editor top bar and collapse behind a single avatar when crowded (2 Jun 2026). Published-app visibility is a SEPARATE axis from project access: "Publishing only makes the app available at the published URL. It does not grant anyone access to your project in the editor or your project code."

findings.title: 194 community templates, each with a distinctive capability one-liner instead of a category
findings.detail: lovable.dev/templates: "Website and app templates / Built with AI", "Production-ready apps from the Lovable community", "194 results" with a Filters control. Descriptors are specific mechanisms, never genres: "Drag-and-drop images with text notes", "Beeswarm chart with explainable scores", "Butterfly funnel with cohort trends", "Pickup time slots with catering form", "Live type tester with filter sidebar", "Command palette with versioned changelog", "Timezone-aware slots, one shared link", "Live amortization with PMI drop-off". This copy pattern alone makes the gallery feel curated rather than scraped.

findings.title: Remix is off by default and the dialog is explicit about what does NOT copy
findings.detail: "Public remixing" is a Project settings → Sharing toggle, disabled by default and unavailable in Enterprise workspaces. Remix dialog fields: Project name, Target workspace, Target folder, "Include project history", "Include custom knowledge", Region. Copied: code, database SCHEMA only, optionally chat history and knowledge. NOT copied: database records, version history, secrets/API credentials, custom domains, collaborators, Git sync and external integrations. Reachable from the project-name menu ("Remix this project"), Project settings → Project actions, and the dashboard card menu.

findings.title: The /community route is now a Discord-and-events page, not a project gallery
findings.detail: lovable.dev/community reads "Welcome to the Lovable community", "Build the future with thousands of creators, founders, and dreamers", claims 160K+ Discord members, and offers "Browse events", "Join Lovable on Discord", "Become a community leader", Ambassador and Campus Leader cohort programs, and SheBuilds buildathons. The showcase function has migrated to /templates. Community is being run as a distribution channel, not a gallery.

findings.title: Cloud is Supabase-derived but presented as 11 native tabs — and enabled implicitly
findings.detail: Lovable Cloud ("based on Supabase's open-source foundation") activates automatically "when a feature you ask for requires backend functionality", governed by a permission setting: Always allow (default) / Ask each time / Never allow. Cloud tab contains AI, Emails, Database, Users, Storage, Secrets, Jobs, Edge functions, SQL editor, Logs, Usage. Region (Americas / Europe / Asia Pacific) is chosen once and "cannot be changed"; "Migration from Supabase to Cloud is not supported."

findings.title: ~90 named connectors across three architecturally distinct types
findings.detail: Docs split them into app connectors (your app calls the service), chat connectors (the agent calls the service), and app USER connectors (each of your app's end-users authorises their own third-party account — launched 13 Jul 2026, enabling multi-tenant apps). Coverage spans Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, ClickHouse, Redshift, Microsoft Fabric, dbt Semantic Layer, Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe, Shopify, WooCommerce, Xero, QuickBooks, Notion, Linear, Slack, Twilio, Mapbox, PostHog, Semrush, Wiz, Aikido, plus custom MCP servers on all plans. Connector action approvals pause before write operations (8 Jul 2026).

findings.title: Zero-setup privacy-preserving analytics built into the editor
findings.detail: More → Analytics. Metrics: Visitors, Page views, Views per visit, Visit duration, Bounce rate, plus a live counter of active users in the past 5 minutes. Breakdowns by Source, Page, Device, Country (from browser time zone). Periods: today, yesterday, 24h, 7d (default), 14d, 30d, 90d, current month. "Nothing to set up" — it works on publish. Explicitly aggregate-only: no individual visitor profiles, no cross-visit tracking. A 'Visitor analytics' toggle sits in Project settings → Publishing.

findings.title: Project monitoring (Beta, Pro+) turns post-launch into a scheduled agent job
findings.detail: Settings → Project settings → General → Project monitoring. Controls: "Enable project monitoring" toggle, "Configure", "Schedule" (daily/weekly, timezone-aware), "Runs" dropdown ("Every time" / "If edited since last check"), "Minimum edits made". Findings surface via a "View issues" button in the editor above the chat, with "Try to fix", "Skip", "Ignore" per issue and "View history" showing past checks with dates, credits used and issues found. It detects but never auto-fixes.

findings.title: Security is merchandised as a user-facing surface, not a compliance footnote
findings.detail: More → Security. Basic scan (automatic, config + dependency check, auto-fixes RLS and DB-access findings) and Deep scan (on-demand agentic code review) — both free of credits. Aikido AI penetration testing on all plans (22 Jun 2026); Wiz vulnerability scanning with selectable CI/CD policies. Auto-revoke of leaked API keys triggered by GitHub notifications (25 Jul 2026). Since 7 Aug 2026 every published app can expose an auto-generated Trust Center at /.well-known/trust.html. SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, GDPR; 2FA, SSO, SCIM.

findings.title: Server-side rendering by default since 13 May 2026, plus a Cerebras inference partnership
findings.detail: "Apps created after May 13, 2026 use server-side rendering for all visitors"; older apps pre-render for verified search engines and AI crawlers. Projects can be upgraded to TanStack Start. Global CDN delivery is automatic and independent of the Cloud backend region. On 5 Aug 2026 Lovable announced a Cerebras partnership "for reduced response times", and on 11 Aug 2026 published "The model picker is a dead end" — an explicit strategy of hiding model choice from users (contrast with competitors who expose model dropdowns).

findings.title: Marketing-site craft wart: the visual hero is not the h1
findings.detail: querySelector('h1') on lovable.dev returns "AI App Builder" at 14px/400 in rgb(97,97,97), while the visually dominant "Build something Lovable" computes at 48px/600 and is not an h1. The page also embeds a simulated product mock ("Bug tracking for teams that ship fast", "Purpose-built for engineering teams. Triage, track, and resolve issues without slowing down.", "Get started for free") that renders a literal "h1" tag badge — an animated demo of click-to-select visual editing showing the selected element's tag name. Semantically muddled, but the tag-badge idea is worth stealing for Remixer's visual editor.

findings.title: Knowledge and Skills split persistent context from on-demand context
findings.detail: Knowledge = always-on instructions, 10,000 characters each at workspace level (owners/admins only, one per workspace) and project level (any editor); project knowledge wins on conflict. Skills = on-demand playbooks invoked automatically by description match or manually via '/'. This two-tier model is cleaner than a single 'custom instructions' box and directly addresses AI-slop drift across a team.

findings.title: Design systems (Enterprise) are versioned, released projects with an update prompt
findings.detail: A design system is itself a Lovable project. Created via '+' → Design → "Use a design system" → "Create design system"; either a local component library or an npm wrapper reading the package's published type definitions. "Release version" generates .lovable/design-system.json ("canonical schema (tokens, components, constraints)") plus a hand-authored system.md. Attaching copies components to src/design-system/<slug>/ and rules to .lovable/rules/libraries/<slug>/. Connected projects see an "Update available" prompt on each new release. One design system per project; React only.

standout_ux.name: One composer, three contexts
standout_ux.what_it_is: The identical ProseMirror composer component — '+' actions menu, contenteditable, Build/Plan mode chip, mic — is the marketing hero, the dashboard 'new project' box, and the in-editor chat input. Same data-testid, same affordances, same shortcuts.
standout_ux.why_it_works: The marketing site is not advertising the product, it IS the product's primary control. Muscle memory formed before signup transfers intact into the editor, so the first in-app moment feels already-learned. Remixer's landing prompt box and builder chat panel should be literally the same component.

standout_ux.name: Typewriter placeholder that teaches prompt grammar
standout_ux.what_it_is: An aria-hidden span cross-fading at 500ms ease-out through rotating prompts like 'Ask Lovable to create a landing page for my…', sitting under the real contenteditable.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It solves blank-page paralysis without a modal, a tooltip or an onboarding tour, and it silently trains verb-first prompt shape. Costs nothing, converts hesitation into typing.

standout_ux.name: Three design directions before any code
standout_ux.what_it_is: For visually open-ended prompts, Lovable renders three parallel HTML/Tailwind previews to compare side by side, with up to six refinement turns, before committing to a build.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It converts the highest-variance moment in AI building — 'will it look generic?' — into a choice the user owns. It also front-loads taste before expensive generation, and it deliberately switches OFF for dashboards and admin tools where the user wants speed, not art direction.

standout_ux.name: Free-by-policy recovery
standout_ux.what_it_is: 'Try to fix' on error cards, 'Try to fix all' on security findings, both Basic and Deep security scans, and design-system verification turns are all billed at zero credits. The first 100 inline text edits per user per day are also free.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Credit burn is the #1 documented complaint about metered AI builders. Lovable never charges you to fix its own mistake or to correct a typo, which removes the specific charges that generate rage while keeping the meter running on real work. Remixer, which bills credits even for publishing, is exposed here.

standout_ux.name: Highlight-to-revise plans with a strikethrough diff
standout_ux.what_it_is: Plan mode renders a full-screen structured document; selecting any passage opens a 'Describe the change...' box; revisions render as struck-through old wording and highlighted new wording, toggled with 'Show changes' / 'Edit plan'.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It borrows the review affordance every knowledge worker already knows from Docs/Word and applies it to AI intent. The user negotiates the spec at 1 credit/message instead of discovering the misunderstanding after an expensive build.

standout_ux.name: The manipulable message queue
standout_ux.what_it_is: Prompts sent while the agent works stack in a visible queue above the input, where they can be paused, reordered, edited, copied, removed, or repeated up to 50 times.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It turns the multi-minute agent wait — normally dead, anxious time — into a planning surface, and it removes the 'did my message get lost?' failure mode entirely.

standout_ux.name: Draggable preview toolbar with four single-key modes
standout_ux.what_it_is: S = Select elements (multi-select with Cmd), T = Edit text inline, D = Draw annotation with auto-cleaned shapes, C = Add a comment. Drags to any corner, minimises to a tab, remembers position, and themes Auto/Light/Dark against the underlying page.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It puts editing ON the artifact rather than in a side panel, uses one keystroke per mode like a design tool, and the Auto theme means the toolbar never fights the user's own design. The auto-cleaned freehand shapes ('a quickly drawn circle becomes a clean one') is a delight beat competitors don't have.

standout_ux.name: Three consistent signals for one deploy state
standout_ux.what_it_is: A dot on the Publish button when live is stale, a 'Published' badge on the live version in History, and the plainly-stated snapshot model ('Changes made afterward don't affect the live site until you republish').
standout_ux.why_it_works: Staging-vs-live confusion is the most common support cost in site builders. Lovable expresses the same fact three times in three places without contradiction, so users never have to guess what visitors are seeing.

standout_ux.name: A recovery verb for every domain failure state
standout_ux.what_it_is: Verifying → 'Check status'; Unable to verify → 'DNS verification did not complete within one hour'; Stalled → 'Retry'; Offline → 'Recover'; Removed → 'Reconnect'. Plus Cloudflare-specific guidance to switch from Proxied to DNS-only.
standout_ux.why_it_works: DNS is where AI builders lose users. Lovable never leaves a terminal red state without a button and a next action, and it names the specific third-party misconfiguration that causes the error. This is exactly the pattern Remixer needs given it has no Domain Connect.

standout_ux.name: Hue-constant dual theming in OKLCH
standout_ux.what_it_is: Light and dark redefine only the neutral ramp (six ~2.5%-lightness elevation steps in dark) while all six semantic hues — accent, destructive, special, positive, attention, highlight — keep byte-identical OKLCH values across themes; only translucency alpha shifts .16 → .2.
standout_ux.why_it_works: OKLCH keeps perceptual lightness honest across hues, so a single alpha and lightness system works everywhere. The result is that the product is recognisably the same brand in both themes with zero per-theme colour hand-tuning — the structural reason the UI reads as expensive rather than themed.

weaknesses.issue: Unpredictable credit burn is the single most-cited complaint across every review platform
weaknesses.evidence: G2 reviewer: "The biggest drawback I've run into is the credit-based usage model." Saiprasad A. on G2: "Credits can disappear pretty quickly, especially when I'm iterating on designs." Reviewers repeatedly describe debugging loops where the AI fixes one thing, breaks another, and charges for each attempt. Build-mode pricing is explicitly variable ('requests can cost less than 1 credit or several credits depending on complexity'), so the user cannot forecast cost before sending.

weaknesses.issue: Credits expire and are forfeited when a subscription ends, which users describe as punitive
weaknesses.evidence: Trustpilot review: "The subscription is basically extortion. If you do not use your tokens and end the subscription, they are gone." Docs confirm monthly plan credits expire 2 months after issuance, annual credits 1 month after the period ends, and daily grants same-day with no rollover. The pricing FAQ carries three separate defensive questions: 'Do credits expire?', 'What happens to my credits if my subscription ends?', 'Are credits refundable?'

weaknesses.issue: Reliability collapses past roughly 70% of a non-trivial app
weaknesses.evidence: Trustpilot reviewer summary: Lovable gets you about 70% of the way before fixes start breaking other things. Superblocks' hands-on review found a bill-splitting app whose 'Settle' button produced incorrect math and balances that didn't update, requiring manual code fixes; the reviewer concluded CRUD screens are reliable and 'anything beyond that is unreliable'. Multi-step flows require heavy hand-holding.

weaknesses.issue: Three security incidents in thirteen months, including a 48-day unpatched authorization flaw
weaknesses.evidence: A Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) flaw let any free account access other users' source code, Supabase database credentials, Stripe customer IDs and full AI conversation histories. Reported 3 Mar 2026, left open 48 days, then initially denied — The Register (20 Apr 2026) headline: 'Lovable denies data leak, cites intentional behavior'. This followed a February 2026 RLS crisis. Axios (7 May 2026) covered vibe-coding data leakage more broadly; RedAccess found ~380,000 publicly accessible assets from Lovable/Base44/Replit/Netlify, ~5,000 containing sensitive corporate data.

weaknesses.issue: Trustpilot sentiment is bimodal — people either love it or feel burned
weaknesses.evidence: G2 sits at 4.6 across 270+ reviews, but Trustpilot is 3.9 (as of May 2026) with 1,000+ reviews distributed as 64% five-star and 17% one-star, with very little in between. The complaints cluster on billing and reliability rather than capability.

weaknesses.issue: Fine-grained design edits get silently overwritten by later prompts
weaknesses.evidence: Superblocks' review documents that 'fine-grained design edits can be overwritten by subsequent prompts'. Because visual edits and chat edits write to the same files with no lock or protected-region concept, careful manual polish is not durable across agent turns.

weaknesses.issue: Revert restores code but not data — a real foot-gun after a bad migration
weaknesses.evidence: Docs state plainly that reverting 'does not restore or roll back your database data'. Revert is also blocked entirely for projects originating from a Cloud remix, and for old versions with the tooltip 'Cannot revert this far back in history'. A user who believes 'undo' is complete can lose or corrupt production data.

weaknesses.issue: Backend lock-in: region is permanent and Supabase→Cloud migration is unsupported
weaknesses.evidence: Docs: once Cloud is enabled 'the region cannot be changed' for a project and existing projects cannot migrate between regions. 'Migration from Supabase to Cloud is not supported'; Cloud→Supabase requires manual data export and schema rebuilding. An early wrong region choice is unfixable without rebuilding.

weaknesses.issue: Business plan doubles the price for identical credit capacity
weaknesses.evidence: The live pricing page shows Pro at $25/month with '100 monthly credits' and Business at $50/month with '100 monthly credits'. The pricing FAQ contains a dedicated defensive entry: 'Why is the Business plan more expensive?'. Teams needing SSO or role-based access pay 2x for the same throughput.

weaknesses.issue: Free tier is a demo, not a workspace — code is read-only and no custom domain is possible
weaknesses.evidence: Docs: 'Code editing is available on paid plans. On the Free plan the editor is read-only.' Free also cannot download the codebase as a zip, cannot buy or connect custom domains, and is capped at 30 build credits per calendar month and 5 lovable.app domains. Downgrading also brings the 'Edit with Lovable' badge back on the next publish (changelog, 14 Jul 2026).

weaknesses.issue: Credit exhaustion takes the backend down, not just the builder
weaknesses.evidence: Docs: at zero credits, building halts immediately, AI features in deployed apps fail, and 'built-in backend services will pause' — database, storage and authentication remain safe but inaccessible. Only static published pages keep serving. A live customer-facing app can therefore break because the owner ran out of build credits.

weaknesses.issue: Mobile app cannot do the design work it most needs to
weaknesses.evidence: Docs list preview-toolbar interactions, inline comments, the full mention picker, detailed code review, OAuth integration setup and account creation as desktop-only. So the four visual-editing modes — the product's most distinctive feature — are unavailable on mobile. Android users must also leave the app and buy through a web browser.

pricing_2026:
VERIFIED from lovable.dev/pricing and docs.lovable.dev (fetched 13 Aug 2026).

TIERS (monthly billing; the toggle offers Monthly / Yearly with a "2 months free" badge, i.e. ~16.7% off):
- FREE — $0/month. "Discover what Lovable can do for you". "No credit card needed". Includes: Free grants, Workspace-private projects, Unlimited collaborators, 5 lovable.app domains, Cloud, Community support.
- PRO — $25/month, 100 monthly credits. "Designed for fast-moving teams building together in real time." Adds: Unlimited users, all Free features, Credit rollovers, On-demand credit top-ups, Unlimited lovable.app domains, Custom domains, User roles & permissions, Per-member credit limits, Remove the Lovable badge, Email support.
- BUSINESS — $50/month, 100 monthly credits (same capacity as Pro at 2x price). "Advanced controls and power features for growing departments." Adds: Team workspace, Role-based access, Internal publish, Personal projects, SSO, Security center, Design templates, Priority support.
- ENTERPRISE — "Platform fee", "Volume based pricing", "Book a demo". Adds SCIM directory sync, audit logs, publish/invite restrictions, auto-retire abandoned apps, scheduled deep security scans, sensitive data detection, bring-your-own design systems, Git sync data residency, GitHub Enterprise (cloud or self-hosted), private npm registry, named CSM, custom SLA.
- STUDENT — "Verify student status and get access to up to 50% off Lovable Pro." Also "Lovable for campus" (contact sales) and "Lovable for kids" (with imagi).

CREDIT LADDER (docs, both tiers scale 100→10,000 credits/month):
Pro: 100/$25, 200/$50, 400/$100, 800/$200, 1,200/$294, 2,000/$480, 3,000/$705, 4,000/$920, 5,000/$1,125, 7,500/$1,688, 10,000/$2,250. Annual equivalents run ~$21/mo at the 100-credit rung up to ~$1,875/mo at 10,000.
Business: 100/$50, 200/$100, 400/$200, 800/$400, 1,200/$588, 2,000/$960, 3,000/$1,410, 4,000/$1,840, 5,000/$2,250, 7,500/$3,300, 10,000/$4,300. Annual ~$42/mo to ~$3,584/mo.

FREE GRANTS (Free, Pro and Business all receive these on top of plan credits):
- 5 daily build credits, resetting 00:00 UTC. Free is capped at 30 per calendar month; Pro and Business have no monthly ceiling. Unused daily credits expire same-day, no rollover.
- 20 Cloud credits per month.
- 4 AI credits per month (for AI features inside the user's published app).

WHAT CONSUMES CREDITS — one unified balance since 18 Jun 2026 covering three categories:
1) BUILD — messaging the agent. Plan mode is a flat 1.00 credit per message and never touches code. Build mode is usage-based, priced on files modified, logic complexity, codebase exploration and tool usage. Published examples: simple update/button styling 0.50, component removal 0.90, authentication setup 1.20, landing page with images 1.70–2.00. Per-message cost is visible in the message's three-dot menu.
2) CLOUD — database server size, storage, network bandwidth, file storage, compute, realtime features.
3) AI GATEWAY — model calls made by the deployed app's own AI features, scaling with model capability, token volume and call frequency. Veo 3.1 video generation is priced per second of output.

EXPLICITLY FREE (no credits): publishing and republishing; hosting, SSL and CDN delivery; Basic and Deep security scans; "Try to fix" on errors and "Try to fix all" on security findings (both "free within our fair use policy"); the first 100 inline text edits per user per day in the preview toolbar; adding comments in the preview; design-system verification turns; up to 50,000 transactional emails/month per workspace (overage 4 credits per 1,000).

TOP-UPS (Pro and Business only): Pro $0.30/credit ($15 for 50); Business $0.60/credit ($30 for 50). One-time purchases 50–10,000 credits, billed immediately via Stripe. Auto top-up triggers at a 25, 50 or 100 credit threshold, adds 50–1,000 credits per event, with a monthly limit of 100–25,000 credits or unlimited.

EXPIRY: monthly plan credits roll over while the subscription is active but expire 2 months after issuance; annual-plan credits expire 1 month after the period ends; top-up credits expire 12 months from purchase; Cloud/AI grants expire at calendar-month end (Free) or billing-cycle end (Pro/Business); daily build credits expire same-day. Spend order is documented: usage-specific grants first, then general credits closest to expiry.

SEATS: none. "Workspaces support unlimited members on all plans, and plans are priced by the credits they include, not by seats."

TRIAL: there is no time-limited trial. The Free plan is perpetual and card-free — a structurally different acquisition model from Remixer's 30-day no-card trial.

UNVERIFIED: the actual dollar price Lovable charges for a domain registration or transfer in-app. Docs state costs "vary by domain", that transfers carry a one-time fee adding one year per ICANN rules, and that "the annual renewal price is shown separately", but no price table is published. Do not quote a figure.
