one_line_positioning: A real in-browser Node.js dev environment (WebContainers) wrapped in a chat-first AI builder — "What will you build today?" — that gives non-developers a live preview and gives developers a file tree, editor and terminal one icon away, monetised by raw LLM token burn rather than per-message credits.
summary:
Bolt.new is StackBlitz's AI app builder. Its structural differentiator is WebContainers: a full Node.js runtime, npm and dev server executing inside the browser tab, so the generated app is genuinely running (not a rendered preview of a remote build) and the user can open a real terminal against it. In 2026 the product has been repositioned away from "AI IDE" toward "product builders" — the landing page speaks to Product managers, Entrepreneurs, Marketers, Agencies and Students, not engineers — while keeping the IDE intact behind a single disclosure control.

Landing → first render. The hero is "What will you build today?" (Inter Display 700, 48px, -1.2px tracking) over a blue radial glow on near-black #171719, sub-headed "Create stunning apps & websites by chatting with AI." The centre of gravity is a dark prompt card (#1E1E21, placeholder "Let's build a prototype...") with a plus icon bottom-left, a pill-shaped "Plan" toggle bottom-right, and a bright #2BA6FF pill "Build now" button. Below the card sit four 64×88 intent tiles — Website, Slides (badged "New"), App, Prototype — then "or import from" with Figma and GitHub pills. This is scope-setting without a wizard: no style chooser, no template picker, no questionnaire before the box.

The signup wall lands hard and early. Per Bolt's own quickstart, clicking "Build now" routes straight to "Sign in or sign up (Google, GitHub, or email: no credit card required)", then a survey, then "approximately five minutes while Bolt creates your app." Nothing is generated anonymously — the opposite of Remixer's 30-day no-card trial, and materially worse than competitors who render first and gate later. Generation itself takes ~5 minutes by their own documentation, not 2-3.

The builder shell. Left is the chat panel at a CSS-declared 450px default (`--chat-default-width: 450px`), resizable via a drag handle tinted brand-blue at 50% opacity. Right is the "workbench" at `calc(100% - 450px)`. The top bar is 50px (`--header-height`) and splits three ways: project title menu left; an icon cluster dead centre — database icon, gear icon ("All project settings"), the `<>` Code Preview icon, a Device Preview icon (Expo QR), and a clock icon for Version history (moved there from the title menu in the 13–19 July 2026 release); and Share / Publish / GitHub icon top-right. One `<>` click swaps the preview for Code View: Files list, a CodeMirror editor (`--cm-cursor-width: 2px`) with an explicit "Save" button and Ctrl+S, and a bottom drawer carrying three tabs — Bolt, Publish Output, Terminal. That is the whole IDE, gated behind exactly one control, which is the cleanest solution in the category to the "expose code without scaring people" problem.

The editing model is unusually cost-aware. Right-clicking a file offers "Target file" (limit the agent's focus) and "Lock file" / "Lock all" (exclude it) — user-controllable blast radius. Highlighting code surfaces an "Ask Bolt" button that links the selection into the prompt box. In chat, "Select" targets a live preview element (with a "Pick from layers" sub-option), `@` tags files and folders, the plus icon opens Enhance prompt / Search Help Center / Import Figma frame / Connectors, `/clear` surfaces "Clear context", and the agent name ("Standard" or "Max", Max being Pro-only) sits bottom-left. Plan Mode — which replaced Discussion Mode on 3 Aug 2026 — is a pill that "highlights blue when active" and ends in quick-action buttons like "Implement plan". Version history is a labelled, bookmarkable timeline with "Restore this version" → "Restore version", but explicitly does not roll back databases.

Publish and go-live. "Publish" top-right opens "Publish your project": visibility dropdown (Public/Private), Manage access, "Run security audit" (paid, costs no tokens, results render in chat with a "Needs your action" section, resting label "Security audit up to date", 30/day), an "Edit domain" pencil, and Unpublish (two clicks). The default URL is a random `*.bolt.host`. Changes are not auto-live — you must click "Update". Custom domains are entirely manual DNS: www CNAME and root ALIAS/ANAME/flattened CNAME both to `site-dns.bolt.host`, TXT for subdomain verification, "up to 24 hours", SSL auto-issued after verification. Bolt does sell domains in-flow (transferable to Name.com after a 60-day lock) but offers no mailboxes at all.

Money. Free is $0 with a 300K/day and 1M/month token cap and Bolt branding. Pro is $25/mo ($18/mo billed yearly, "Save up to 28%") and pointedly says "Start at 10M tokens per month" — because the real ladder (Pro 50 = $50, Pro 100 = $100, Pro 200 = $200) only appears after signup. Teams is $30/member ($27 yearly). Tokens are raw LLM tokens, not abstracted credits, and that is the product's central wound: every message re-syncs the file system, so cost scales with project size, error loops bill at full price, and Trustpilot sits at 1.4/5. Bolt's own docs teach token thrift as a skill — the strongest possible admission that the meter is the experience.
pricing_2026:
Verified live from bolt.new/pricing on 13 Aug 2026 (verbatim). Toggle: "Monthly | Yearly" with badge "Save up to 28% with yearly billing". Header: "Start for free. Upgrade as you go."

FREE — $0. Bullets verbatim: "Public and private projects" / "300K tokens daily limit" / "1M tokens per month" / "Bolt branding on websites" / "10MB file upload limit" / "Website hosting" / "Up to 333k web requests" / "Unlimited databases".

PRO — "$25 per month billed monthly"; yearly toggle shows "$18 per month billed yearly" (= $216/yr). Bullets verbatim: "No daily token limit" / "Start at 10M tokens per month" / "No Bolt branding on websites" / "Share sites privately" / "100MB file upload limit" / "Website hosting" / "Up to 1M web requests" / "Unused tokens roll over to next month" / "Custom domain support" / "SEO boosting" / "Unlimited databases" / "Expanded database capacity" / "Choice of database provider" / "Image editing with AI".

TEAMS — badged "POPULAR". "$30 per month and member billed monthly"; yearly shows "$27 per month and member billed yearly". "You get everything in Pro, plus:" Centralized billing / Team-level access management / Granular admin controls & user provisioning / Share with your organization / Private NPM registries support / Design System knowledge with per-package prompts.

ENTERPRISE — "Custom", CTA "Ask for a quote". SSO, audit logs, compliance, dedicated account manager, 24/7 priority support, custom SLAs, data governance.

HIDDEN PRO LADDER (not on the public pricing page; named in support.bolt.new/account-and-subscription/billing): "Pro 10M" $216/yr, "Pro 26M" $540/yr, "Pro 50" $50/mo, "Pro 100" $100/mo, "Pro 200" $200/mo. Third-party 2026 sources map these to 26M / 55M / 120M tokens per month respectively — MEDIUM confidence, not confirmed on a Bolt-owned page.

TOKEN MODEL: raw LLM tokens, not abstracted credits. Consumed when Bolt "reads your prompts and project files, thinks, responds to your prompts, and builds in your project." Bolt's own FAQ: "Most token usage is related to syncing your project's file system to the AI: the larger the project, the more tokens used per message." Plan Mode "uses fewer tokens because it doesn't make any changes to your project." Security audits cost NO tokens. Version-history restores and UI-button actions cost no tokens. Rollover: paid-plan unused tokens "stay valid for two months from the start of the billing cycle in which you received them", consumed first-in-first-out; free-plan tokens do not roll over. Free daily cap resets daily, monthly allowance resets on the 1st; paid resets on renewal date.

TOKEN RELOADS: documented as existing but priced per-plan — "You'll see the cost for your plan when you go to reload tokens." Third-party sources cite "$20 per 10M tokens" and say reload tokens never expire while the subscription is active — MEDIUM/LOW confidence, no Bolt-owned page states a number.

HOSTING LIMITS: Free "Up to 10 GB bandwidth", 333,333 requests/month, site goes offline until next billing cycle on overage. Pro "Up to 30 GB bandwidth", 1M requests/month, pay-as-you-go overage with a user-set spending cap.

TRIAL: none. No free trial of paid features; Free tier is the trial. No credit card required to sign up.

REFERRAL (release notes, 4–12 July 2026): referred friend gets 20% off, referrer earns "15% of their revenue (up to $50 per referral)".

REFUNDS: "Bolt subscriptions are non-refundable, as stated in our Terms of Service." Cards/debit only — no PayPal or bank transfer.

UNVERIFIED: exact token counts attached to Pro 50/100/200; exact reload SKU prices; Enterprise pricing.

findings.title: Full design-token set extracted live from bolt.new (measured, not inferred)
findings.detail: Read directly from the running :root CSS custom properties on 13 Aug 2026. Brand: --bolt-ds-brand = rgb(20 136 252) = #1488FC; --bolt-ds-brandHover = #2BA6FF; --bolt-ds-onBrand = #EEF9FF; brandBgSubtle/brandBorderSubtle = #2ba6ff1a. Surfaces: --bolt-ds-bg #111114, --bolt-ds-bgAlt/bgSecondary #171719, --bolt-ds-bgTertiary #1E1E21, bgTertiaryHover #2C2C30, inverseBg #FFFEFE, utilHover #FFFEFE0a. Text: textPrimary #F9F6F9, textSecondary #D6D5DE, textTertiary #A4A3AC. Icons: iconPrimary #F9F6F9, iconSecondary #A4A3AC, iconTertiary #73737B. Borders: borderPrimary #2C2C30, borderSecondary #1E1E21, divider #2C2C30. Semantics: success #16A34A (hover #4ADE80), warning #F79009, danger #EF4444, neutral #73737B — each with a matching *BgSubtle at 1a alpha and hover at 33 alpha. NOTE FOR REMIXER: Bolt's action blue #1488FC is within 3 points of our #1587FF. We are already colour-twins with them; that is a differentiation problem, not a coincidence to celebrate.

findings.title: Typography: Inter Display for headings, Inter for body, with optical sizing and stylistic sets on
findings.detail: document.fonts reports exactly six loaded faces: Inter 400/500/600/700 and Inter Display 600/700. The h1 computes to font-family "Inter Display", 48px size, 48px line-height (1.0 ratio), weight 700, letter-spacing -1.2px (-0.025em), colour #F9F6F9. Root sets --font-settings: "cv01", "ss03" (Inter's single-storey a and rounded-quote alternates) and --font-variations: "opsz" auto. Monospace stack is --bolt-font-monospace: ui-monospace, "Fira Code", Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New". The expensive feel comes from three cheap decisions: a display-optical cut for headings only, line-height locked to 1.0 at display size, and negative tracking — not from a custom typeface.

findings.title: Radius language is deliberately mixed: 6px chrome, 8px base, full pills for AI actions
findings.detail: --radius is .5rem (8px) as the base token, but measured components diverge on purpose. Nav 'Sign in' and 'Get started' = 6px. Project-type tiles = 6px. But the two AI-intent controls — the 'Plan' toggle and the 'Build now' submit — are border-radius: 9999px full pills, as are the Figma/GitHub import chips (73×28 and 78×28). Pill shape is reserved as the visual signature for 'this talks to the AI'. That is a legible, stealable rule: chrome is rectilinear, agent actions are capsules.

findings.title: Chat panel is 450px by default and resizable, with a brand-blue drag handle
findings.detail: --chat-default-width: 450px; --chat-min-width: var(--chat-default-width); --chat-width: var(--chat-default-width). The resize affordance is themed: --chat-resize-handle-background-color: rgb(var(--bolt-ds-brand) / 50%), i.e. #1488FC at 50%. In chat-only mode (before the workbench exists) the panel expands to --chat-only-max-width: clamp(720px, 50vw, 1024px) — so the composer is generous pre-generation and collapses to a rail afterwards. Remixer's chat is ~408px; Bolt runs 42px wider and lets the user drag it.

findings.title: Layout maths are declared in CSS: 50px chrome, 35px side menu, workbench = 100% minus chat
findings.detail: --header-height: 50px, --panel-header-height: 50px (top bar and workbench panel headers deliberately match so the seam reads as one band), --side-menu-width: 35px, --workbench-width: calc(100% - var(--chat-min-width)), --workbench-inner-width: calc(var(--workbench-width) - 1rem) giving a 16px gutter that makes the preview float rather than butt against the edge. Dashboard: --dashboard-sidebar-width 300px, collapsed 64px, --account-selector-width 282px, --dashboard-content-max-width 1428px.

findings.title: The entire IDE hides behind ONE top-centre icon — the '<>' Code Preview icon
findings.detail: Bolt's answer to 'expose code without scaring civilians' is progressive disclosure through a single control. Docs verbatim: "switch to Code view using the Code Preview icon (<>)" located "in the top center of your screen", and the eye icon returns to Preview Mode. Nothing about the file tree, editor or terminal is visible until that one toggle is hit. The framing copy is explicitly reassuring: "Although Code View is generally intended for more technical users, the interface is shaped to feel approachable for anyone who wants to dig deeper."

findings.title: Top bar is split three ways with an unusual centre icon cluster
findings.detail: Left: project title menu (Duplicate, Rename). CENTRE (unusual — most competitors put these left or right): database icon → Database settings; gear icon → 'All project settings'; code icon (<>) → Code View; Device Preview icon → Expo QR for mobile; clock icon → 'Version history'. RIGHT: 'Share', 'Publish', and the GitHub icon. The version-history clock was moved INTO the top nav in the 13–19 July 2026 release: "The version history option has moved from the project's title menu to the top navigation." Centre-clustering the project-state icons keeps left/right reserved for identity and destructive/publishing actions.

findings.title: The terminal is a tab in a bottom drawer alongside 'Bolt' and 'Publish Output'
findings.detail: Docs verbatim: "In the bottom section of the page, notice three tabs: Bolt, Publish Output, and Terminal." So the real shell is not a separate mode — it sits beside the agent's own log and the deploy log in one drawer. Users are documented running `npm run build` and `npx knip --production --fix --allow-remove-files` in it. This is the single biggest capability gap versus every no-code AI builder: a genuine POSIX-ish shell against a live Node process, reachable in two clicks, and it is presented as just another tab rather than a scary developer mode.

findings.title: Terminal is themed with the Hyper Snazzy palette, not default xterm colours
findings.detail: --bolt-terminal-foreground #eff0eb on --bolt-terminal-background = bgAlt (#171719); red #ff5c57, green #5af78e, yellow #f3f99d, blue #57c7ff, magenta #ff6ac1, cyan #9aedfe, white #f1f1f0, brightBlack #686868; selection #97979b33. Bright variants are identical to normal variants (no washed-out second row). Someone deliberately picked a designer terminal theme instead of shipping xterm defaults — a small, cheap signal that reads as craft to exactly the technical audience most likely to judge the product.

findings.title: Editor is CodeMirror with an explicit Save step and Ctrl+S — not autosave
findings.detail: --cm-cursor-width: 2px in :root confirms CodeMirror. Docs give the exact loop: "Click the file in the Files list. Edit the file in the editor. Click Save or press Ctrl+S. Bolt automatically builds your changes. Switch back to Preview mode to see them." Manual edits therefore have a visible commit moment (Save button top-right of the editor) and trigger a WebContainer rebuild. Right-click in the Files list gives "New file…" and "Delete".

findings.title: 'Ask Bolt' appears on text selection inside the code editor and links the selection into the prompt
findings.detail: Docs verbatim: "Highlight the code you want to discuss or change. Click the Ask Bolt button (if the button doesn't appear immediately, try right-clicking). Bolt links the selection in the prompt box." This is the code-side twin of click-an-element-to-edit, and it converts an intimidating wall of code into a set of addressable targets. The parenthetical fallback ('try right-clicking') is a tell that the hover trigger is unreliable.

findings.title: 'Select' element-picker with a 'Pick from layers' sub-menu for overlapping elements
findings.detail: Docs verbatim: "Use Select to target a specific element in your app's preview and focus your prompt on that part of the interface." The Select button carries a small arrow revealing additional options including "Pick from layers" — the z-order disambiguation problem that every element-picker hits, solved with a dropdown rather than alt-clicking. Bolt has NO WYSIWYG/drag visual editor equivalent to Remixer's Visual Editor; selection scopes a prompt, it does not enable direct manipulation.

findings.title: Only two agents, named for outcome not model: 'Standard' and 'Max'
findings.detail: Verbatim: Standard = "Balanced for everyday building", "fast and token-efficient"; Max = "Maximum reasoning for complex tasks", "thinks more about each step". Switched via a drop-down at the bottom of the homepage chatbox, or by clicking the current agent name in the bottom-left of the chatbox inside a project. "Only Standard is available on the free plan. To use Max, upgrade to a paid plan." The landing page renders this as a comparison chip pair: "Bolt Agent / Standard / All users / Max / Pro only". Underlying model names are hidden from the picker — the marketing claim is "The best model, every time... Bolt automatically routes to the right model for each task, balancing quality and cost."

findings.title: Plan Mode is a pill in the composer that 'highlights blue when active' and ends in quick-action buttons
findings.detail: Toggled bottom-right of the chatbox; docs say it "highlights blue when active" and clicking again returns to Build Mode. It produces conversational strategy rather than code, and terminates in contextual quick-action buttons — documented examples include "Implement this plan" (which auto-switches to Build Mode), "Show an example", "Refine this idea", and "Implement plan". Plan Mode replaced the older Discussion Mode on 3 Aug 2026: "Plan Mode replaces Discussion Mode for exploring ideas or working through a build strategy without changing your code." On the homepage the same 'Plan' pill sits next to 'Build now', so the plan/build fork is offered before the very first prompt.

findings.title: Composer packs six affordances into a plus icon, an @ trigger and slash commands
findings.detail: Plus icon (bottom-left of chatbox) opens: "Search Help Center", "Enhance prompt", "Import Figma frame", and "Connectors" (MCP servers). Typing `@` tags a project file or folder with a filtering autocomplete. Slash commands: `/clear` surfaces "Clear context" in a menu; `/skill-creator` generates a reusable skill; `/$skill-name` manually applies a skill. 'Enhance prompt' opens a dialog titled "Help us enhance your prompt" with guided questions, then returns an editable recommended prompt rather than silently rewriting the user's words.

findings.title: User-controllable AI blast radius: 'Target file', 'Lock file', 'Lock all' via right-click
findings.detail: Docs verbatim: "Right-click the files you want to focus on. Click Target file." and "Right-click the files or directories you want to exclude. Click Lock file (single file) or Lock all (directory)." Framed as "Guide Bolt's focus" with the rationale "You'll get more accurate results if you're explicit about what Bolt should and shouldn't change." This is the most under-copied idea in the product: it simultaneously improves accuracy, prevents the 'small change broke another page' failure, AND reduces token cost — three complaints answered by one context menu.

findings.title: Hard signup wall BEFORE any generation — nothing renders anonymously
findings.detail: Bolt's own quickstart sequence: paste prompt in the chatbox → click "Build now" → "Sign in or sign up (Google, GitHub, or email: no credit card required)" → complete a survey → wait "approximately five minutes while Bolt creates your app." There is no anonymous preview, no teaser render, no 'see it first' state. Click count to first pixel of a real app: roughly 4–6 (type, Build now, choose auth provider, complete OAuth, answer survey) plus a ~5 minute wait. STRATEGIC READ FOR REMIXER: our 30-day no-card trial plus 2-3 min generation beats this on both axes, and Bolt inserting a survey between intent and payoff is a conversion leak we should never copy.

findings.title: Intent is set by four 64×88 tiles, not a template gallery or style chooser
findings.detail: Beneath the prompt card sit four icon tiles measuring exactly 64×88px, 6px radius, transparent background, 12px/500 labels in #D6D5DE: Website, Slides (carrying a small 'New' badge), App, Prototype. Below them, the line "or import from" with two pill chips — Figma and GitHub — styled bg rgba(16,20,28,0.55), 1px border rgba(150,190,255,0.16), 73×28 and 78×28, transition background 0.2s. There is NO style/theme chooser, NO colour picker, NO template carousel on the landing page. Scope selection happens in one row; aesthetics are deferred entirely to the prompt.

findings.title: A bespoke shimmering brand-blue loading bar gradient is a first-class design token
findings.detail: --loading-bar-background: linear-gradient(90deg, #0a0a0a 0%, #2ba6ff 21.5%, #fff 33%, #2ba6ff 65.5%, #0a0a0a 100%) — a five-stop sweep that runs black → brand blue → pure white → brand blue → black, so the highlight reads as a specular glint travelling along the bar. Paired with --shimmer-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, .06) for skeleton shimmer and --base-gradient-color: rgb(var(--bolt-ds-textPrimary)) driving a text-shimmer effect (--bg: linear-gradient(90deg,#0000 calc(50% - var(--spread)),var(--base-gradient-color),#0000 calc(50% + var(--spread)))) used for 'thinking' prose. Cheap to build, and it is a large part of why the wait feels premium rather than broken.

findings.title: Generation takes ~5 minutes by Bolt's own documentation — roughly double Remixer
findings.detail: Quickstart states the user should wait "approximately five minutes while Bolt creates your app." Because WebContainers actually installs npm dependencies and boots a dev server, the wait includes real package installation, not just token streaming. Users watch the file tree fill in, the agent's step log in the 'Bolt' tab, and the preview boot. Documented empty state during this window: "Your preview will appear here" — and it being stuck on that string is listed as one of the top documented failure modes.

findings.title: Documented top failure modes read like an error-state design brief
findings.detail: Bolt's own troubleshooting page enumerates: white/gray screen or missing preview; preview stuck on "Your preview will appear here"; Bolt not completing all requested tasks; project exceeding prompt size limits; Bolt becoming stuck or unresponsive; out of memory errors; WebContainer startup failures. Notably there is NO documented one-click 'Attempt fix' / 'Fix error' button — recovery is manual: read the Terminal tab, or switch to Plan mode and click "Implement plan". Bolt also tells users to open the BROWSER's own console ("On macOS: press CMD + Option + J") — outsourcing debugging to devtools is a real polish gap.

findings.title: Version history is a labelled, bookmarkable timeline — but it does NOT roll back the database
findings.detail: Clock icon in the top navigation → "View history" shows "a clear visual timeline of your backups". Backups are created automatically. Users can preview a version before committing, then click "Restore this version" (top-right after preview) and confirm with "Restore version", after which "a success message in the chat history" confirms it. Versions can be renamed via a "Change name" pencil and pinned via a "Bookmark" button. Critical caveat verbatim: "Restoring to an earlier project version will not change your current Bolt or Supabase databases." Restores cost no tokens and are explicitly recommended as a token-saving alternative to prompting an undo.

findings.title: GitHub auto-commits on every non-breaking change and polls for external edits every 30 seconds
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Bolt saves your work automatically. Every time you make a change that doesn't break the project, Bolt creates a commit for you" and Bolt "checks GitHub every 30 seconds for any updates made outside Bolt and pulls those in." The GitHub icon (top-right) menu offers "Log in to GitHub", "Configure the GitHub App", "Create new branch", "Disconnect project". Gap: "Bolt currently doesn't support merging branches in-app. You need to merge branches in GitHub." No commit-message UI — messages are machine-generated. The 'only commit if it builds' heuristic is a genuinely smart, stealable rule.

findings.title: Publish modal is a single dense surface: visibility + access + security + domain + unpublish
findings.detail: 'Publish' top-right opens a modal titled "Publish your project" containing: a visibility dropdown defaulting to Public; a Publish button; "Manage access" for private sites; "Run security audit" (paid plans); an "Edit domain" pencil icon to rename the URL; and "Unpublish" at the bottom (requires clicking twice to confirm). Visibility copy verbatim — Public: "Anyone on the web can view it and search engines can find and list it"; Private: "Only your team and invited users can see it." Private sites also support a trusted-domain rule so anyone with an email at a given domain can view. Consolidating go-live, who-can-see-it, and a security gate in ONE modal is a strong pattern.

findings.title: Publishing is explicitly NOT continuous — a separate 'Update' click ships changes
findings.detail: Verbatim: "changes you make to your Bolt project aren't automatically applied to your published site" — users must click "Update" in the Publish menu. Default URL is a random auto-generated `*.bolt.host` subdomain, editable later via the pencil icon. (If a user opts for Netlify instead, the URL is a random `netlify.app` name, and editing that name is "available on Teams plans only.") Draft/live separation matches Remixer's model; the exact unpublished-changes badge treatment is not documented — LOW confidence on whether there is a visual dirty-state indicator.

findings.title: Netlify was demoted from default deploy target to an opt-in dropdown choice
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Bolt now includes built-in hosting and custom domain management. Previously, these features were handled through Netlify." New projects default to Bolt Hosting; Netlify is selected via gear → 'All project settings' → 'Domains & Hosting' → dropdown. This is the same vertical-integration move DreamHost is structurally positioned to win: Bolt spent 2025-26 buying back the hosting layer it had outsourced, because the publish moment is where retention and margin live.

findings.title: Custom domains are 100% manual DNS — no Domain Connect, no one-click, even for domains bought through Bolt
findings.detail: Path: gear icon → "All project settings" → "Domains & Hosting" → "Connect a domain you own". Required records: www subdomain = CNAME to `site-dns.bolt.host`; root domain = ALIAS, ANAME, or Flattened CNAME to `site-dns.bolt.host`; subdomains additionally require a TXT verification record. No nameserver change is required. Timing copy verbatim: "Most domains connect within a few hours, but in some cases, it can take up to 24 hours." Verification is manual-refresh: a "Status" column plus a "Verify domain status" button. SSL auto-issues after DNS verifies. READ FOR REMIXER: Bolt is exactly as bad at external domains as we are — our known Domain Connect gap is category-standard, not a category-losing deficit. The real weapon is domains already in the user's DreamHost account.

findings.title: Bolt sells domains in-flow but is a thin registrar reseller with a 60-day transfer lock
findings.detail: Path: gear → All project settings → Domains & Hosting → "Buy a new domain", or Profile icon → Settings → Cloud → Custom Domains tab → "Buy a new domain". Search results show a "Buy" button, then a "Purchase domain" / "Cancel" confirm. "The renewal cost is shown during checkout." Auto-renew is on by default and the card is charged "1 month and 5 days before the official renewal date" with a retry "5 days before the renewal date"; auto-renewal "must be enabled no later than 6 days before the expiration date." Domains are transferable to Name.com only after a 60-day lock (strongly implying Name.com is the upstream registrar). Since Jan 2026 users can buy a domain without attaching it to a project. Underlying registrar is not named on any Bolt page — MEDIUM confidence on Name.com being the provider.

findings.title: Zero mailbox offering — Bolt sells you a domain and then cannot give you an address at it
findings.detail: Across the full domains documentation set (domains, connect, purchase, aliases, dns-records, ssl-https, troubleshoot-domain) there is no mention of mailboxes, @yourdomain email, or MX provisioning for the user. The only email capability is transactional/outbound FROM the app (support.bolt.new/cloud/database/send-emails). DNS docs list MX as a supported record type the user may add manually, i.e. bring-your-own mail host. THIS IS THE CLEAREST STRUCTURAL WIN AVAILABLE TO REMIXER: Bolt will sell a domain at checkout and then leave the user to go buy Google Workspace. DreamHost can hand them hello@theirdomain.com in the same flow.

findings.title: Database is a 10-section settings surface behind a top-centre database icon
findings.detail: Database icon (top centre) → "Database settings" containing: Tables, Authentication, File Storage, Logs, Secrets, Security Audit, Server Functions, User Management, Advanced settings, FAQs. Postgres under the hood; Supabase became the default project database provider in Jan 2026, and Pro advertises "Choice of database provider". Bolt auto-provisions: "Bolt creates a database automatically if your project needs one, or if you explicitly ask Bolt to create a database." Framing copy: users "focus on building features rather than configuring servers" and get "one place for monitoring" without leaving for external tools. As of the 20–26 July 2026 release, "Databases in projects you've published to a live site are no longer automatically paused due to inactivity."

findings.title: User Management leads with a sign-ups graph, not a raw table
findings.detail: Database icon → User Management shows "a graph of sign-ups over time", "a list of the most recently added users", and search by email/ID. Actions: an "Add User" button offering "Create new user" or "Send invitation". A "Prevent Leaked Passwords" setting (shipped 20 June–3 July 2026) checks new user passwords "against a list of passwords that have appeared in known data breaches." Leading with a growth chart rather than a grid is a deliberate reframe: it makes an admin panel feel like a product dashboard.

findings.title: Stripe is a genuine one-click connector, not AI-written payment code
findings.detail: gear icon → "Stripe". Labelled steps: "Add Stripe API Key" → "Retrieve my products" → "Apply selection" → "Apply changes". Critically: "Bolt automatically handles webhook endpoint registration and signature verification. You don't need to manually configure webhook endpoints in your Stripe dashboard." Test-mode guardrails are explicit — "Make sure you are in test mode", "Test keys start with sk_test_", "Never use real payment details in test mode." Pulling the user's existing Stripe catalogue in ('Retrieve my products') rather than making the AI invent products is the detail worth copying.

findings.title: Figma import is outsourced to Anima and offers a Screenshot-vs-Code fork
findings.detail: Entry points: "Import from Figma" on the homepage, or plus icon → "Import Figma frame" in the chatbox. Flow: connect Figma account → "paste the URL of the Figma frame you want to import" → "Import Figma frame into Bolt". Verbatim: Bolt uses "Anima to handle turning Figma designs into apps." The user chooses "Screenshot" or "Code"; Screenshot is recommended when a design system is attached because the Code option "won't build with your components." Exposing that fork to the user is arguably a leaked implementation detail — most users cannot reason about it.

findings.title: MCP connectors, Google Stitch import, and a one-click Lovable importer
findings.detail: Connectors: plus icon → Connectors attaches MCP servers (shipped Feb–Mar 2026). Google Stitch designs can be imported as a build source. There is a dedicated "Import from Lovable" migration path — a direct competitor-poaching funnel documented as a first-class integration, which is a notably aggressive product decision worth noting for our own acquisition surface. Docs also warn connectors cost tokens: "Turn on connectors only when you need them" because activating them "adds information to context".

findings.title: 'Run security audit' lives inside the Publish menu, costs zero tokens, and has a resting 'up to date' state
findings.detail: Placed at the exact moment of consequence — inside the publish modal, not buried in settings. Scans, verbatim: "Who can see and change your data", "What information your app makes public", "How people sign in and stay signed in", "Ways your app can be misused", "What input your app accepts from visitors", "Your keys and security settings". Results render in the chat thread with an expandable summary of what was auto-fixed plus a "Needs your action" section for what the user must do. After a clean run the button becomes "Security audit up to date". Full-project audit is paid; the database security check is on all plans. Limit: 30 audits/day, reset midnight UTC. It does NOT consume tokens — a deliberate 'safety is free' signal.

findings.title: The public Pro price is a decoy — the real ladder (Pro 50/100/200) only appears after signup
findings.detail: bolt.new/pricing shows Pro as "$25 per month" with the hedge "Start at 10M tokens per month". The billing docs then reference "Pro 10M" ($216/yr), "Pro 26M" ($540/yr), "Pro 50" ($50/mo), "Pro 100" ($100/mo) and "Pro 200". Third-party 2026 sources map Pro 50 = 26M, Pro 100 = 55M, Pro 200 = 120M tokens (MEDIUM confidence — unconfirmed on a Bolt page). Practical effect: the advertised $25 anchors acquisition while heavy users land at $50–$200/mo. Upgrades are prorated ("You're charged only the difference"); downgrades "take effect at the beginning of your next billing cycle"; "Bolt subscriptions are non-refundable."

findings.title: Raw LLM tokens, not abstracted credits — and Bolt's own FAQ names the cost driver
findings.detail: Pricing FAQ verbatim: "Most token usage is related to syncing your project's file system to the AI: the larger the project, the more tokens used per message." So cost scales with project SIZE, not with user intent — a 'change the button colour' prompt on a big project can cost more than a whole feature on a small one. Rollover on paid plans: unused tokens "stay valid for two months from the start of the billing cycle in which you received them", consumed first-in-first-out. Free tokens never roll over. STRATEGIC CONTRAST: Remixer's 1,000 credits/mo is an abstraction that hides this volatility. Bolt's honesty about raw tokens is precisely what generates the complaint volume — exposing the meter makes users audit it.

findings.title: Paywall interruption points are scattered, not centralised — at least six distinct gates
findings.detail: Documented gates: (1) Max agent — "Only Standard is available on the free plan. To use Max, upgrade to a paid plan." (2) Custom domains — Pro only. (3) SEO Boost — requires a paid plan AND a custom domain, so it is unusable on .bolt.host. (4) Full-project security audit — paid only. (5) Analytics — "published to Bolt Hosting on a paid plan". (6) AI image editing/generation — "available only on paid plans", with generation additionally requiring a manual opt-in at Avatar → Settings → Account → "Add-on features" → toggle "Image Generation". Plus Bolt branding on free sites and a 10MB→100MB upload cap. Free users also hit a hard 300K/day wall that reviewers report exhausting "before a first build finishes."

findings.title: Token-free escape hatches are explicitly documented as a cost-management strategy
findings.detail: Bolt's token-efficiency guide teaches users to avoid the meter: Plan mode "uses fewer tokens because it doesn't make any changes to your project"; use UI buttons instead of prompting ("doesn't consume tokens"); "Use Version History to undo changes without tokens"; "Clear context"; "Tell the agent to focus on specific files or functions"; "Turn on connectors only when you need them"; "Reduce the size of your project by removing unused files"; "Avoid repeated automated error fix attempts". Security audits are also free. Having to publish a strategy guide for not spending money is simultaneously good customer service and an admission that the pricing model is hostile.

findings.title: One easing curve, one duration, applied uniformly across chrome
findings.detail: Every measured button transition resolves to 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) — Tailwind's ease-in-out — enumerated per-property (color, background-color, border-color) rather than 'all'. The exceptions are deliberate: the Figma/GitHub import chips use `background 0.2s, border-color 0.2s` (slower, because they are decorative glass chips), and the nav 'Resources' item uses `all`. A single 150ms curve for interactive chrome plus a slower 200ms for ambient elements is the whole motion system — no springs, no bounce, no scale-on-press. Restraint is doing the work here.

findings.title: No native Bolt app, and the mobile web builder is severely amputated
findings.detail: There is no iOS/Android app for Bolt itself. On mobile browsers, per supported-technologies: "Code view, project settings, and database access are unavailable on mobile devices." Separately, Safari (desktop or mobile) is degraded: "In Code view, your project files are read-only" and previews are hosted rather than run in-browser, requiring the user to prompt "Load the preview" — because WebContainers cannot run in Safari the way they do in Chromium. Safari support only arrived in the 27–31 July 2026 release. This is the direct cost of the WebContainer bet: the differentiator is also the portability ceiling.

findings.title: Mobile app BUILDS use Expo with a Device Preview QR — but Bolt cannot produce a store binary
findings.detail: Prompting for a "mobile app" scaffolds an Expo/React Native project. A "Device Preview icon" in the top centre generates a QR code for testing in Expo Go on a real phone. But shipping requires leaving Bolt entirely: users download the code and run `npx expo export --platform web` + `eas deploy --prod`, or `eas build --platform ios --auto-submit` / `eas build --platform android` on their own machine, because WebContainers cannot run Xcode, Android Studio, or the EAS build pipeline. Hard trap documented: "You can't change the slug after you create your first build, so choose carefully."

findings.title: Three named roles plus real multiplayer editing on public projects
findings.detail: Share button (upper-right) → roles: Viewer ("open, duplicate, and view the project and code"), Editor (adds environment variables, prompting, and code editing), Co-owner (adds inviting external collaborators and publishing). Link sharing via "Anyone with the link" with a warning: "Only set access to Editor if you want anyone with the link to be able to make changes to your project." Email invites show status `Pending` until accepted. Verbatim on multiplayer: "When your project visibility is set to public, collaborators can work together in multiplayer mode. This lets you prompt and edit in the same project at the same time" — though "Bolt processes one prompt at a time." Sharing and publishing "are available on all plans."

findings.title: Community and Templates are top-nav destinations, and Teams get private template libraries
findings.detail: Primary nav (verbatim, left to right): Community, Enterprise, Templates, Resources, Careers, Pricing, then 'Sign in' and 'Get started'. The Templates marketplace offers "pre-built projects with real data and working features that you can customize". Teams plans additionally get "Team templates" to "standardize project structure and configuration across organizations" (shipped Feb–Mar 2026). Project cards on the dashboard support a three-dot menu with "Rename", "Transfer", "Delete", plus "Duplicate" from the title menu. Dashboard sidebar filters verbatim: "Projects", "Created by you", "Starred", "Recently viewed", "Shared with you".

findings.title: 'Skills' — portable, conditional instruction files with a /skill-creator generator
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Skills are reusable instructions that teach Bolt how to handle specific scenarios." Distinguished from Knowledge: "Skills only apply in certain situations (defined in the skill description), while knowledge applies to every prompt." Created three ways: gear → Skills → "Add skill" → "Write manually"; via the built-in `/skill-creator` in chat; or imported from GitHub repos or local .md/.mdx/.zip files. Format is frontmatter with `name` and `description` plus plain-language instructions. Limits: 256 KB per file, 2 MB per .zip. Toggled on/off per skill; manually invoked with `/$skill-name`. Curated starters include "SEO/GEO" and "Web Design Guidelines". Available on all plans. Shipped 20–26 July 2026.

findings.title: Design systems generate a browsable Storybook — but it is a paid-Teams wall
findings.detail: A design system gives Bolt "a set of visual rules to follow" (colours, typography, spacing, component styles) so that "Bolt generates UI code that's ready to use because it's built from your actual components." Once processed, users can "explore the generated Storybook and see what components, tokens, and patterns are available" before prompting. Free users get read-only pre-loaded systems — Chakra, Material UI, Shadcn — but "you can't update or change them." Adding your own requires a paid Team plan. Marketing copy: "Build with design system — Stop building from scratch. Start building on-brand." Generating a live Storybook as the user-facing artefact of an abstract 'brand upload' is the standout idea here.

findings.title: Bolt Slides: a whole second output type shipped in July 2026 with presenter mode
findings.detail: Prompt-generated decks with "default slide layouts, presenter mode, and annotations built in." UI: slide thumbnails sidebar, grid view, an editing canvas for selecting individual elements, and bottom presentation controls labelled sidebar, grid, previous, next, fullscreen, annotate, presenter. Decks publish to a live URL and support an optional password gate: "Add a password screen before the presentation loads." Available on all plans. Strategically this is Bolt widening from 'websites and apps' into a third artefact class — worth watching as a pattern for Remixer's own surface expansion.

findings.title: Built-in analytics exist but ship with an honest, damaging caveat about bot traffic
findings.detail: gear icon → Analytics. Metrics: "unique visitors, pageviews, top pages, and bandwidth usage", plus "top traffic sources, visitor locations, and a list of top 'not found' (404) pages." Up to 30 days of data with Day/Week/Month filtering. Paid plans only, and only for sites published to Bolt Hosting. Caveat verbatim: the system currently includes "visits and actions from web crawlers and bots" without built-in filtering, so "reported page views, sessions, and other engagement metrics may be higher than actual human activity." Admirable honesty, but it renders the numbers unusable for anyone making decisions — a soft spot Remixer could beat with basic bot filtering.

findings.title: SEO Boost is prerendering, gated behind BOTH a paid plan and a custom domain
findings.detail: gear → All project settings → Domains & Hosting → "Enable SEO Boost" (becomes "Disable SEO Boost" when active). Mechanism verbatim: "When a crawler visits your site, SEO Boost renders the page and serves that HTML version instead of your JavaScript app." This exists because Bolt's output is a client-rendered SPA that crawlers cannot execute — a self-inflicted problem solved with a paid feature. Requires a paid plan AND a custom domain (explicitly not available on the free .bolt.host address), so free-tier sites are structurally invisible to search.

findings.title: WebContainers is both the moat and the ceiling — JavaScript only, no PHP or Python
findings.detail: Verbatim: "languages such as PHP or Python aren't compatible" and "Bolt only supports JavaScript-based backends." Supported: JavaScript frontends and Node.js backends, Postgres via Bolt Database/Supabase. Documented failure modes include "out of memory errors" and "WebContainer startup failures" — the browser tab is the VM, so the user's own RAM is the ceiling. Landing-page counter-claims: "98% less errors" and "Bolt handles projects 1,000 times larger than before. Its improved built-in context management can handle complexity" — both unsourced marketing numbers with no methodology given (LOW confidence in the claims themselves; HIGH confidence they are the exact strings on the page).

findings.title: Marketing voice is outcome-led and mildly under-punctuated
findings.detail: Section headers read as promises rather than features: "Empowering product builders with the most powerful coding agents"; "The best model, every time"; "Build big without breaking"; "Everything you need to scale — Built in."; "Whatever your role — Bolt gives you superpowers"; "Ready to build something amazing? Try it out and start building for free." Anti-friction framing recurs: "Stop stitching together platforms", "Bolt gives you everything you need inside one familiar interface no extra accounts, no steep learning curve", "Stop building from scratch. Start building on-brand." Note the missing em-dashes ('interface no extra accounts', 'iterates reducing errors') — the copy ships with real punctuation errors, which slightly undercuts the premium read.

findings.title: bolt.diy: StackBlitz maintains an open-source fork supporting 19+ model providers
findings.detail: stackblitz-labs/bolt.diy, ~19.2k GitHub stars, tagline "Prompt, run, edit, and deploy full-stack web applications using any LLM you want!" Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, OpenRouter, Google/Gemini, LMStudio, Mistral, xAI, HuggingFace, DeepSeek, Groq, Cohere, Together AI, Perplexity, Hyperbolic, Moonshot (Kimi), Amazon Bedrock, GitHub Models. Built on the same WebContainer foundation. Strategic effect: it converts the 'you're locked into their model and their token pricing' objection into a community goodwill asset, and seeds developer mindshare that funnels back to the paid product. Star count MEDIUM confidence (single source, point-in-time).

findings.title: Enterprise credibility is built on a logo wall and a May 2026 Microsoft Azure partnership
findings.detail: Landing page logo strip verbatim: "Trusted by Google, Microsoft, Salesforce, AWS, Meta, HubSpot, Accenture, TikTok, Shopify, Chegg, Cloudflare, Netlify, FactSet, ByteDance, PwC, Mozilla, Intel, Xano, Stripe." In May 2026 Bolt announced a Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 partnership adding Microsoft Marketplace as a procurement channel (alongside AWS Marketplace), Azure-native deployment into a customer's own tenant, and Teams/M365 Copilot integration. Funding context: StackBlitz raised $105.5M Series B (Jan 2025, ~$700M valuation, ~$135M total) and reportedly hit $40M ARR by March 2025. Funding/ARR figures from third-party trackers — MEDIUM confidence.

standout_ux.name: One-icon IDE disclosure (the '<>' toggle)
standout_ux.what_it_is: The entire developer environment — file tree, CodeMirror editor, and a bottom drawer with Bolt / Publish Output / Terminal tabs — is hidden behind a single '<>' icon in the top-centre bar. The default view is chat + preview only. An eye icon returns you.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It resolves the central tension of AI builders: technical users abandon products that hide the code, non-technical users abandon products that show it. One toggle serves both without a mode-switcher, a settings flag, or a separate 'pro' surface. The docs even soften the entry: 'the interface is shaped to feel approachable for anyone who wants to dig deeper.' Remixer's right icon rail could carry the same single-control promise.

standout_ux.name: Right-click file governance: Target file / Lock file / Lock all
standout_ux.what_it_is: Right-clicking any file or directory in the Files list lets the user pin the agent's attention ('Target file') or fence it out ('Lock file' / 'Lock all'), under the heading 'Guide Bolt's focus'.
standout_ux.why_it_works: One context menu answers three separate complaints at once: the AI changed something I didn't ask about, the AI hallucinated across unrelated files, and the AI burned my credits re-reading everything. Giving users a manual blast-radius control converts an opaque cost into a lever they feel in charge of. Nothing in Remixer currently lets a user say 'do not touch this page'.

standout_ux.name: 'Ask Bolt' on code selection
standout_ux.what_it_is: Highlighting any span of code surfaces an 'Ask Bolt' button that links the selection into the prompt box as a referenced object.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It is click-an-element-to-edit, but for code — it turns an intimidating file into a set of addressable, promptable targets. Crucially the selection becomes a visible chip in the composer, so the user can see what scope they attached before sending. Cheap to build, and it makes code view feel conversational instead of clinical.

standout_ux.name: Plan Mode as a composer pill with terminal quick-actions
standout_ux.what_it_is: A pill-shaped 'Plan' toggle sits beside 'Build now' — on the landing page AND inside the builder — that 'highlights blue when active'. It produces strategy in chat rather than code, and the response ends in contextual buttons like 'Implement this plan', 'Show an example', 'Refine this idea' that auto-switch back to Build Mode.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Three things at once: it is the cheapest possible undo (nothing was built, so nothing must be reverted), it is a token-saving mechanism Bolt explicitly markets as such, and offering it before the FIRST prompt reframes the product from slot machine to collaborator. The quick-action button that flips the mode for you removes the one step users would otherwise forget.

standout_ux.name: Security audit inside the Publish modal, free of tokens
standout_ux.what_it_is: A 'Run security audit' button placed in the publish flow itself. It scans data access, public exposure, auth, abuse vectors, input handling and key hygiene; auto-fixes what it can; surfaces the rest under a 'Needs your action' heading in chat; then settles into a 'Security audit up to date' resting state.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Placement is the whole trick — the anxiety about shipping something insecure peaks at the moment you press publish, and that is exactly where the reassurance sits. Making it cost zero tokens signals 'we are not monetising your safety'. And the resting label turns a one-off action into a persistent trust badge the user can re-check.

standout_ux.name: The one-surface Publish modal
standout_ux.what_it_is: 'Publish your project' bundles visibility (Public/Private with plain-English consequences), Manage access, Run security audit, an Edit-domain pencil, the Publish/Update action, and Unpublish — in a single modal.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Every other builder scatters these across a publish button, a settings page, and a share sheet. Consolidating go-live, who-can-see-it, is-it-safe, and what's-the-URL into one surface means the user makes all the launch decisions in one cognitive pass. The Public/Private copy ('Anyone on the web can view it and search engines can find and list it') explains the consequence rather than naming the setting.

standout_ux.name: Commit-only-if-it-builds GitHub sync
standout_ux.what_it_is: 'Every time you make a change that doesn't break the project, Bolt creates a commit for you', plus a 30-second poll of GitHub to pull in changes made outside Bolt.
standout_ux.why_it_works: The heuristic is the insight: auto-committing everything produces a history of garbage, while manual commits never happen. Gating on 'the project still builds' means every point in history is a restorable, working state — which is exactly what a non-developer's mental model of 'undo' actually expects. The 30s pull makes Bolt a citizen of the repo rather than the owner of it.

standout_ux.name: Design system → browsable Storybook
standout_ux.what_it_is: Uploading a design system produces a generated Storybook the user can explore before prompting: 'see what components, tokens, and patterns are available'. Free users get read-only Chakra / Material UI / Shadcn.
standout_ux.why_it_works: 'Upload your brand' is an abstract promise users cannot verify. Rendering it back as a browsable component catalogue makes an invisible configuration tangible, sets accurate expectations about what the AI can compose from, and gives the user vocabulary to prompt with ('use the Card component'). It converts a settings screen into a confidence-building artefact.

standout_ux.name: The shimmering brand loading bar
standout_ux.what_it_is: A five-stop CSS gradient token — linear-gradient(90deg, #0a0a0a 0%, #2ba6ff 21.5%, #fff 33%, #2ba6ff 65.5%, #0a0a0a 100%) — that sweeps a white specular highlight through brand blue, paired with rgba(255,255,255,.06) skeleton shimmer and a text-shimmer gradient for 'thinking' prose.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Bolt makes users wait roughly five minutes. Rather than a spinner, the wait is dressed as something precise and mechanical happening. It costs nothing to implement, it is a reusable token rather than a one-off component, and it is a large part of why a slow product still feels expensive.

standout_ux.name: Token-free escape hatches, documented as strategy
standout_ux.what_it_is: Bolt publishes a guide teaching users to avoid its own meter: Plan mode uses fewer tokens, UI buttons cost nothing, 'Use Version History to undo changes without tokens', '/clear' the context, target specific files, turn connectors off, avoid repeated auto-fix attempts.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It is a double-edged pattern worth understanding rather than copying wholesale. The good half: naming which actions are FREE (restores, UI edits, security audits) removes the low-grade anxiety of 'is this click costing me money', which is the single most corrosive feeling in a metered builder. Remixer should adopt the free-action labelling without adopting the need for a thrift manual.

weaknesses.issue: Token burn is the defining complaint, and it scales with project size rather than with user intent
weaknesses.evidence: Bolt's own pricing FAQ concedes the mechanism: "Most token usage is related to syncing your project's file system to the AI: the larger the project, the more tokens used per message." Third-party 2026 reviews report a simple 'add a login button to the navbar' consuming 15,000–25,000 tokens and 'add Stripe subscription billing with webhook handling' burning 50,000–100,000. Reddit sentiment analysis of r/boltnewbuilders (April 2026) is cited at roughly 54% positive / 29% negative / 17% neutral, with negatives clustering on token burnout. Some users report exhausting a 10M Pro allowance on one project in two weeks.

weaknesses.issue: Error loops bill at full price — users pay to have Bolt fix Bolt
weaknesses.evidence: Product Hunt reviewer, verbatim: "The tokens are a generous amount but it's unfortunate that they still get consumed when there's errors because solving the errors can take quite a while." Another: "When you ask Bolt to fix a simple bug or syntax issue, it often rewrites the entire file, breaks your UI/UX structure, and still fails to fix the original problem." Product Hunt reviewers estimate up to half their tokens went to errors. One 2026 review reports error loops consuming 7–12 million tokens in an afternoon; a Taskade-cited user reports 20M+ tokens spent fixing a single authentication issue. Bolt's own docs advise "Avoid repeated automated error fix attempts."

weaknesses.issue: Cost is unpredictable before you act — there is no documented pre-flight estimate or per-message token readout
weaknesses.evidence: Product Hunt, verbatim: "Token usage burns faster than you expect on bigger builds, and it is not always clear what a given action will cost before you run it." Bolt's token documentation describes viewing a balance (Profile icon → Subscription) but contains no reference to per-message cost display or a pre-send estimate. The docs' remedy is behavioural advice, not instrumentation.

weaknesses.issue: Trustpilot rating reported at 1.4/5
weaknesses.evidence: Cited in a 2026 aggregate review (superdesign.dev/blog/bolt-review) alongside billing-dispute support described as "thin". Single-source and not independently verified against Trustpilot directly — treat the exact figure as medium confidence, but the direction is consistent across Product Hunt and Reddit evidence.

weaknesses.issue: Small edits break unrelated parts of the app, and quality degrades with project size
weaknesses.evidence: Taskade review, verbatim: "The most common user complaint: making small changes (layout tweaks, format adjustments) can break other parts of the app." Same source: "Projects exceeding 15-20 components experience degraded context retention." Bolt's landing page counter-claims '98% less errors' and 'handles projects 1,000 times larger than before' with no stated methodology for either number.

weaknesses.issue: Free tier's 300K daily cap can be exhausted before the first build finishes
weaknesses.evidence: Bolt's own free tier is '300K tokens daily limit'. A Taskade review reports the free tier "running out after 6-7 minutes of code generation"; an aggregate 2026 review states "the free daily cap often runs out before a first build finishes" — while Bolt's own quickstart says the first build takes "approximately five minutes".

weaknesses.issue: Hard signup wall plus a survey before any output is generated
weaknesses.evidence: Bolt's quickstart: click 'Build now' → "Sign in or sign up (Google, GitHub, or email: no credit card required)" → complete a survey → wait ~5 minutes. Nothing renders anonymously. This is the longest gap between intent and payoff in the category, and inserting a survey between the two is a textbook conversion leak.

weaknesses.issue: Custom domains require entirely manual DNS, with a 24-hour uncertainty window and manual status refresh
weaknesses.evidence: Docs require the user to add a www CNAME and a root ALIAS/ANAME/flattened CNAME to site-dns.bolt.host at their own registrar, plus a TXT record for subdomains. Verbatim: "Most domains connect within a few hours, but in some cases, it can take up to 24 hours." Verification is a manual 'Verify domain status' button against a 'Status' column. No Domain Connect, no automated registrar handshake — and notably this manual path is not documented as being bypassed even for domains purchased through Bolt itself.

weaknesses.issue: No mailbox capability whatsoever — Bolt sells the domain then abandons the user on email
weaknesses.evidence: The complete domains documentation set (domains, connect, purchase, aliases, dns-records, ssl-https, troubleshoot-domain) contains no mention of mailboxes or @yourdomain email provisioning. MX appears only as a record type users may add manually for a third-party mail host. The only email feature is outbound transactional sending from the app.

weaknesses.issue: Free-tier sites are structurally invisible to search engines
weaknesses.evidence: Bolt's output is a client-rendered JavaScript app; SEO Boost exists specifically because "crawlers cannot execute" it and serves "a pre-rendered HTML version of your pages to web crawlers". But SEO Boost requires BOTH a paid plan AND a custom domain, and is explicitly unavailable on the free .bolt.host address.

weaknesses.issue: Built-in analytics count bots and offer no filtering
weaknesses.evidence: Docs verbatim: the system currently includes "visits and actions from web crawlers and bots" without built-in filtering, so "reported page views, sessions, and other engagement metrics may be higher than actual human activity." This makes the paid analytics feature unreliable for any real decision.

weaknesses.issue: Version history does not roll back data — a restore can leave the app inconsistent with its database
weaknesses.evidence: Docs verbatim: "Restoring to an earlier project version will not change your current Bolt or Supabase databases." A user restoring a version that predates a schema change gets code and data out of sync, with no warning documented in the restore confirmation flow.

weaknesses.issue: WebContainers caps the addressable market: JavaScript only, no PHP or Python, and Safari/mobile are degraded
weaknesses.evidence: Verbatim: "languages such as PHP or Python aren't compatible"; "Bolt only supports JavaScript-based backends." Safari — only supported since the 27–31 July 2026 release — has read-only Code View and hosted rather than in-browser previews. On mobile browsers, "Code view, project settings, and database access are unavailable." Documented failure modes include "out of memory errors" and "WebContainer startup failures" because the browser tab is the VM.

weaknesses.issue: Mobile apps can be generated but never shipped from inside Bolt
weaknesses.evidence: Expo/React Native projects preview via a Device Preview QR in Expo Go, but store submission requires leaving Bolt entirely to run `eas build --platform ios --auto-submit` on a local machine, since WebContainers cannot run Xcode, Android Studio, or the EAS pipeline. Plus a permanent trap: "You can't change the slug after you create your first build, so choose carefully."

weaknesses.issue: No in-app error-recovery button; debugging is outsourced to the browser's devtools
weaknesses.evidence: The troubleshooting docs describe no 'Attempt fix' or 'Fix error' control. Recovery guidance is to read the Terminal tab, or switch to Plan mode and click 'Implement plan'. Bolt also instructs users to open the browser console directly: "On macOS: press CMD + Option + J" — a hard stop for the non-technical personas the landing page targets.

weaknesses.issue: No refunds, and the advertised $25 Pro price understates real cost for active users
weaknesses.evidence: Verbatim: "Bolt subscriptions are non-refundable, as stated in our Terms of Service." Payment is card/debit only. Meanwhile the real usage ladder (Pro 50 = $50/mo, Pro 100 = $100/mo, Pro 200 = $200/mo) is absent from the public pricing page, which advertises "$25" with the hedge "Start at 10M tokens per month". Reddit reports of users spending $1,000+ on top-ups for ambitious builds are cited in 2026 reviews.

weaknesses.issue: Cannot merge Git branches in-app, breaking the workflow it invites users into
weaknesses.evidence: Docs verbatim: "Bolt currently doesn't support merging branches in-app. You need to merge branches in GitHub." Bolt offers 'Create new branch' in its own UI, so users are led into a branching workflow they must then leave the product to complete.

weaknesses.issue: Positioned as worse than Lovable for the exact non-technical personas Bolt's landing page now targets
weaknesses.evidence: Multiple 2026 head-to-head comparisons converge: "Lovable produces more polished output and handles deployment to custom domains automatically"; "Lovable is the better choice for non-developers shipping real products; Bolt is better for fast prototyping and throwaway demos"; Bolt's apps "usually need cleanup before launch." Bolt's homepage sells to Product managers, Entrepreneurs, Marketers and Agencies while reviewers keep describing it as "developer-centric".
