one_line_positioning: "Every builder needs a base" — a batteries-included, non-technical vibe-coding platform where the backend (DB, auth, email, analytics, payments, hosting) is invisible and pre-wired, now the growth engine of Wix's AI product line and the first app builder shipping its own in-house LLM.
summary:
Base44 is Wix's non-technical AI app/website/agent builder, acquired June 2025 for ~$80M and now reported at ~2M users and a ~$150M ARR run rate (TechCrunch, June 2026). Its thesis is the opposite of Lovable/Bolt: hide the stack entirely. Database, auth, storage, transactional email, analytics, payments and hosting are pre-provisioned in every app — no Supabase, no Vercel, no keys. The marketing line is "The whole stack. No setup slowdown."

ONBOARDING. base44.com's hero is not a working prompt box — it's an animated composer showing "Build"/"Send" cycling through [Apps][Websites][Games][Tools], with a "Start building" CTA that hands off to app.base44.com. The signup wall lands at prompt submission, before you get an app: docs say "you will be asked to sign up. This makes sure your work is saved, so you can return to your app anytime." Free tier needs no card. Five documented start paths sit behind a "+" in the prompt box: plain prompt, Plan mode, start from an existing URL, import a Figma frame (OAuth, public frame link, not a plugin), or connect tools. Plan mode is the interesting one — the AI interviews you about problem, audience, core functionality, design preferences and key flows/roles at "a fraction of a credit per message," then you click "Start building" and the first build costs ~1 credit. Time to first app is reported at 3–5 minutes.

BUILDER SHELL. Three zones: AI chat LEFT, live preview RIGHT, and a Dashboard reached from the top bar. The top bar carries preview, dashboard, code, testing tools, a Theme (palette) icon, a Canvas icon, a device/screen switcher, a searchable page dropdown (600 pages max), and Publish at top right. Credit balance appears when you click the Base44 logo in the editor. Canvas is a genuinely distinctive surface: an infinite board where every page renders as a live-preview frame at desktop/tablet/phone, with real-time multiplayer (named cursors, colored selections, sticky notes, freehand drawing, reference images) and Figma-grade shortcuts (V/H/D/N/I, ⌘1 fit, ⌘0 100%, ⇧⌘L lock).

EDITING MODEL. Three chat modes — Default (acts instantly), Discuss (plans safely, flat 0.3 credits), Edit (click elements in preview) — switched with Cmd+. / Ctrl+. even mid-typing. You can queue 7 messages, dictate via mic, set Custom Instructions, and Freeze Files so the AI can't touch them. Edit mode's toolbar exposes real tokens: Colors, font family/size/content, text style, per-side spacing in px, corner radius in px, opacity 0–100, and raw Tailwind classes. Crucially, manual visual edits cost zero credits. Versioning is a clock icon in chat plus a Revert icon on every chat message; branches (Aug 2026) replace Publish with "Merge to main" and support 5 parallel builds, but disable publishing, secrets, connectors, workflows, code editor, theme settings and version-history restore.

PUBLISH. Apps live at myapp.base44.app (renameable via Dashboard → Domains → "Edit URL"). The publish menu offers copy URL, "Connect a custom domain"/"Get Domain", "Share your app", "App Visibility" (Public/Private/Workspace with smart defaults) and "Publish App". A "Testing Link" shares unpublished changes running against test data. Domains buy-in-flow via Wix or IONOS is DNS+SSL automatic; external domains are manual — ANAME/ALIAS @ → base44.onrender.com or A @ → 216.24.57.1, plus CNAME www, remove AAAA, fix CAA, 48–72h, then click "Verify". They are Render-hosted. Email is outbound-only from no-reply@base44-apps.com via SendGrid CNAMEs; docs state flatly "Custom email domains are for sending only" — Base44 cannot give you a mailbox, which is exactly Remixer's structural opening.

MONEY. Free $0 / Starter $16 / Builder $40 / Pro $80 / Elite $160 monthly-equivalent billed annually ("SAVE 20%"), or $20/$50/$100/$200 month-to-month. Two currencies: message credits (25/100/250/500/1,200) and integration credits (100/2,000/10,000/20,000/50,000). Free is capped at 5 message credits/day and 5 apps. Nothing rolls over. The dangerous one is integration credits — a shared workspace pool consumed by your live app's users, so exhaustion pauses production features, not just building.

DESIGN. Two design languages. The marketing site runs Dazzed + Geist on warm paper neutrals (#f9f7f4, #f1eeea, ink #1e1e24) with orange #ff6a00, tight 6–8px radii and easeOutQuint. The editor runs a formal token system namespaced `[data-ds=base44]` on Wix Madefor Text/Display + Dazzed + Azeret Mono — Wix's corporate typeface now sits inside the product. Two neutral ramps (cool `neutral`, warm `stone`), a 4px spacing grid, 5%-alpha warm-black shadows, and a motion set of 80/120/180/260/360ms on cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) with a spring variant. The standout: "premium" is a first-class semantic intent alongside accent and destructive — orange, with full primary/secondary/light/ghost × default/hover/active/disabled coverage and its own focus ring. Upsell is designed, not bolted on.
pricing_2026:
VERIFIED from base44.com/pricing (fetched 13 Aug 2026) and Base44's own blog "How much does Base44 cost".

Toggle: "Yearly / SAVE 20%" vs "Monthly".

Annual-billed (displayed as /mo, "Billed annually"):
- Free — $0
- Starter — $16/mo
- Builder — $40/mo (badged "Popular")
- Pro — $80/mo
- Elite — $160/mo

Month-to-month: Starter $20, Builder $50, Pro $100, Elite $200 (confirmed by Base44's own blog table).

CREDIT ALLOWANCES (two separate currencies):
- Free: 25 message credits/mo + 100 integration credits/mo. Hard sub-cap of 5 message credits/DAY, reset at midnight in the workspace owner's timezone (UTC if none recorded). Max 5 apps. Max 3 custom analytics events.
- Starter: 100 message + 2,000 integration. Unlimited apps.
- Builder: 250 message + 10,000 integration.
- Pro: 500 message + 20,000 integration.
- Elite: 1,200 message + 50,000 integration, plus "25 credits to share with a friend".
Enterprise: custom credits, quote-only ("Contact sales").

WHAT BURNS MESSAGE CREDITS (build-time, per docs):
- Simple visual/text change ~0.5
- Small feature improvement ~1
- Complex module addition ~2
- Large-scale/app-wide change ~3–4
- Discuss-mode message: flat 0.3
- Plan mode: "a fraction of a credit per message"; first build after "Start building" ≈ 1 credit
- Testing-agent run: 1–4 credits; AI-generated tests ~half a run
- Social content plan: 10 credits; post improvement/image regen: 1

WHAT BURNS INTEGRATION CREDITS (runtime, consumed by your live app's end users):
- Email 1 (2 from a custom domain); file upload/extraction 1 each; image generation 1; video generation 5 per second; speech 1 per 50 characters (max 100/call)
- LLM call: Automatic ~1, Gemini 3 Flash ~5, GPT-5.4 ~15
- In-app agents per message: Automatic ~3, Gemini 3 Flash ~5, GPT-5.6 Sol ~40
- Automations: 1 baseline + nested integrations; workflow steps consume fractions per step

FREE OF CHARGE: database reads/writes, manual visual edits (drag, layout, direct text editing), adding components from the component library.

NO ROLLOVER: "Unused credits do not carry over." Non-refundable for AI mistakes.

TOP-UPS — CONFLICTING OFFICIAL SOURCES, UNRESOLVED: docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Credits states top-ups are unavailable and users must "upgrade or adjust your plan"; base44.com/blog/how-much-does-base44-cost FAQ states "You can top up your credits at any time without changing plans." Treat as unverified.

TRIAL: no time-boxed trial. The Free plan is the trial, permanent but 5 credits/day. No credit card required.

REFERRALS: referee gets 30 credits at signup; referrer gets 30 when the referee publishes and sends a message, +100 when they upgrade. Referral credits expire 40 days after being earned.

PAYWALL GATES: custom domain + private apps + in-app code edits + unlimited apps (Starter+); AI model select, GitHub integration, connectors, backend functions, workflows, design systems, Base44 Payments, app-store IPA/AAB export (Builder+); code-vulnerability scanning (Builder+); entity/data version history (Elite, 7-day; Enterprise 30-day); premium support (Elite).

BILLING MECHANICS: upgrades effective immediately on payment; downgrades at end of period; monthly→yearly credits the already-paid month. Visa/Mastercard/Amex/Discover; Enterprise can pay by invoice or ACH. Student/educator discount claimable in-product via a 3-step flow (shipped 30 Jul 2026).

findings.title: Hero is a decorative composer, not a working prompt box
findings.detail: base44.com's hero renders headline "Every builder needs a base" over an animated fake composer cycling "Build" / "Send" against rotating nouns [Apps] [Websites] [Games] [Tools]. There is no real generation input on the marketing page — every CTA ("Start building", "Build an app", "Build a website with AI", "Create an AI agent") hands off to app.base44.com. Contrast with Lovable/Bolt/Remixer, which let you type the first prompt on the landing page.

findings.title: Signup wall fires at prompt submission, before you see an app
findings.detail: Docs state verbatim: "you will be asked to sign up. This makes sure your work is saved, so you can return to your app anytime." The gate is framed as work-preservation rather than as a wall. This is EARLIER than the industry-common pattern of showing a first render then gating — meaning Base44 never gives an anonymous taste of output.

findings.title: Five documented start paths behind a single "+" in the prompt box
findings.detail: Accordion in the quick-start names: (1) Use a prompt, (2) Use plan mode, (3) Start from an existing URL, (4) Start from a Figma design, (5) Connect your tools (Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub). In the composer these live behind a "+" icon: Import from Figma, Start from URL, Attach Files (images, PDFs, spreadsheets, documents), Connectors, Explore component library, Use a design system.

findings.title: Plan mode: the AI interviews you before it builds anything
findings.detail: Selecting Plan mode from the mode dropdown makes the AI ask structured questions about problem definition, target audience, core functionality requirements, design preferences, and key flows and roles. The user refines conversationally, then clicks "Start building". Docs: "Plan mode costs only a fraction of a credit per message. Once you click 'Start building', your first build uses about 1 credit." This is a deliberate cheap-discovery / expensive-execution split.

findings.title: 3–5 minutes to first render, with a checkbox build log
findings.detail: Multiple 2026 hands-on reviews report ~5 minutes for the initial build with "real-time updates on the app's features and design". No Code MBA's teardown describes a build log panel rendering tasks as checkboxes: "Generate schema, Create routes, Seed data" — a task-list metaphor rather than streaming prose or a filling file tree. Remixer's 2-3 min is faster.

findings.title: Model picker with 7 named models, gated at Builder ($40/mo)
findings.detail: Editor Settings icon → "AI Model" exposes: Auto, Base 1, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8, GPT-5.6 Terra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Fable 5. Docs: access "requires a Builder plan or higher". Different models carry different credit costs, so model choice is simultaneously a quality and a billing decision surfaced to non-technical users.

findings.title: Base 1: first app-builder with its own proprietary LLM (29 June 2026)
findings.detail: Founder Maor Shlomo announced Base1 on 29 June 2026 — a model fine-tuned on an open-source foundation using "tens of millions of real user interactions" from Base44's own build sessions, positioned for latency/cost/UI-generation gains. It appears in the model picker as "Base 1". This is a defensibility play no competitor in the category has matched.

findings.title: Preview assembles live on the right; explicit thinking states with a Stop button
findings.detail: Docs describe the preview window showing "the app updating in real time as Base44 generates it". Troubleshooting names the AI's visible processing states as "thinking" and "applying changes", with a Stop button when it hangs. So the disclosure model is: named state label + task checklist + live preview, not a raw build log.

findings.title: Skeleton shimmer is a tokenized, per-theme gradient
findings.detail: Editor CSS defines --gradient-shimmer twice: light theme linear-gradient(90deg, var(--stone-100), var(--stone-200), var(--stone-100)) and dark theme linear-gradient(90deg, var(--neutral-700), var(--neutral-600), var(--neutral-700)). Loading states are treated as design-system citizens with warm stone in light mode and cool neutral in dark, not one hardcoded grey.

findings.title: Three-zone shell: chat LEFT, live preview RIGHT, Dashboard as a mode
findings.detail: Docs: "The Base44 editor has 3 main working areas: the AI chat, the preview, and your app's dashboard, with a top bar above them." AI chat is on the left, preview on the right updating in real time. Structurally near-identical to Remixer's left-chat/center-canvas, but Base44 puts the entire backend behind a Dashboard *mode switch* rather than Remixer's right icon rail.

findings.title: Top bar inventory: preview, dashboard, code, testing, theme, canvas, device, page dropdown, Publish
findings.detail: Top bar gives "quick access to preview, dashboard, code, testing tools, and publishing". Also documented in the top bar: the Canvas icon, the Theme (palette) icon, a screen/device icon for Mobile/Desktop, and a searchable page dropdown above the preview showing the active page name. Publish sits top RIGHT. Credit balance is revealed by clicking the Base44 logo in the editor.

findings.title: Dashboard is a full second application: 10+ named sections
findings.detail: Documented Dashboard destinations: Overview (App Visibility, Payments Manage), Data, Security, Domains, Analytics, SEO & GEO, Logs, Workflows, Code (with Functions and Secrets), Settings → App Settings. This is a genuine admin console bolted to a chat builder — far deeper than a settings drawer.

findings.title: Canvas: infinite board of live app frames with Figma-grade shortcuts
findings.detail: Opened from an icon in the top bar. Every page appears as a live-preview frame at desktop/tablet/phone on an infinite board. Right-side toolbar: Select (V), Hand (H), Draw (D), Sticky note (N), Image (I). Bottom-right zoom bar; ⌘1 fit canvas, ⌘0 reset 100%, ⌘+/⌘- zoom, ⇧⌘L lock. Arrow connections drag from hover-revealed edge handles. Each frame has its own viewport dropdown top-right. Undo/redo in canvas shipped 30 May 2026.

findings.title: Three chat modes with a keyboard switch that works mid-typing
findings.detail: Default ("Acts instantly on your prompts"), Discuss ("Lets you plan and refine ideas safely before applying changes"), Edit ("Lets you click elements in your preview to adjust visuals directly"). Docs: "Press Cmd + . on macOS or Ctrl + . on Windows and Linux to switch modes, even while you're typing a prompt." That mid-typing qualifier is a real craft detail — you can reclassify an in-flight thought without losing it.

findings.title: Discuss mode is priced at a flat 0.3 credits to make thinking cheap
findings.detail: "Each message in Discuss mode uses 0.3 credits" — a fixed rate, versus variable 0.5–4 credits for Default/Edit. Base44 has explicitly made planning ~3-10x cheaper than executing, which nudges users toward conversation before generation and reduces wasted expensive builds.

findings.title: Message queueing (7 deep), speech-to-text, Custom Instructions and Freeze Files
findings.detail: "You can queue up to 7 messages at once." A microphone icon provides speech-to-text. Two agent-control features: "Custom Instructions: Add default guidance for every AI interaction" and "Freeze Files: Lock specific files or entities so the AI does not modify them". Freeze Files is the standout — a non-technical safety rail against the AI wrecking work you already approved.

findings.title: Two undo surfaces: clock icon in chat + per-message Revert icon
findings.detail: Version History is "the clock icon in AI chat". Separately, docs say "Click the Revert icon on a chat message to restore your app to a previous working version" — every AI turn is its own restore point, inline. Docs also warn that asking the AI to roll back in chat "never actually undoes prompt changes" — only Revert or Version History work.

findings.title: Branches (Aug 2026): Publish is literally replaced by "Merge to main"
findings.detail: Created by clicking the app logo/name at the top of the chat panel → "Create new branch"; AI auto-names the branch. While on a branch the branch name replaces the app name at the top of chat, and a "Merge to main" button occupies the slot where Publish normally sits. Statuses: Active, Working, Merging, Merged. Up to 5 parallel branch builds. After merge the branch becomes read-only but stays listed.

findings.title: Branches are heavily crippled — and they share LIVE production data
findings.detail: Unavailable on a branch: publishing, secrets, connectors, automations, workflows, in-app agents, code editor, theme settings, chat undo/edit, and version-history restore — all "only available on main". Worse, branches share live app data: "all branches read/write identical records". So a branch is a UI sandbox, not a data sandbox. Real risk of a non-technical user corrupting production data from an experiment.

findings.title: Data version history is an Elite-only ($160/mo) upsell shipped 1 Aug 2026
findings.detail: Changelog 1 Aug 2026: "Entity version history now available on the Elite plan" — 7-day data snapshots on Elite, 30 days on Enterprise. Everyone below Elite has no point-in-time recovery for their database. Separately, deleted apps are recoverable from Trash for 30 days (shipped 9 Aug 2026), and deleted records for 30 days via "Recently Deleted".

findings.title: Edit-mode toolbar exposes real CSS tokens including a raw Tailwind escape hatch
findings.detail: Clicking an element in Edit mode reveals: Colors (background + text, theme or custom), T (font family, size, text content), Text Style (alignment, case, decoration), Spacing (margin and padding in px, per side), Corners (border radius in px), Opacity (0–100), Tailwind Classes (custom CSS utilities), and a trash Delete icon. Shipping a raw Tailwind field to a non-technical audience is unusually brave — and a pressure-release valve for the design ceiling.

findings.title: Manual visual edits cost ZERO credits — the single smartest pricing decision
findings.detail: Docs list what does not consume credits: "Database reads/writes, manual visual edits (dragging, layout changes, direct text editing)." AI-assisted edits in the same Edit mode do cost variable credits. This means nudging padding or retyping a headline is free forever, so users never feel metered for fiddling. Directly relevant to Remixer, where publishing changes also burns credits.

findings.title: Theme panel: named color roles, eyedropper, and a two-stage Apply / Save & Apply
findings.detail: Palette icon at the top of the editor opens a Theme panel with Colors and Fonts tabs. Colors shows "a preview of your current palette at the top, followed by a list of color roles you can customize, such as background, foreground, primary, secondary, card, and popover" (shadcn/ui role naming). Picker supports drag, hex entry, screen eyedropper, or palette. Buttons: "Apply" (preview) then "Save & Apply" (global). Fonts tab has a per-font dropdown split into "Brand Fonts" and "All Fonts".

findings.title: Redesign prompts return four options side by side with previews before commit
findings.detail: Design Pack (May 2026): typing "redesign this in different styles" returns "four AI design options side by side". Section-scoped variants work too ("redesign this section as a vibrant product gallery") and "The rest of the project stays exactly as it is". Marketing copy: "Ask for design options, pick the one you want. AI shows previews before it touches anything." This directly attacks the #1 AI-builder complaint — generic output you can't steer.

findings.title: Design System object: brand-level tokens including tone of voice and core values
findings.detail: Two-panel editor (settings left, live preview right showing "buttons, icons, and cards"). Fields: Overview (brand description), Logos (upload or AI-generate primary + secondary), Typography (heading/body fonts with weights), Color Palette (editable or AI-generated), Tone of Voice, Core Values, Corner Radius, Spacing Scale, Shadow (position, blur, spread, color), Design Guidelines. Gated to Builder+, one system per workspace (unlimited on Enterprise). Note: "Applying a design system takes effect on a build turn in the AI chat." Generation from a text brand description shipped 28 Jul 2026.

findings.title: Code tab: split-screen code+preview with explicit Save/Discard, plus "Files used in this page"
findings.detail: Opened from the dashboard Code tab. File explorer left, editor main, split-screen toggle and More Actions top right, Save/Discard at bottom, "Exit split" to leave. More Actions → "Files used in this page" maps which files power the current page grouped by project location, with "See all files". That reverse-lookup is the bridge that lets a non-coder find the right file without understanding the tree.

findings.title: AI diffs are opt-in behind a message hover menu, colour-coded and side-by-side
findings.detail: Hover an AI-generated change in chat → three-dot icon → "View Changes" opens a modal with a file tree colour-coded green (new), amber (modified), red (deleted), a side-by-side diff view, and a stats bar of additions/modifications/deletions. Diffs are deliberately hidden by default so the non-technical default view stays clean — a good pattern for Remixer.

findings.title: Two separate observability surfaces: Activity Monitor (HTTP) and Logs (events)
findings.detail: Activity Monitor (More Actions menu) lists HTTP method, path, timestamp, status code with a search field, and a details panel with General / Request / Response tabs. Dashboard → Logs is a separate searchable event history split into Runtime (user activity, function calls, integrations, automations) and Setup (config, schema, domain changes), with an All Events dropdown, filter-by-email, an "Errors only" toggle, Refresh, and Details / Outputs / Error tabs per row.

findings.title: Test-data toggle lives as a database icon inside the preview itself
findings.detail: Preview carries a database icon labelled "Turn on test data" for mid-session environment switching. Copy is explicit and reassuring: "Your published app always uses production data. Turning on testing mode only affects data in the dashboard and in preview." The Data tab gains a "Test" button to switch views. Enabled from Dashboard → Settings → App Settings → Test Data toggle.

findings.title: "Act as a user" role impersonation before publishing
findings.detail: Quick-start pre-publish checklist: click the More Actions icon (⋯) and select "Act as a user" to test different roles; use the device menu for mobile; use incognito for a first-time visitor view. Role impersonation baked into the editor is a genuinely mature touch for apps with auth.

findings.title: Testing Agent runs real browser E2E tests and is free on every plan
findings.detail: More Actions → "Testing Agent". Buttons: "Generate tests with AI", "Add Test", "Add test manually", "Enhance Prompt", "Run test", "Stop test", "Fix with AI", "Test Again". Results split into Issues (labelled "Critical" or "Warning" with fix checkboxes) and Activity (step-by-step agent actions, expandable). Stale-state copy: "App changed since last run". Costs 1–4 credits per run but "available on all plans, including the free plan".

findings.title: Data panel shows tables as cards with an inline row-level-security warning icon
findings.detail: Dashboard → Data shows every table as a card with a More Actions ellipsis offering "View Data", "Export", "Schema", "Recently Deleted", "Delete All". Warning icons on the card flag row-level security risks — surfacing a security concept to non-technical users at the exact object it applies to. Field types: Text, Number, Yes/No, Date/Time, File, Reference, Object. "Add Item" → "Submit". Search bar spans all text fields; a Filters button sits top right. Unified Data page shipped 13 Jun 2026.

findings.title: Permissions are per-entity Read Access / Write Access, in plain words
findings.detail: Dashboard → Security → select entity → configure "Read Access" (view records) and "Write Access" (create, update, delete). No SQL, no policy language — two dropdowns per table. This is the deliberate simplification that made the July 2025 Wiz/Imperva vulnerabilities possible, and the reason a default-permissive trust model persists.

findings.title: App Visibility has smart defaults that infer public vs private from what you built
findings.detail: Dashboard → Overview → "App Visibility" dropdown: Public ("Anyone on the internet can open the app. No account is needed."), Private ("Only invited people can open and use the app. Sign in is required."), Workspace ("Everyone in your Base44 workspace can open and use the app. Sign in is required."). Base44 auto-applies a default — landing pages and portfolios default to Public without login. Private apps require a paid plan.

findings.title: Five zero-plan built-in integrations vs OAuth connectors gated at Builder
findings.detail: Free on all plans, "preinstalled in every app": Invoke LLM, SendEmail, UploadFile, GenerateImage, ExtractDataFromUploadedFile (CSV, PNG, JPG, JPEG, PDF). Requiring Builder+: OAuth Connectors (Notion, Slack, Salesforce, Google Workspace, LinkedIn, TikTok, GitHub, Gmail, Google Search Console, Snowflake, Databricks), backend functions, custom OpenAPI integrations and MCP connections. Marketing string: "Connect your Base44 apps, workspaces, and account to external tools and services".

findings.title: Custom integrations deprecated 1 March 2026 — a post-acquisition narrowing
findings.detail: Post-acquisition analysis dates the deprecation: from 1 March 2026 new custom integrations are no longer supported; existing ones keep working, new ones must be built as backend functions (Builder+). This moves a previously accessible capability behind a $40/mo plan and a more technical mechanism. Cited from a third-party tracker, not an official Base44 announcement.

findings.title: Publish button is top-right and opens a menu, not a modal wizard
findings.detail: Documented publish menu contents: copy the app URL, "Connect a custom domain" or "Get Domain", "Share your app" (email/social distribution), "App Visibility" access settings, and "Publish App" to push live. Notably there is no changed-files summary or diff-since-last-publish in the menu — reviewing changes before publishing is an open, upvoted request on Base44's own feedback board.

findings.title: "Testing Link": share unpublished changes running on test data
findings.detail: Publish (top right) → "Testing Link" → "Copy testing link". Docs: "People who open the testing link see your unpublished changes and interact with test data only" and "the link does not change your live app or production records." This is a real staging-share primitive that most AI builders lack, and it composes unpublished code with a sandboxed database in one link.

findings.title: Staging URL is myapp.base44.app with an inline "Edit URL" rename
findings.detail: Every app launches on a free myapp.base44.app subdomain "that can be personalized without DNS setup or payment". Renamed via Dashboard → Domains → "Edit URL" under the built-in domain section. Functionally identical to Remixer's editable *.remixer.app, but Base44 buries it in a Domains page rather than exposing a pencil affordance in the toolbar.

findings.title: Three domain paths, only two of which are one-click — and both require buying from Wix or IONOS
findings.detail: Dashboard → Domains offers: buy via Wix, buy via IONOS, or "Connect existing domain". Purchases get "DNS and SSL are set up for you automatically". Wix flow: "Buy new domain" → "Get It" → registration period → contact info → privacy option → "Submit Purchase". A free-year voucher "covers your first year" but only the free Basic Protection tier; Private Registration and DNSSEC cost extra. Base44 has no Domain Connect either — external domains are manual for everyone.

findings.title: External DNS exposes that Base44 apps are hosted on Render
findings.detail: Recommended: ANAME/ALIAS @ → base44.onrender.com, CNAME www → base44.onrender.com. Fallback where ANAME is unsupported: A @ → 216.24.57.1 (a Render IP), CNAME www → base44.onrender.com. Users must also "Remove any AAAA (IPv6) records" and "Remove or update any CAA records". Wildcard subdomains unsupported. 48–72h propagation, then a "Verify" button next to the domain. Docs even send users to whatsmydns.net — i.e. Base44 hands DNS debugging to a third-party site.

findings.title: Base44 cannot give you a mailbox — explicitly sending-only, via SendGrid
findings.detail: Docs state verbatim: "Custom email domains are for sending only" and that real business email "requires separate purchase or external provider configuration". Default sender is no-reply@base44-apps.com. Custom domain setup: Dashboard → Domains → Email domain section → "Use Your Custom Domain" → sender name + address prefix → "Connect Domain", status "Pending verification" → "Active". Three CNAMEs reveal SendGrid: em → u58367809.wl060.sendgrid.net, s1._domainkey and s2._domainkey → s1/s2.domainkey.u58367809.wl060.sendgrid.net. This is the clearest structural gap DreamHost can attack.

findings.title: Built-in email can only reach registered app users — no attachments, no external addresses
findings.detail: The zero-setup SendEmail integration is "limited to people who are registered users of your app" and does not support external addresses or file attachments. So a contact form that emails the site owner at their own Gmail is not a first-class path. Costs 1 integration credit per email, 2 from a custom domain, one custom email domain per app, Starter+.

findings.title: Two-currency credit model: message credits (you) vs integration credits (your users)
findings.detail: Message credits are burned by you while building (0.5 simple change, ~1 small feature, ~2 complex module, ~3–4 app-wide, 0.3 Discuss). Integration credits are burned at RUNTIME by your live app's end users (email 1, image gen 1, video 5/sec, speech 1/50 chars, LLM 1–15, in-app agent messages 3–40). Splitting build-time from run-time cost is more honest than a single pool — but it means a viral app can drain your workspace.

findings.title: Free tier is throttled to 5 credits per DAY, not just 25 per month
findings.detail: Docs: Free plan gets "5 credits daily (25/month), reset at midnight workspace owner's timezone (UTC if no timezone recorded)". The daily cap is the real constraint — it makes a single evening's build session impossible and forces a paid upgrade or a multi-day drip. Product Hunt review verbatim: "25 message credits a month, max 5 a day, and you'll burn through them just tweaking UI."

findings.title: Running out of integration credits pauses features in the LIVE production app
findings.detail: Integration credits are a shared workspace pool consumed by end users. Docs confirm out-of-credits "cancels in-progress runs" for workflows, and the Testing Agent shows "Test paused" if credits are exhausted mid-run. Third-party analysis reports mid-month feature pausing for emails, AI calls and automations affecting the live app, not just development. This is the harshest paywall placement in the category: your customers hit it, not you.

findings.title: Official sources contradict each other on whether credit top-ups exist
findings.detail: docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Credits says top-ups are unavailable and users must "upgrade or adjust your plan" from the billing dashboard. base44.com/blog/how-much-does-base44-cost FAQ says the opposite: "You can top up your credits at any time without changing plans." A Product Hunt reviewer's experience matches the docs: "You can't buy more credits unless you upgrade to an expensive tier plan." Unresolved — do not cite either as fact.

findings.title: No refunds for AI mistakes, stated bluntly in docs
findings.detail: Docs: "Credits are non-refundable for tool behavior and AI mistakes. Each prompt still requires work" from the builder, even if results are unsatisfactory. Combined with widely reported retry loops ("The AI sometimes gets stuck on a feature, retries multiple times, and burns through credits without making progress"), this is the single most inflammatory policy in Base44's pricing.

findings.title: The editor now runs on Wix's corporate typeface — the clearest fingerprint of the acquisition
findings.detail: Extracted from app.base44.com/static/index-Dg-ALxaG.css: --font-body: "Wix Madefor Text", --font-titles: "Wix Madefor Display", --font-brand: "Dazzed", --font-mono: "Azeret Mono". The marketing site meanwhile runs Dazzed + Geist. So Base44 kept its startup brand font (Dazzed) for identity while swapping the workhorse UI type to Wix Madefor. Azeret Mono for code is an unusual, characterful choice over the default JetBrains/IBM Plex.

findings.title: "Premium" is a first-class semantic intent in the design system, coloured orange
findings.detail: The editor token system defines a full premium intent alongside accent and destructive: --sem-fill-premium-{primary,secondary,light,ghost}-{default,hover,active,disabled}, --sem-border-premium-*, and a dedicated --focus-ring-premium: 0 0 0 3px var(--orange-100). Light theme maps premium to orange-500 #ff773c; there is also --gradient-premium: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--orange-100) 0%, var(--purple-200) 50%, var(--purple-300) 100%). Upsell is systematised, consistent and pre-designed — every paywall control looks intentional rather than bolted on. Remixer should steal this exact idea.

findings.title: Two parallel neutral ramps — warm 'stone' and cool 'neutral' — and warmth is what reads as expensive
findings.detail: Editor CSS defines both: stone-50 #f8f6f4 → stone-100 #f1eeea → stone-300 #ddd8d2 → stone-700 #3d3c3a → stone-950 #1b1a19 (warm, used for surfaces and borders), and neutral-50 #fcfcfc → neutral-500 #5d5d5d → neutral-950 #0f0e0e (cool, used for disabled states and dark shimmer). The marketing site is entirely warm paper: #f9f7f4, #f1eeea, #eeeceb, #edebe7, #e2ded7 on ink #1e1e24 with warm grey text #6d6a67. Base44 never uses a pure cold grey for a surface. That warmth is the primary 'expensive' tell — most AI builders default to Tailwind slate/zinc and read as generic.

findings.title: Full 2026 colour and shape scales, measured
findings.detail: Brand orange ramp: orange-50 #fff5ef → orange-500 #ff773c → orange-950 #300f00 (marketing hero uses a hotter #ff6a00 / #f50). Accent blue: blue-500 #3b51e5 (also on the marketing site as #3950e6). AI purple: purple-500 #4d33de. Success green-500 #568f63. Destructive red-500 #df3336. Radius scale: none 0, xs 2, sm 4, md 6, lg 8, xl 12, 2xl 16, 3xl 24, 4xl 32, plus card 10px, pill 100px, full 9999px. Spacing is a strict 4px grid: 2/4/6/8/10/12/14/16/20/24/28/32/40/48/56/64/80/120. The marketing site restricts itself to just 6px and 8px radii — restraint reads as premium.

findings.title: Shadows are near-invisible warm-black at 5% alpha, plus a glass inset highlight
findings.detail: --shadow-xs: 0 1px 10px 0 #1c1a180d, 1px 0 2px -.7px #1c1a180d; --shadow-sm layers four such shadows; --shadow-md: 0 10px 20px 0 #0f0e0e0d; --shadow-lg: 0 20px 30px 0 #0f0e0e1a. Note the hex alpha: 0d = 5%, 1a = 10%. Shadows are tinted with warm black (#1c1a18 / #0f0e0e), never pure #000. There is also --shadow-glass-top: inset 0 1px 0 #ffffff80 — a 50%-white top inset that fakes a lit glass edge. Extremely restrained elevation plus one specular trick is exactly the recipe for 'expensive'.

findings.title: Three named themes and a namespaced, swappable design system
findings.detail: The editor CSS carries [data-theme=dark], [data-theme=white] and [data-theme=marketing] selectors, and 152 rules scoped to [data-ds=base44] — a design-system namespace implying more than one DS can be mounted (very likely a Wix DS alternative). Semantic tokens are defined three times over (light stone / dark stone / a purple-pink variant), so the system supports at least a third branded theme beyond light and dark. Base44's editor is therefore light-first with a real dark mode, unlike Remixer's dark-only #18181B shell.

findings.title: A five-step duration scale and three named easings, all tokenized
findings.detail: --duration-instant 80ms, --duration-fast .12s, --duration-base .18s, --duration-slow .26s, --duration-slower .36s. Easings: --ease-out cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) (easeOutExpo — fast start, long settle), --ease-in-out cubic-bezier(.65, 0, .35, 1), --ease-spring cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1) (overshoot for playful confirmations), --ease-linear. The marketing site's dominant curve is cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) (easeOutQuint, 23 occurrences). Nothing is left to the browser default — that discipline is why it feels engineered rather than assembled.

findings.title: Interaction state is tokenized as opacity, not as extra colours
findings.detail: --opacity-disabled .4, --opacity-muted .65, --opacity-hover .85, --opacity-press .75, --opacity-scrim .32. Plus a named z-index ladder: base 0, dropdown 1000, sticky 1020, banner 1030, overlay 1040, modal 1050, popover 1060, toast 1070, tooltip 1080. Focus rings are 3px with per-intent variants (default, destructive, accent, premium, standard-light, inverse). This is design-system maturity you rarely see in a two-year-old startup.

findings.title: Suggestion-led empty states rather than blank panels
findings.detail: Workflows' empty state offers "Create workflow" with "Add trigger" or "Or start from these suggestions". The component library empty state is "Explore component library" from the plus menu. Launchpad uses "Submit your app" with an "Improve with AI" assist and "Preview your Launchpad card". The pattern is consistent: never an empty box, always a prefilled path plus an AI assist.

findings.title: Raw stack-trace errors leak to non-technical users
findings.detail: Base44's own troubleshooting doc lists the errors users actually see: "Failed to load app: Error serializing to JSON: UnicodeEncodeError" (from unsupported characters in an app NAME), "Uncaught Error: Error in json schema: properties is required for object type", "'dict' object has no attribute 'lower'", and ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR on custom domains. A Python AttributeError surfacing to someone who was promised no-code is a serious craft failure and a direct opportunity for Remixer.

findings.title: Native iOS and Android apps exist — and are the only AI builder in this cohort shipping them
findings.detail: iOS: apps.apple.com/app/base44-build-with-ai/id6757432427. Android: play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.base44.android. Mobile-web building also works: base44.com → "Start Building" → sign up → prompt. Editing an existing app on mobile is entered via "Chat to Edit" on the app card. Lovable, Bolt, v0 and Remixer have no native builder app.

findings.title: Mobile is chat-only: visual edits, code, domains, security and templates are all cut
findings.detail: Docs: "Some features such as connecting a domain and managing your app's security are not available on mobile." Also unavailable: Visual Edits, RLS/security settings, code editing, API work, and app templates. Push notifications are "not currently supported". Users can add a built app to their home screen via share → "Add to Home Screen", where it "appears as a native icon and auto-updates". App-store submission (scan against store guidelines, AI fixes, generate IPA and AAB) requires Builder+.

findings.title: Real-time multiplayer on Canvas with named cursors and colored selections
findings.detail: Design Pack describes "Real-time multiplayer with named cursors, colored selections, sticky notes, drawings, and reference images" on the Canvas. A 2026 review reports smooth operation with 4–5 simultaneous editors and changes syncing in 2–3 seconds. Pricing page lists "Multi-user editing and collaboration" as included on EVERY plan, free included — an aggressive giveaway versus competitors who gate seats.

findings.title: Workspaces are the org primitive, with templates, skills and Enterprise publish permissions
findings.detail: Documented: About workspaces, managing workspace members, managing workspace apps, creating workspace templates, managing workspace skills, workspace connectors, workspace secrets. Credit usage is found at Workspace name → Settings → Credit usage. Changelog 31 May 2026 added "Publish permissions for workspaces" (Enterprise) — role-based publishing controls. Credits are pooled per workspace, so one member can drain the team.

findings.title: Template marketplace where creators can charge money
findings.detail: Gallery at base44.com/templates and app.base44.com/app-templates, browsable by category (e.g. Education, Operations) with hover "View details". Free templates use "Use Template", paid ones use "Purchase". Docs: "You can choose to offer your template for free or set a price for others to use it via the marketplace." Templates with reviews show an average rating. Using one copies the app into your workspace; "your original app stays the same". Workspace templates stay private.

findings.title: Launchpad turns publishing into a Product Hunt-style competitive loop
findings.detail: Sidebar → "Launchpad" → "Submit your app". Submission requires an automatic security-scan pass, up to 3 categories, a tagline and description, and either up to 5 screenshots (min 1280×720) or a demo video (MP4/WebM, max 50MB). Buttons: "Continue", "Improve with AI", "Preview your Launchpad card", "Submit", "My submissions", "Share". Signed-in users upvote each app once daily; top apps "earn credits and a featured spot" plus Wall of Fame. Shipped 13 May 2026; an Achievements points system followed 19 Jul 2026. Post-publish retention engine, not just a gallery.

findings.title: Security scan with severity grading and bulk AI fixes — free on all plans
findings.detail: Dashboard → Security → "Run Security Scan". Six issue categories: data permission gaps, exposed credentials, login verification gaps, package vulnerabilities, code vulnerabilities (Builder+), security headers. Severities Critical / High / Medium / Low. Actions: "Fix all issues", "Fix selected", "Fix with AI", "Apply Fixes", More Actions → "Ignore" (with a separate ignored section and "Restore"). Cards and Table views, filterable by type and severity. Explicit caveat: "The scan does not apply fixes automatically." Also integrates Wiz vulnerability scanning.

findings.title: Two disclosed 2025 vulnerabilities; the underlying permissive-default model was not re-architected
findings.detail: July 2025: Wiz disclosed an SSO bypass where supplying only the non-secret app_id to undocumented registration and email-verification endpoints created a verified account on private SSO-only apps. Imperva separately disclosed stored XSS in /apps-show/ endpoints and JWT leakage via URL fragments. Both patched within 24 hours of disclosure (9 July 2025). Third-party analysis holds that the default-permissive trust model between authenticated users remained architecturally unaddressed as of mid-2026 — which is why the security scanner exists at all.

findings.title: Analytics is a real product surface with two tabs and customizable cards
findings.detail: Dashboard → Analytics. Traffic Overview (default): "Total visits", "Unique visitors", "Visit duration", "Live visitors", plus cards for pages visited, visitor location, traffic source, device/OS, custom events. Sales Overview: "Total payments", "Transactions", "Customers", "Refunds", plus "Payments by day of week (avg)", "Top customers", "Recent transactions". Controls: a Customize icon (sliders-simple) to toggle and reorder cards via grip handles, a calendar for date ranges, a Filters button, and More Actions to change chart type per card. "+ Add Event" for custom events (Free capped at 3). Session recordings shipped 22 Jun 2026.

findings.title: SEO & GEO tab optimizes for ChatGPT and Gemini, not just Google
findings.detail: Shipped 26 Apr 2026: a dashboard page that runs a scan producing a visual score and a prioritized checklist, with AI able to apply the fixes, plus a "Meta tags" tab for custom page titles and descriptions and controls for indexing and structured data. Marketing copy: "Get found where people are actually looking – on Google, ChatGPT, Gemini and more. Run a scan, get a prioritized fix list, and let AI apply the fixes." Explicitly naming GEO (generative engine optimization) as a first-class surface is ahead of the category.

findings.title: Social content generation reads your app and writes posts in your voice
findings.detail: Marketing copy: "Base44 reads what you build, picks the right social platforms, and generates ready-to-post content – in your voice." Priced at 10 integration credits for a content plan and 1 credit per post improvement or image regeneration. Bundled under the section "Built-in marketing tools to grow after you ship" — Base44 is explicitly extending past launch into growth, which is where Wix's DNA shows.

findings.title: Speed work landed twice in the first week of August 2026
findings.detail: Changelog 1 Aug 2026: "Base44 loads noticeably faster" — reduced initial code load for editor startup. 6 Aug 2026: "Login and signup pages load faster" — responsive background images replacing a single large file. Publicly shipping and naming perf work in a user-facing changelog is a trust signal worth copying.

findings.title: Undocumented runtime ceilings surface only via support, per critic analysis
findings.detail: A critical third-party analysis reports: 150 operations/minute rate limit on all sub-Enterprise plans (per user, not per app; bulk imports/deletions trigger 429s), a 5,000-item cap per request where pages "silently display only first 5,000 records without error messaging", 3-minute automation execution cutoff, 5-minute backend-function limit, and max 50 backend functions per project. Also: no user-controlled DB backups, no direct SQL access, no database indexing control. These numbers are NOT in Base44's own docs — treat as unverified but directionally important.

findings.title: Wix ownership is now visible in the product, not just the footer
findings.detail: Concrete evidence of absorption: footer reads "© 2026 Wix.com Ltd."; the editor uses Wix Madefor Text/Display; "Base44 Payments powered by Wix" (Builder+, US/UK/EU/CH, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal US-only, 2–5 business day payouts, refunds and CSV settlement reports in-dashboard); domains purchasable through Wix as registrar with automatic DNS/SSL; a Wix connector for Superagents (Plugins → Connectors tab → Add Connector → search Wix → Wix App Installer, ~20 permission categories across store orders, inbox, bookings, blog, forms, contacts, payments, coupons); and changelog 31 Jul 2026 handling "Wix-billed workspaces". Business result: ~$100M ARR nine months after acquisition, ~2M users and a ~$150M ARR run rate by mid-2026.

findings.title: Superagents are a second product line with a different shell
findings.detail: Distinct from apps: workspace-wide AI agents built in "four steps: Define the goal. Connect your tools. Add files, memory, and context. Create automations." UI includes a chat with file upload and voice, a "+ New Automation" button, a Plugins tab (Connectors and Skills), and a Customize panel with General, Sharing & access, Personalization, Channels, Security and Developer sections. They reach users over WhatsApp, Telegram, iMessage, Slack and LINE. Personal by default; shareable as templates with selective inclusion of skills, memory and files. Guardrails via Connector Rules, e.g. "Only draft replies to Inbox messages, never send without my approval." Superagents has its own top-nav item on base44.com.

findings.title: Component library adds UI by injecting a prompt, not by dropping a component
findings.detail: Plus menu → "Explore component library". Categories: All, Commerce, Content, Navigation. Click a component to open a preview and "interact with it to try its different states before you add it", then "Add to chat" — which auto-switches to Build mode and sends a prompt that rebuilds the component as React code. Docs: "Base44 themes it to match your site, adapting its colors, fonts, and content to fit your app." One component per message, no additional credit cost, editable afterward. This keeps a single source of truth (the chat) while giving users a browsable catalogue — solving the drag-drop-vs-chat conflict most builders fumble.

findings.title: Workflows: chat-authored automation that renders as a visual diagram
findings.detail: Dashboard → Workflows, Builder+ only. Users describe the workflow in chat and Base44 generates "a visual diagram showing the trigger flowing through each step", updating as they refine. Vocabulary: Trigger, Steps, Conditions, Actions. Four trigger types: Scheduled (max once per 5 min), Entity (data create/update/delete), In-app agent (per new conversation), Connector (Gmail, Slack events). UI: "Create workflow", "Add trigger", "Or start from these suggestions", Active/Inactive toggle, More Actions → Deactivate/Activate/Rename/Archive/View archive, "Run now" with confirmation, plus "Run history" and a cross-workflow "Activity" tab showing success rate, average runtime and step-level status. Shipped 6 Jul 2026.

findings.title: Figma import is OAuth + public frame link, with named degradations
findings.detail: Requires a Figma Editor seat (View/Collaborator blocked), design files only (no FigJam/Slides), frame link shared as "Anyone with the link – Can view", one Figma account per workspace. New app: base44.com → "+" in prompt box → "Import from Figma" → "Connect to Figma" → OAuth → paste link → "Generate". Existing app: chat "+" → "Add page from Figma" → in Figma right-click → "Copy/Paste as" → "Copy link to selection" → paste → "Add page". Converts layout, structure, visual styling, Auto Layout hierarchy, spacing and alignment; custom fonts are replaced with defaults (only Google Fonts fully supported), image filters and variable-driven styles may drift. Naming the degradations up front is good expectation-setting.

standout_ux.name: "Premium" as a first-class semantic token intent
standout_ux.what_it_is: Base44's editor design system defines a full premium intent alongside accent and destructive: --sem-fill-premium-{primary,secondary,light,ghost} × {default,hover,active,disabled}, --sem-border-premium-*, a dedicated --focus-ring-premium, and --gradient-premium (orange-100 → purple-200 → purple-300). Every upsell control in the product draws from the same orange family.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Most products bolt paywalls on with one-off gold badges that look cheap and inconsistent. By treating monetization as a designed intent with full state coverage, every gate reads as an intentional part of the interface rather than a nag. Remixer should define a comparable intent so credit-limit chips, top-up buttons and plan gates share one visual grammar instead of accumulating ad-hoc treatments.

standout_ux.name: Manual visual edits cost zero credits
standout_ux.what_it_is: Docs explicitly exempt dragging, layout changes and direct text editing from credit consumption, alongside all database reads and writes. Only AI-mediated work is metered.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It removes the worst feeling in a metered builder — being charged to nudge padding. It also teaches an economically correct habit: use the AI for structure, your hands for polish. This is directly actionable for Remixer, where credits are currently consumed by generation, chat edits AND publishing. Charging for publish is the harshest possible placement, because it taxes the moment of success.

standout_ux.name: Cmd + . mode switching that works mid-typing
standout_ux.what_it_is: Cmd+. (macOS) / Ctrl+. cycles between Default, Discuss and Edit chat modes, and the docs specifically call out that it works "even while you're typing a prompt".
standout_ux.why_it_works: Intent frequently changes mid-sentence — you start asking for a change and realize you want to think first. Preserving the in-flight text while reclassifying it removes a retype and a decision. Tiny, cheap, and the kind of detail that makes a tool feel like it was built by people who use it.

standout_ux.name: Discuss mode priced at a flat 0.3 credits
standout_ux.what_it_is: A dedicated planning mode that cannot modify the app, billed at a fixed 0.3 credits per message versus 0.5–4 for execution. Plan mode at first-run is similarly "a fraction of a credit".
standout_ux.why_it_works: It prices thinking cheaply and building expensively, which is the correct incentive: users converge on a spec before burning an expensive build turn, and Base44 spends less compute on doomed generations. It also makes the credit model feel fair rather than extractive — the pricing itself is a UX affordance.

standout_ux.name: Testing Link — unpublished code plus sandboxed data in one shareable URL
standout_ux.what_it_is: Publish (top right) → "Testing Link" → "Copy testing link". Recipients see unpublished changes and interact only with test data. Copy: "the link does not change your live app or production records."
standout_ux.why_it_works: It solves review-before-launch without asking a non-technical user to understand environments. Composing 'unpublished build' and 'sandbox database' into a single link is the whole staging concept collapsed into one button — precisely the abstraction level this audience needs. Remixer has no equivalent.

standout_ux.name: Redesign prompts returning four options side by side
standout_ux.what_it_is: Typing "redesign this in different styles" produces four AI design directions presented simultaneously, scoped either to the whole project or a single section, with "The rest of the project stays exactly as it is." Marketing copy: "AI shows previews before it touches anything."
standout_ux.why_it_works: It converts an unbounded, anxiety-inducing request into a bounded choice, and it directly answers the #1 complaint about AI builders — that output is generic and unsteerable. Showing previews before mutation also removes the fear of losing work you liked, which is the single biggest source of distrust in generative editing.

standout_ux.name: Revert icon on every chat message + clock icon version history
standout_ux.what_it_is: Two undo surfaces: a clock icon in the AI chat opening full Version History, and a Revert icon attached to each individual chat message that restores the app to the state before that turn.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It maps undo onto the unit users actually think in — 'that thing I asked for' — rather than onto files or timestamps. Every message becomes a named checkpoint at zero cognitive cost. Docs even warn that asking the AI to undo in chat does nothing, which usefully teaches where the real control lives.

standout_ux.name: Test-data toggle living inside the preview as a database icon
standout_ux.what_it_is: A database icon in the preview labelled "Turn on test data", switchable mid-session, with copy: "Your published app always uses production data. Turning on testing mode only affects data in the dashboard and in preview."
standout_ux.why_it_works: It puts a consequential, scary switch exactly where the consequence is visible, and pairs it with one sentence that eliminates the only question the user has. This is the right pattern for any destructive-adjacent toggle: co-locate the control with its effect and state the blast radius in plain language.

standout_ux.name: Component library that injects a prompt instead of dropping a component
standout_ux.what_it_is: A browsable catalogue (All / Commerce / Content / Navigation) with interactive previews of component states; "Add to chat" auto-switches to Build mode and sends a prompt that rebuilds the component as themed React, matching the app's existing colors, fonts and content. No extra credit cost.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It resolves the classic conflict between a drag-drop library and a chat builder by keeping the chat as the single source of truth while still giving users something to browse. The output arrives already themed rather than as a foreign pasted block — so nothing ever looks bolted on.

standout_ux.name: Warm neutrals as the entire foundation
standout_ux.what_it_is: Base44 maintains two full neutral ramps and uses the warm one (stone-50 #f8f6f4 through stone-950 #1b1a19) for surfaces and borders, reserving the cool ramp for disabled states. Shadows are warm-tinted (#1c1a18) at 5% alpha, and the marketing site is entirely warm paper (#f9f7f4, #f1eeea, #e2ded7) on ink #1e1e24.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Cold Tailwind slate/zinc is the visual signature of AI-generated software; warmth immediately signals a human made deliberate choices. Combined with 5%-alpha elevation, tight 6–8px radii on marketing, and a --shadow-glass-top specular inset, this is the concrete recipe behind 'feels expensive'. It is fully copyable and costs nothing but discipline.

weaknesses.issue: Credits are burned by failed AI attempts, and there are no refunds — stated as policy
weaknesses.evidence: Base44's own docs: "Credits are non-refundable for tool behavior and AI mistakes. Each prompt still requires work" from the builder, even if results are unsatisfactory. Reviews describe the mechanism: "The AI sometimes gets stuck on a feature, retries multiple times, and burns through credits without making progress. Users routinely report blowing through monthly allowances faster than expected." (banani.co 2026)

weaknesses.issue: Free tier's 5-credits-per-DAY cap makes a single build session impossible
weaknesses.evidence: Docs confirm "5 credits daily (25/month)". Product Hunt review verbatim: "25 message credits a month, max 5 a day, and you'll burn through them just tweaking UI." Multiple 2026 reviews report hitting the free ceiling "within 1-2 days" or "within a few hours", and that 25 credits is "enough to evaluate the tool but not enough to ship a real MVP."

weaknesses.issue: Integration credits are a shared workspace pool consumed by END USERS, so exhaustion degrades the live production app
weaknesses.evidence: Docs confirm integration credits are consumed at runtime by app users (email, LLM calls, image generation, in-app agents at up to 40 credits/message) and that running out "cancels in-progress runs" for workflows; the Testing Agent shows "Test paused". Third-party production analysis reports mid-month feature pausing for emails, AI calls and automations that "affects the live production app, not just development."

weaknesses.issue: Design ceiling — the visual editor handles tweaks but not a real brand system
weaknesses.evidence: 2026 G2/review aggregation: "The visual editor is good for tweaks but not for fully custom design systems. If your brand requires a specific look (custom typography, intricate animations, unusual layouts), you'll hit walls. The styling system is constrained by what the AI templates support." A head-to-head found Base44's output "not that good-looking" versus Lovable's "more minimal and modern-looking" on the same prompt, and lists "Limited visual control over advanced design elements" as a core con.

weaknesses.issue: Complexity ceiling — reliability collapses beyond simple apps
weaknesses.evidence: The most frequently repeated 2026 complaint: "Reviews describe hitting points where the AI can't reliably resolve logic issues or structural changes. Users repeatedly report that Base44 works well for simple applications but breaks down as complexity increases." Product Hunt verbatim: "You hit walls fast. Anything beyond basic logic requires workarounds." A related critique: the agent "has no reliable working knowledge of its own platform" and will start building an approach its own APIs don't support.

weaknesses.issue: Support degraded materially after the Wix acquisition
weaknesses.evidence: Post-acquisition tracking cites G2 and Trustpilot reviews from late 2025 and 2026 with multi-week delays, including "Support ticket opened March 29 never received a single reply," against a pre-acquisition baseline of same-day responses from the founder. Response times are characterised as moving "from hours to days or weeks" for non-enterprise users.

weaknesses.issue: Prices rose and allowances shrank after acquisition, with no announcement
weaknesses.evidence: Product Hunt review verbatim: "Seems the price has gone up since acquired by Wix." Post-acquisition analysis reports price increases and reduced credit allowances discovered by users at billing time with no official announcement (Aug–Nov 2025), estimating 15–30% higher cost per equivalent app footprint versus mid-2025. Also verbatim: "You can't buy more credits unless you upgrade to an expensive tier plan."

weaknesses.issue: Vendor lock-in despite marketing claims of full portability
weaknesses.evidence: The pricing page states "Two-way GitHub sync exports the full source code to your own repo at any time. Nothing is locked to the platform." Users disagree — Product Hunt verbatim: "The exported code is tied to Base44's own infrastructure, so it won't actually run anywhere else." Review aggregation adds: "the integrated database means your data lives in Base44's managed Postgres. Migrating off the platform is genuinely hard — there's no clean 'export everything' button, and GitHub code export was still in beta on most plans as of mid-2026." GitHub integration is also gated at Pro ($80/mo).

weaknesses.issue: Raw stack-trace errors leak to an explicitly non-technical audience
weaknesses.evidence: Base44's own troubleshooting doc enumerates errors users encounter: "Failed to load app: Error serializing to JSON: UnicodeEncodeError" (triggered by unsupported characters in an app NAME), "Uncaught Error: Error in json schema: properties is required for object type", and "'dict' object has no attribute 'lower'" — a Python AttributeError surfaced to someone sold a no-code product.

weaknesses.issue: Branches share live production data, so the 'safe experiment' isn't safe
weaknesses.evidence: Docs state branches share "Live app data (all branches read/write identical records)" alongside connections, automations, app settings and publishing controls. Only the chat, preview and build are isolated. A non-technical user told they can "try changes safely" (changelog, 5 Aug 2026) can still destroy production records from a branch.

weaknesses.issue: Contradictory official messaging on whether you can buy more credits
weaknesses.evidence: docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Credits says top-ups are unavailable and users must "upgrade or adjust your plan"; base44.com/blog/how-much-does-base44-cost FAQ says "You can top up your credits at any time without changing plans." Two first-party sources, opposite answers, on the single most emotionally charged part of the product.

weaknesses.issue: No SLA at any tier, and a multi-hour outage in 2026 with no post-mortem
weaknesses.evidence: Post-acquisition analysis dates a platform-wide outage to 3 February 2026 lasting close to three hours, notes no published post-mortem, and states no SLA exists at any tier — making the absence of a contractual commitment "a tangible production risk" for apps carrying real users and payments.

weaknesses.issue: Security model is default-permissive by design, with two disclosed 2025 breaches
weaknesses.evidence: Wiz (July 2025) found that supplying only a non-secret app_id to undocumented registration and email-verification endpoints created a verified account on private, SSO-only enterprise apps. Imperva separately disclosed stored XSS on /apps-show/ endpoints and JWT leakage via URL fragments, where "Injected code had access to authentication tokens stored in browser local storage." Both patched in 24 hours, but third-party analysis holds the default-permissive trust model between authenticated users was still not architecturally fixed as of mid-2026.

weaknesses.issue: No way to review what will change before publishing
weaknesses.evidence: There is no diff or changed-pages summary in the documented publish menu, and "Provide an option to preview changes before publishing" is an open item on Base44's own feedback board, alongside "Revert to Published Version: Mark and Restore Last Published App Version from History" and "Restore Published Versions and Delete broken work" — three separate user-filed requests around the same gap.

weaknesses.issue: Placeholder and sample data ships into apps users demo to customers
weaknesses.evidence: 2026 review: "generated apps sometimes include placeholder data where real data should go. You'll demo your app to a customer and find 'Sample Item 1' or 'user@example.com' in unexpected places." A second independent review of a chore-scheduler build noted "sample data sometimes slipped in where real data should be."

weaknesses.issue: Base44 cannot provide a real mailbox — sending only
weaknesses.evidence: Docs state flatly: "Custom email domains are for sending only" and real business email "requires separate purchase or external provider configuration." Built-in email is further restricted to "people who are registered users of your app" with no external addresses and no attachments. Even after buying a domain through Wix inside the flow, there is no @yourdomain inbox.
