one_line_positioning: The world's largest registrar bolted a full-stack conversational app builder onto its domain funnel — "the ultimate vibe coding platform" that rides on GoDaddy's existing domain, hosting, email and payments stack, so the parts beginners get stuck on (data, auth, payments, DNS) never leave the chat.
summary:
GoDaddy Airo is not one product — it is a brand stretched across at least five surfaces, and untangling them is the single most important thing to understand about this competitor.

(1) **Airo** (godaddy.com/airo) is the agentic layer bundled free with every new domain purchase. It is domain-first by design: you type a business idea into an "AI Domain Search" prompt, review and *buy* a domain, and that purchase is what unlocks the rest — 12 AI logo options, a Microsoft 365 mailbox on your domain, suggested social handles, social/email campaign content, a free LLC filing, and a "Personalized One-Page Site, delivered instantly." Launched as Airo.ai on 13 Nov 2025 with six named agents (Airo Agent orchestrator, Airo App Builder, Compliance Agent, Domain Search & Registration Agent, Website Builder Agent, Logo Agent). (2) **Airo Plus** ($59.88/yr first year, renews $95.88/yr) adds a Marketing Consultant, Site Optimizer, Compliance (ToS/privacy generator), 3D logo and AI product photography. (3) **Websites + Marketing** is the legacy section-based editor; its AI chat variant, "GoDaddy AI Website Builder," is being **discontinued 31 July 2026**. (4) **Airo for WordPress** builds WP sites from chat inside the WP dashboard. (5) **Airo AI Builder** (airo-builder.godaddy.com, badged BETA) is the actual Lovable/Remixer competitor and the focus of this audit.

**Airo AI Builder end-to-end.** The entry screen is a dark violet-black canvas: "Airo" wordmark + purple BETA pill top-left, Discord and account icons top-right, and a headline in mixed white/violet — "Describe your idea. Get a live website in minutes." Under it a single trust row: "Get started for free · 50 AI credits/mo · No credit card required." The centrepiece is a fully-rounded **white pill prompt box sitting inside a large soft lavender bloom/glow** — the most expensive-looking element on the page — with placeholder "Design a landing page for my product launch…", a **microphone icon (voice input)** and a circular violet send button. Below: "Describe your own idea above, or try one of these:" and eight pill chips with trailing arrows — Boutique Store, Coffee Shop Website, Yoga Studio Portal, Product Launch, Freelancer Portfolio, **Rebuild my site**, Pressure Washing, Local Food Truck Landing Page. Prompt-first: you type, hit **Start building**, and only then hit the GoDaddy SSO wall (sign in or create account). No credit card.

The builder shell flips to a **light** theme. A left AI chat column carries the composer ("Ask Airo anything") with a **+ Add** button bottom-left (Attach a file / reference a file / take a screenshot), a mic, and a lavender send button; a **History** control sits directly under the chat window. The uppermost menu holds **Preview / Edit / Code / Menu / Media / Settings**, with **Refresh Preview**, a **Change device / Preview Desktop** device selector and **View & Share** (share link → Open in new tab) top-right, and **Publish** in the upper-right. Settings contains **Database** (edit tables, no SQL) and **Secrets** (API keys, tokens). Clicking an element in Edit mode raises a floating white segmented toolbar: **Replace | Modify | On click | (bookmark) | (AI sparkle)**. Everything in Edit, Code, Preview, Media, Menu and History is **free** — credits are burned only by agent actions, which is a deliberate and well-signposted economy.

Generation is a **planned task queue**: given a detailed brief, Airo posts a build plan of numbered next steps in chat that you can click to run or expand for an explanation. It runs semi-automatic post-build code validation and repairs its own errors without charging credits, and surfaces runtime failures with a one-click **"Ask Airo to Fix It"**. Free post-build one-click scans cover security (with line numbers), SEO and code quality.

**Money.** Free = 50 AI credits/mo, unlimited building, **zero publishing**. Starter $9.99/mo billed annually ($14.99 monthly), 150 credits, 1 published project. Professional $24.99/mo annual ($36.99 monthly), 300 credits, 10 published, Share access. Ultimate $99.99/mo annual ($149.99 monthly), 750 credits, 50 published. Credits do not roll over; purchased credits expire after 1 year. The paywall lands hard at exactly one place: the moment you want the thing to be real.

**Domain is the moat.** Connect a GoDaddy domain and Airo **updates DNS automatically** (Domain Connect — a standard GoDaddy invented and open-sourced, now used by ~50 companies including Microsoft, Google and Squarespace); external domains require manual records at your provider. Free sites live on yourbusinessname.godaddysites.com. Contact-form email is wired to the domain — but configuring it means pasting GoDaddy-authored prompts into chat rather than using a settings screen.

**The legacy drag is real**: four overlapping builders with one brand, credit balance buried on a separate Manage-my-plan page, no per-message diffs, day-granularity backups instead of true checkpoints, and a corporate mega-nav wrapping every help page. The interface feels expensive at the entry screen and administratively ordinary once inside.

findings.title: Prompt-first, auth wall lands AFTER the prompt is written
findings.detail: On airo-builder.godaddy.com the user types into the hero prompt pill and presses "Start building" BEFORE any account exists. GoDaddy's own walkthrough sequences it explicitly: "Enter the prompt that you've created and click the Start Building for Free button" → "Log in to your GoDaddy account, or create your account if you don't have one." The sunk-cost of a written prompt carries the user through SSO. No credit card at any point on the free tier.

findings.title: Zero pre-generation questionnaire in Airo AI Builder — one box, one shot
findings.detail: Unlike the Websites+Marketing Airo chatbot (which interrogates: business name → industry → description), Airo AI Builder asks nothing before generating. Help step 3 is the entire brief: "In the text box, describe your idea and then select Start building." All shaping happens after the first render, in chat. This is the Lovable/Remixer model, not the legacy wizard model.

findings.title: Eight starter chips including a competitive-migration hook, "Rebuild my site"
findings.detail: Below the prompt box, under "Describe your own idea above, or try one of these:", eight pill chips each with a trailing → arrow, centre-aligned across three ragged rows: Boutique Store, Coffee Shop Website, Yoga Studio Portal / Product Launch, Freelancer Portfolio, Rebuild my site, Pressure Washing / Local Food Truck Landing Page. "Rebuild my site" is a deliberate switcher hook; "Pressure Washing" is a deliberate signal that this is for actual small trades, not SaaS founders. Read directly from GoDaddy's own help-centre screenshot dated 20 April 2026.

findings.title: The OTHER GoDaddy funnel is domain-first and the domain purchase IS the paywall
findings.detail: godaddy.com/airo describes the flow as: (1) "Enter some info about your idea or business into our AI Domain Search prompt." (2) "Review domain options and purchase your domain. You'll also see business name suggestions." (3) "Publish your One-Page Site or wait to customize your full site, then continue to your dashboard." (4) logo, site, marketing. The site is the free gift; the domain registration is the transaction. This is the exact structural play DreamHost can copy — but GoDaddy monetises at step 2, before the user has seen anything built.

findings.title: Legacy Websites+Marketing path puts the signup wall FIRST, before any prompt
findings.detail: April 2026 hands-on: "Go to GoDaddy's website and click Start for Free. The signup page confirms no credit card is required" — three options (email, Facebook, Google) — and only then "GoDaddy redirects you directly into the Airo chatbot interface to begin building. You will not be dropped into a dashboard or asked to browse templates first." Two GoDaddy products, two opposite wall placements. The newer product moved the wall later; that direction of travel is the tell.

findings.title: Voice input is a first-class control inside the prompt box
findings.detail: A microphone glyph sits inside the hero prompt pill, immediately left of the circular send button — and again inside the in-builder chat composer next to the send button. Marketing confirms it: "all within the conversational AI chat interface (text or voice chat, it's up to you)." No AI builder in the Lovable/Bolt/v0 set ships voice as a peer of typing.

findings.title: GoDaddy publishes a 13-row "Avoid this / Do this" prompt table as official docs
findings.detail: The prompt best-practices article is a full comparison table by use case. E.g. Design change — Avoid: "Make it look better"; Do: "Redesign the homepage to feel more modern. Use a dark color scheme (#1a1a2e primary and #e94560 accent), larger hero image and replace the current text-heavy layout with short headlines and visual cards for each service." Rows cover e-commerce, booking apps, bug fixes, dashboards, blogs, SaaS, layout changes, API integration, create/connect database. Last row is telling: Preview isn't working — Avoid "I can't see my preview"; Do "Restart dev server".

findings.title: The docs frame prompting as a credit-conservation discipline, not a quality discipline
findings.detail: Framing verbatim: "Be specific about the problem: 'Fix my site' costs more credits than 'The checkout button isn't processing payments after I added the discount code field.'" and "One clear task per prompt." Teaching users to economise reads as honest, but it also permanently reminds them the meter is running — the opposite of the flow state a builder wants.

findings.title: Long prompts can hard-fail with a raw "Bad Request"
findings.detail: A 2026 hands-on reviewer pasting a full Product Requirements Document hit a "Bad Request" error and had to split the prompt into smaller sections. An unhandled HTTP-level error string surfaced to a non-technical audience at the single highest-intent moment in the funnel.

findings.title: Generation renders as a clickable, numbered build-plan queue in chat
findings.detail: Given a detailed brief, Airo "generates a prioritized task queue displayed in chat" — "a comprehensive build plan with a queue of suggested next steps" rather than doing everything at once. Users click an individual step to run it, or click its number to open a pop-up explanation. This is a materially different mental model from a streaming file tree: it's a to-do list the user co-drives, which also conveniently makes credit spend feel elective.

findings.title: Sibling product shows the best generation-feedback pattern in GoDaddy's portfolio: an elapsed-time work log
findings.detail: The Websites+Marketing AI builder's left panel shows a "Generating Site" card with an elapsed counter "Worked for 45s" and a live checklist filling in with check icons: "Understood your brand — Customers looking for freshly baked goods and artisanal treats in Tempe, AZ — welcoming, whimsical, delicious", "Mapped out 5 pages for your site", "Applied gelato color theme — Paired with bubblegum fonts.", then per-page section manifests ("Home — Hero, Menu, Gallery, Testimonials, and Contact"). Naming the colour theme and font pairing in plain language is the single most stealable detail here.

findings.title: Legacy path uses a narrated loading screen: "Matching styles to your industry…"
findings.detail: April 2026 hands-on on the W+M Airo path: "A loading screen appears with the status message 'Matching styles to your industry…' alongside an animated icon" and generation "completed in well under a minute." The reviewer's verdict is the design lesson: "Unlike builders that show nothing during generation, Airo's status messages give you a basic sense of what is happening. You will not see individual sections being built, but you are not staring at a blank progress bar either." A middling pattern that still beats a spinner.

findings.title: Six-item primary mode bar: Preview / Edit / Code / Menu / Media / Settings
findings.detail: GoDaddy's help doc enumerates the "uppermost menu" exactly: Preview (preview your app), Edit ("Select the desired part of your app and then use the toolbar to edit your selection"), Code ("Edit your app files"), Menu ("Upload and insert images, videos or documents"), Media ("Edit, upload and manage your app's visuals"), Settings. Note Menu and Media are two separate asset surfaces — an obvious information-architecture smell.

findings.title: Chat lives left; History sits directly beneath the chat window
findings.detail: Restore instructions are anchored spatially: "Under the AI chat window, select [History icon] History." Third-party walkthroughs place "the chat interface at the bottom left of your screen, where you can chat with Airo to modify code, add features or explain implementation." So: left column = chat, with History docked under it; centre/right = canvas. Same skeleton as Remixer, but with version history bolted to the chat rather than the toolbar.

findings.title: Settings is only two things: Database and Secrets
findings.detail: Verbatim: "(Optional) For more edits, select Settings: Database: Edit your database tables. Secrets: View and store sensitive information like API keys, access tokens, and other credentials." A two-item settings panel is a strong signal that everything else is intended to be reached by prompt — a genuine architectural bet, and a risky one.

findings.title: Chat composer is a white rounded card, plus-left / mic-and-send-right
findings.detail: From GoDaddy's own composer screenshot: white card with ~12px radius and hairline grey border, placeholder "Ask Airo anything" in mid-grey top-left, a square-outline "+" button at bottom-left, and at bottom-right a microphone glyph followed by a lavender (~#B4A5E8) rounded-square send button carrying an up-arrow ↑. Note the builder interior is LIGHT while the entry screen is DARK — two different visual worlds in one product.

findings.title: No documented keyboard shortcuts or command palette anywhere
findings.detail: Across the full get-started series, the credits FAQ, the backup/restore doc, the prompt guide and every 2026 hands-on review, not one keyboard shortcut, hotkey or command palette is mentioned. One review of the sibling W+M builder lists "lacks keyboard shortcuts" as an explicit limitation. For a product courting "Developers" as a named audience segment on its own pricing page, this is a conspicuous hole.

findings.title: Attachment menu is "+ Add" with three options, only one of which actually inserts content
findings.detail: Verbatim: "In the chat, select + Add" → "Select Attach a file and then select an image on your device" → then write a prompt like "Add this logo to my header" or "Use this photo in my About section." Critically: "When you select + Add you'll also see options to reference a file or take a screenshot. These help you provide context for your request but you can't add the screenshot or file to your website." A built-in screenshot-capture-as-context affordance is a genuinely good idea, and the disclaimer preempts the obvious misunderstanding.

findings.title: Agent self-heals its own code for free — errors are not billed
findings.detail: After most build steps the agent validates generated code and fixes errors without consuming credits. Reviewer observation: "Once in a while, it would miss something, but when I brought it to its attention, it fixed it without consuming any AI credits." Not charging users for the model's own mistakes is the single most important trust decision in any credit-metered builder, and GoDaddy got it right.

findings.title: Runtime failures surface a one-click "Ask Airo to Fix It" button
findings.detail: A separate error-catching mechanism surfaces failures encountered while testing the app and offers a literal "Ask Airo to Fix It" button for one-click resolution. Verbatim label. Converts a dead-end into a single tap — and note the imperative-with-object phrasing rather than a bare "Fix".

findings.title: No inline diffs, no file chips, no per-message revert — the transcript is prose plus a checklist
findings.detail: Nothing in GoDaddy's documentation or any 2026 hands-on describes a diff view, changed-file chips, per-message rollback, or a chat-vs-agent mode toggle. Recovery is exclusively via the separate History list and Backups. Compared with Lovable/Bolt/v0 (and Remixer), the editing model is the least legible part of the product: you can see what it did to the page, but not what it did to the code, unless you open Code yourself.

findings.title: Two-layer recovery: "History" for content versions, "Backups" for files+database
findings.detail: Layer 1 — History: "Under the AI chat window, select History" → "Select the version you want to go back to, and then select Restore this version" → "Once restored, select Publish to make it live." With: "You can preview each version before restoring to confirm it's the right one." Layer 2 — Backups: Backups → "Backups History" → "View Backup Date" → choose a date → choose files, databases, or both (default "Select All") → Restore → Publish. Warned: "Restoring from a backup will overwrite your current site with the backup version." The database-vs-files split at restore time is more sophisticated than most AI builders offer.

findings.title: Restoring does NOT go live — restore and publish are deliberately decoupled
findings.detail: Both restore paths end with the same instruction: "Once restored, select Publish to make it live." Rolling back is a staging-only act until the user separately confirms. This is the correct model and worth matching: it means a panicked restore can be previewed and reversed again before the public sees anything.

findings.title: Deletion is unrecoverable by the user: 30-day support-only window, "no undo button"
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Airo AI Builder retains app records for up to 30 days" and recovery requires phoning support with the domain, account email and approximate deletion time. Warning: "Recovery is not guaranteed." Tips section: "Don't delete your app unless you're certain: There is no undo button for deletion." A destructive action with no in-product safety net, papered over with a support phone number — a classic legacy-hosting reflex.

findings.title: Element toolbar is a floating white segmented pill: Replace | Modify | On click | bookmark | AI sparkle
findings.detail: Read directly from GoDaddy's screenshot: selecting an image in Edit mode raises a horizontal white pill (~full radius, subtle shadow, hairline dividers) with icon+label pairs — a picture glyph + "Replace", a pencil + "Modify", a sparkle-cursor + "On click", then two icon-only buttons (bookmark/save and a violet AI sparkle). "On click" as a first-class inline control — assigning link/interaction behaviour to any element without leaving the canvas — is unusually app-builder-ish for a click-to-edit toolbar.

findings.title: The docs actively steer users AWAY from chat toward direct manipulation
findings.detail: Verbatim tip: "Use Edit for simple edits: If you only need to change text, swap an image or adjust a color, use Edit instead of typing a prompt. It's free, and Airo AI Builder can't make unintended changes when you're editing directly. Save the AI chat for complex tasks." GoDaddy is telling users the AI is the riskier, costlier path. Honest, effective — and quietly an admission that the agent over-reaches.

findings.title: Image replacement is a documented zero-credit path with its own confirm label
findings.detail: "Replace an existing image (no AI credits used)": Edit → select image → toolbar "Replace" → pick from device → "Use this image". Then: "Your image updates right away. No prompt is needed and no credits are used." Contrast with the AI path (generate an image, or "Find a stock photo of a cozy coffee shop for my hero section") which does bill. Splitting the asset flow explicitly by cost is a good pattern and a good microcopy pattern.

findings.title: Code editing is free, in-product, and on every tier including Free
findings.detail: The credits FAQ lists among no-credit actions: "Make changes to your code or files using Code." The Code mode is a first-class peer of Preview and Edit in the top menu, not a hidden developer escape hatch — and it isn't paywalled. Code EXPORT is what's gated, not code ACCESS.

findings.title: Code export is a ZIP on paid plans; GitHub sync is explicitly "coming soon"
findings.detail: "Airo AI Builder lets you download your entire project as a ZIP file at any time: your full codebase, ready to edit, deploy elsewhere, or archive" — gated to paid plans. GoDaddy's own Base44 comparison scores it "Code download: Yes — ZIP export" vs Base44's "GitHub (Builder+ only)." The March 2026 launch post lists "two-way Git integration for version control synchronization" as upcoming. So: no live repo sync as of this audit.

findings.title: Device switching is a dropdown labelled "Preview Desktop" / "Change device", top-right
findings.detail: Two docs, two labels for the same control: the build article says "To preview your app for different devices, select Preview Desktop, and then select your desired device"; the publish article says "in the upper-right, select Change device and then choose a device." It's a current-state-labelled dropdown, not a segmented icon row — so the control announces what you're looking at rather than what you can switch to. Label inconsistency across the docs suggests it was renamed and not everything was updated.

findings.title: A manual "Refresh Preview" button exists — the preview is not reliably live
findings.detail: Step 6 verbatim: "(Optional) If you don't see your edits updating, select Refresh Preview." Shipping a user-facing refresh control is an admission that the preview desyncs, and the prompt guide reinforces it — the documented fix for "I can't see my preview" is to prompt "Restart dev server". A dev-server concept leaking into a no-code product's help text is exactly the seam Remixer should not have.

findings.title: Shareable preview URL exists pre-publish via "View & Share" / "Share link"
findings.detail: "To view or share your preview URL in a browser, select View & Share." The publish doc names the same affordance "Share link" and branches on state: "If this is your first time publishing, select Open in new tab. If you've published before, select Preview and then select Open in new tab." A state-aware share control that distinguishes draft-preview from live is a nice touch; the two names for it are not.

findings.title: Managed MySQL, 1GB+, editable through a no-SQL table UI in Settings
findings.detail: "Managed MySQL database with over 1 GB of capacity" with an "intuitive management interface within settings (no SQL required)" — reached at Settings → Database → "Edit your database tables." Capacity scales by plan. Airo can also connect an external database: a documented example prompt is "Connect my existing PostgreSQL database to the app. The database has a 'products' table with columns: id, name, description, price, category and image_url."

findings.title: Secrets manager is a named, first-class Settings section
findings.detail: Settings → Secrets: "View and store sensitive information like API keys, access tokens, and other credentials." The prompt guide teaches users to reference it inline: "I'll add my API key in the Secrets section in Airo AI Builder Settings." Giving credential storage its own top-level home (rather than burying it in an integrations page) is worth copying — it makes third-party integration feel safe to a non-technical user.

findings.title: Auth and payments are prompt-provisioned, not toggle-provisioned
findings.detail: "Airo AI Builder includes built-in database and backend capabilities, so your app can store data and manage users. You can also integrate third-party development tools and services like Stripe, analytics, or custom APIs just by asking Airo to connect them in your prompt." Documented example: "Add a payment page to my existing tutoring site. Students should be able to buy session packages (1 session for $50, 5 for $200, 10 for $350), pay via Stripe, and receive a receipt by email." GoDaddy Payments is also available as the native processor.

findings.title: Getty Images stock library is a headline differentiator vs AI-only imagery
findings.detail: GoDaddy's own comparison tables score "Professional images: Yes — Getty Images library" against both Base44 and Hostinger Horizons, each marked "AI-generated only." Licensed stock is reachable straight from chat ("Find a stock photo of a cozy coffee shop for my hero section") alongside AI generation and direct upload. For small-business sites this materially outperforms AI imagery, which reviewers repeatedly call "unpolished."

findings.title: Contact-form configuration is done by pasting GoDaddy-authored prompts — there is no settings UI
findings.detail: The official help article instructs users to paste literal strings into chat, e.g. "Can we update our contact form and use the new email skill to see if we need to make any changes? Let me know if you need any information from me." and "CC [your email address here] to my email contact form." and "Change my To email address to [your GoDaddy Conversations email here]." Note "email skill" — an internal skills architecture leaking into user-facing docs. This is prompt-as-config: brittle, non-discoverable, and it spends credits to change a setting.

findings.title: Publish is a bare upper-right button with no modal — deliberately anticlimactic
findings.detail: Verbatim: "When you're ready to make your changes live, in the upper-right, select Publish." No plan picker, no domain step, no confirmation dialog, no summary of what changed. Preview and device-check are optional steps BEFORE it. Publishing is also the terminal action of both restore flows. The paywall is enforced upstream at plan level ("If you experience issues publishing, check if you need to upgrade your plan") rather than in a modal — which means the free user hits a wall, not a pitch.

findings.title: Free-tier staging URL is a long autogenerated godaddysites.com subdomain
findings.detail: Published free sites land on the pattern site-nwujq32p6.godaddysites.com, or more generally yourbusinessname.godaddysites.com. Unlike Remixer's editable *.remixer.app subdomain with a pencil affordance, there's no documented rename control — and reviewers flag it directly: "This subdomain is not viable for a professional business presence and will not help your SEO."

findings.title: Downgrading to Free takes the site offline but preserves content, reversibly
findings.detail: Verbatim: "If you downgrade from a paid Airo AI Builder plan to the free plan, your published app or site is not immediately deleted. Instead, your site goes offline temporarily, but your content is preserved. If you return to Airo AI Builder and interact with your site or app again (or upgrade back to a paid plan), it can be restored." A soft-landing churn policy that leaves the door open — better than deletion, and cheap goodwill.

findings.title: GoDaddy-hosted domains get zero-touch DNS; external domains get manual records
findings.detail: Verbatim: "If your domain is using GoDaddy nameservers, Airo AI Builder automatically updates your DNS. If your domain is not using GoDaddy nameservers, you'll need to update DNS at your non-GoDaddy provider." The in-house flow is three clicks — Domain → Settings next to the domain → "Connect Domain" → "Yes, Continue." The external flow is: "External Domains" → enter domain → "Connect External Domain" → "Yes, Continue" → "Once your DNS records appear, update them at your non-GoDaddy provider" → come back and select "Connect Domain" again. This is precisely DreamHost's structural advantage — and note GoDaddy has NOT closed the external gap either.

findings.title: Buying a domain mid-build kicks the user out to the storefront and back
findings.detail: The documented "Buy a domain" path is: "Go to GoDaddy domains, search for a desired domain, and then purchase it" → return to the Airo apps page → select the app → Domain → Settings → Connect Domain → Yes, Continue. Even the world's largest registrar does NOT sell a domain inside the builder shell. That is a live, unclaimed opportunity — an in-flow search-buy-attach step with no context switch would beat GoDaddy at its own game.

findings.title: DNS state is communicated with a single "Active" status and a 48-hour expectation
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Connecting a domain requires a DNS change. It can take up to 48 hours for DNS changes to show up on the internet globally" and "Once propagated, your DNS will show an Active message to confirm the change." Setting the 48h expectation up-front and then having exactly one green terminal state is clean — but there is no documented intermediate state (pending / verifying / records-not-found), which is where users actually panic.

findings.title: GoDaddy invented and open-sourced Domain Connect — the standard DreamHost doesn't support
findings.detail: GoDaddy "developed a simple protocol and experience that allowed customers to setup applications without having to worry about the specifics of DNS records through a 'one click' configuration" and then "open sourced Domain Connect — allowing partners and competitors to benefit from it as well," now adopted by ~50 companies including Microsoft, Google, 1&1 and Squarespace. Relevant to us twice over: it is why GoDaddy's own attach flow is frictionless, and it is a ready-made spec DreamHost could implement to close the external-domain gap rather than inventing guided-DNS UI.

findings.title: Contact-form sender address is bound to the connected custom domain
findings.detail: To customise the From address the doc states the address "must be from the custom domain connected to your Airo AI Builder (for example, if your custom domain is coolexample.com, a usable address would be jane@coolexample.com)." Submissions can be CC'd, auto-replied to, or forwarded into GoDaddy Conversations. Domain → deliverable transactional email in one product is exactly the registrar-plus-host advantage; DreamHost can go further by provisioning a real mailbox rather than only a From address.

findings.title: Mailboxes are Microsoft 365 resold at $7.99/mo, or GoDaddy pro email at $2.99/user/mo — never free
findings.detail: Airo bundles "set up an email address" with a domain purchase, but the mailbox itself is a paid add-on: professional email listed at $2.99 per user/mo and Microsoft 365 at $7.99/mo. GoDaddy's own comparison table concedes it: "Professional email: Yes — Purchase required." GoDaddy resells someone else's mail platform; DreamHost operates its own, which is a real margin and integration advantage if mailboxes are bundled into the plan rather than upsold.

findings.title: Hosting/CDN/WAF are Cloudflare, not first-party
findings.detail: "Every site deployed through Airo AI Builder sits behind Cloudflare's Web Application Firewall and CDN, giving DDoS protection and filtering of malicious traffic without any configuration on your part, plus daily automatic backups with version restore." Marketing claims 99.9% uptime and "Global edge, fast caching, and sensible defaults." GoDaddy rents its edge; DreamHost's own SmartEdge (10 PoPs) is a first-party story GoDaddy structurally cannot tell.

findings.title: Exact 2026 Airo AI Builder ladder — annual vs monthly, with strikethrough anchoring
findings.detail: Pricing page carries an Annual/Monthly toggle and shows the monthly price struck through above the annual price. Free — "Best for simple apps and sites", 50 AI credits/mo, "Get building immediately", "No credit card required". Starter — "Best for increased editing power", 150 AI credits/mo, SAVE 33%, $14.99 → $9.99/mo billed annually, "Powerful core build features". Professional — "Most Popular", "Best for collaborative projects", 300 AI credits/mo, SAVE 32%, $36.99 → $24.99/mo, "Advanced build capabilities", bullets: "Create unlimited apps or sites / 10 published apps or sites / Connect a domain / Download your code / Share access". Ultimate — "Best for scaling fast", 750 AI credits/mo, SAVE 33%, $149.99 → $99.99/mo, "Full feature access".

findings.title: The paywall is publishing, and only publishing — building is unlimited forever
findings.detail: Free tier gives unlimited app creation and 50 credits/mo but "can only build, not publish." Published-project caps then ladder 1 / 10 / 50 across Starter / Professional / Ultimate. Compare Remixer's 30-day no-card trial: GoDaddy's free tier never expires but never ships; ours ships for 30 days then stops. GoDaddy's version is better for tyre-kickers and worse for anyone who wants a URL today — which is the moment we should own.

findings.title: Credits are billed for agent actions only — an explicit, published free-list
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Credits are used when you perform an action that uses Airo AI Builder's agents (for example, using the Airo AI Builder chat). Credits are not used for non-agent actions." The published no-charge list: Preview, Code, Edit (non-AI changes), uploading images/videos/files via Menu, Media management, and "Restore your app to a previous version using History." Publishing is NOT listed as a credit-consuming action anywhere — a direct contrast with Remixer, where publishing changes burns credits. That is a competitive vulnerability for us and the clearest single thing to reconsider.

findings.title: Credits expire monthly with no rollover; purchased credits expire after 1 year; spend order is expiry-first
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Purchased credits expire 1 year from the time of purchase" and "Airo Builder uses credits in order of expiration, starting with those expiring soonest. This includes both free and paid credits." Monthly free credits do not roll over. The expiry-first spend order is user-favourable and worth stating explicitly in our own credits UI — it removes the "am I burning the credits I paid for?" anxiety.

findings.title: Credit balance is exiled to a separate Manage-my-plan page — the loudest UX complaint
findings.detail: To see your balance: User menu → "Manage my plan" → under "Total AI Credit Usage". Reviewer verdict: "unlike other AI builders that display a running tally of your AI credit use somewhere on the dashboard, GoDaddy keeps Airo's tucked away on a separate screen" — called "a nuisance" requiring constant navigation. Remixer's persistent credits chip in the top toolbar is straightforwardly better and should stay.

findings.title: Real-world burn rate: 314 credits for one LMS across 39 prompts over 3 days
findings.detail: A 2026 reviewer built an LMS called EduFlow consuming 314 total credits (50 free + 264 on the Professional plan) across 39 prompts over three days — roughly 8 credits per prompt. Against that rate the Free tier's 50 credits buys about six prompts, Starter's 150 about nineteen, and Professional's 300 about thirty-eight. Another reviewer "maxed out as soon as our website was finished" on the free tier. Useful as a calibration benchmark against Remixer's 1,000 credits/mo.

findings.title: The surrounding GoDaddy price stack is where the resentment lives
findings.detail: Airo Plus $59.88/yr year one, renewing $95.88/yr. Airo All Access renews at $323.88 after a 14-day trial. Websites+Marketing: Basic $16.99/mo (intro ~$9.99 annual), Premium $26.99 (~$14.99), Commerce $29.99 (~$16.99), Commerce Plus $49.99 (~$29.99). Payment processing ~2.7% + $0.30. Reviewers converge on the same verdict: "GoDaddy advertises the first-year price and renews materially higher, so the number that matters for a budget is the two-year total, not the promo." Remixer's flat $9.99/$14.99 with no renewal cliff is a positioning weapon.

findings.title: The entry screen is the most expensive-feeling asset: dark violet-black, glowing prompt pill
findings.detail: Read from GoDaddy's own 20 April 2026 screenshot. Near-black violet ground (approx #150A1F–#1B0D2B) with a subtle radial lift behind the headline. "Airo" wordmark in white with a swash over the A, a violet BETA pill beside it. Headline at very large weight with tight tracking, alternating white and violet (approx #8B5CF6) per phrase: white "Describe", violet "your idea", white "Get a", violet "live website", white "in minutes." The prompt input is a pure-white full-radius pill floating inside a multi-layer lavender bloom — the glow, not the border, is what makes it read as premium. Everything else on the page is deliberately quiet so the halo carries the whole composition. Exact hex values are estimated from the image.

findings.title: Dark entry, light builder — the product changes visual identity at the door
findings.detail: The dark violet entry screen gives way to a light interior: white chat composer, white floating element toolbars, light canvas. Remixer is dark throughout (#18181B shell). GoDaddy's split means the moment of highest emotional charge (the blank prompt) gets the cinematic treatment and the working surface gets the utilitarian one. It's defensible, but it costs them continuity — the product you fell for is not the product you use.

findings.title: Type is GoDaddy's proprietary GD Sherpa / GD Sage pairing
findings.detail: GoDaddy commissioned an in-house family: GD Sherpa, "a crisp, sans typeface" modified in-house that "allows for a tighter presentation of product UX to help users focus on task completion", paired with GD Sage, "a sharp and refined editorial-style serif headline typeface." The Airo headline's tight tracking and slightly humanist geometry is consistent with GD Sherpa. Owning the typeface is a large part of why the marketing surfaces read as expensive rather than generic — worth weighing against Remixer's Inter/Gilroy/Proxima stack.

findings.title: Violet is the AI signal across the whole portfolio, and it is used sparingly
findings.detail: Violet/lavender appears only on: the BETA pill, the alternating headline words, the prompt-box glow, the circular send button, the chat send button, the AI sparkle in the element toolbar, and the avatar chip in the sibling builder. Every non-AI control is neutral (white, grey, black). The discipline is the point — a single hue reserved exclusively for AI affordance. Directly parallel to Remixer's indigo/purple = AI brand rule, and confirmation that rule is correct.

findings.title: Radii are bimodal: full-pill for AI/entry surfaces, ~8–12px for working chrome
findings.detail: Full-radius: hero prompt input, suggestion chips, BETA badge, element toolbar, the circular send button on the entry screen. Moderate radius (~12px): chat composer card, preview canvas corners, section cards. Squared-off with small radius: the send button inside the builder (rounded-square, not circle). The shift from pill to rounded-rect maps exactly onto the shift from marketing-mode to work-mode — an intentional, legible system.

findings.title: Marketing page voice is unusually loose for a legacy incumbent
findings.detail: Section headings include "Nail the vibe in 3 easy steps", "Developer-ready. Newbie-friendly.", "Affordable plans, astounding results", "Skip the blank canvas", "Simple as t-y-p-i-n-g.", "Maximum speed, minimal effort.", "Customize to your heart's content.", "A portfolio that's all you, and only you.", and self-describes as "the ultimate vibe coding platform." The godaddy.com/airo page goes further: "A(bsolutely) I(ncredible)", "Move at the speed of heck yeah", "Customize your heart out", "Your LLC. Headache-free." Audience-segmented rails (Small Businesses / Developers / Creatives) each get their own tone.

findings.title: Generation motion is a named animated icon plus rotating status text, not a progress bar
findings.detail: On the W+M Airo path: "A loading screen appears with the status message 'Matching styles to your industry…' alongside an animated icon." In the AI Builder proper, motion is carried by the prompt-box glow (a static bloom in the screenshot, but composed in layers consistent with a breathing/pulse treatment) and by checklist items resolving to check icons one at a time. No documented easing values or spring specs are publicly available.

findings.title: Out-of-credits state names the reset time and offers upgrade inline
findings.detail: Verbatim: "When you run out of credits, a message will appear that'll include the time your free monthly limit resets and the option to upgrade to add more credits." Purchase paths: Manage My Plan → "Buy AI Credits" for one-time, or "Upgrade" for a higher monthly limit. Giving a concrete reset timestamp rather than a vague "next cycle" is the right call — it converts a dead end into a wait-or-pay choice.

findings.title: Backups explicitly disclaim what they do NOT cover — including AI-generated logos
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Keep your own copies of images and files: Only the images and files you upload will be retained in Backups. Airo AI Builder does not permanently store images or logos between sessions unless you upload them yourself." So AI-generated imagery is ephemeral and can be lost on restore. Stating the limitation plainly is good practice; the underlying behaviour is a genuine data-loss trap.

findings.title: One GoDaddy mobile app for management; advanced editing bounces to mobile browser
findings.detail: "GoDaddy has a single app on iOS and Android that lets you edit your website, manage bookings, track store orders, and view analytics from your phone. Basic text and image edits work from the app, while more advanced editing typically redirects to the mobile browser rather than staying within the native app." No evidence of a dedicated Airo AI Builder mobile app; conversational building is not documented as a mobile-native experience.

findings.title: Mobile is framed as an output property, not an authoring environment
findings.detail: "Airo AI Builder focuses on web applications, but you can build mobile-responsive web apps that work great on any device. All AIRO-generated websites are mobile-friendly by default." Combined with the desktop-only toolbar/preview model, the builder itself is a desktop product. Given the trade-business audience the starter chips target (Pressure Washing, Food Truck), that is a mismatch — and an opening.

findings.title: "Share access" is a Professional-tier ($24.99/mo) gate with no documented role model
findings.detail: "Share access" appears as a Professional bullet and Professional is positioned "Best for collaborative projects." No help article documents inviting a collaborator, permission levels, seat counts, or comment/review workflows. Collaboration exists as a price-tier bullet more than as a designed feature — a soft spot if Remixer wants to court small agencies.

findings.title: A Discord icon sits in the top-right of the builder entry screen — community as primary nav
findings.detail: The entry screen's top-right holds exactly two icons: Discord and account. GoDaddy links discord.com/invite/EfybfxAXg8 as the "active Discord community." A legacy incumbent putting Discord adjacent to the account menu — above any help or docs link — is a deliberate borrow of indie-AI-tool culture, and cheap credibility with the developer segment they name on the pricing page.

findings.title: Showcase is a curated blog gallery of seven real customer builds, not a remixable template gallery
findings.detail: "7 examples of real websites built with Airo AI Builder" covers Hot Fling (chili oil e-commerce, payment processor), Jadilah (multi-currency store), Space Alchemist (organizing portfolio + blog), Dar Gym (built in "minutes"), Futrfund (app landing with pricing), The Daily Brew (café), Dino Letter Quest (educational app landing). No fork/remix affordance, no published prompts, no community submission. Inspiration marketing, not a growth loop.

findings.title: Free one-click security, SEO and code-quality scans with line-number precision
findings.detail: Post-build one-click scans are free: a security scanner that pinpoints vulnerabilities by line number, an SEO analysis, and a code-quality check — reached via the "+" menu's "Security" option, then "Run Analysis", then "Ask Airo to Fix" to repair (scan free, repairs billed). Reviewers single these out as notably thorough. Scan-free/fix-paid is a well-judged monetisation seam: it surfaces value before charging.

findings.title: Trust signalling leans on Trustpilot volume and celebrity press, not on compliance
findings.detail: The AI Builder page embeds "Our customers say / Excellent / 4.4 out of 5 stars based on 139,274 reviews" with the Trustpilot logo, and godaddy.com/airo carries TechRadar, Rolling Stone ("Using GoDaddy Airo is tantamount to, in my world, having the perfect agent." — Walton Goggins) and an Emmy-nominated TV placement. Meanwhile reviewers note the absence of SOC 2, HIPAA and audit logs. Consumer trust theatre, not enterprise trust.

findings.title: Analytics is built in but paid-tier only; a QA agent audits the build
findings.detail: "Built-in analytics dashboard tracking page views and visits" lives in the settings dashboard and is gated to paid plans. Alongside it an "automated QA agent" that "checks technical performance to user experience quality." The post-launch checklist in GoDaddy's guide is: monitor site analytics, update content regularly, continue scaling functionality — a thin post-launch story compared with the pre-launch one.

findings.title: SEO/AEO check is invoked by prompt, and AEO is called out by name
findings.detail: GoDaddy's step-by-step tells users to ask the builder to "run an SEO/AEO check on your website and report on any issues." Answer Engine Optimization is named as a first-class concern alongside SEO in 2026 marketing ("Full-stack ... also includes SEO, AEO, and analytics"). Naming AEO explicitly is ahead of most competitors' copy and an easy positioning borrow.

findings.title: Four overlapping GoDaddy builders — GoDaddy publishes a help article just to disambiguate them
findings.detail: "Which GoDaddy website builder do I have?" tabulates: Classic Websites+Marketing Website Builder (template + manual), GoDaddy AI Website Builder ("being discontinued" 31 July 2026, customers migrated to the classic builder), Airo AI Builder (standalone, free + paid, "Conversational prompts, manual editing and code-level editing", builds "Apps and websites"), and Airo for WordPress (Managed WordPress, chat from a WP sidebar). GoDaddy even warns: "Although Airo AI Builder and Airo for WordPress share the Airo brand, they're separate products that build different things." Needing a disambiguation article is the diagnosis.

findings.title: Airo.ai launched 13 Nov 2025 as six named agents under an orchestrator
findings.detail: Press release: Airo Agent (orchestrates end-to-end requests), Airo App Builder, Compliance Agent (privacy policies + terms of service), Domain Search and Registration Agent, Website Builder Agent, Logo Agent. Executive framing from CBO Gourav Pani: "Small business owners do not want to master a tech stack; they want outcomes that help them start and grow." Exposing named agents rather than one undifferentiated assistant is a legible way to communicate scope — and it maps cleanly onto the "email skill" language leaking into the help docs.

findings.title: GoDaddy shipped domain search into Claude via MCP on 14 Feb 2026
findings.detail: Users can check live domain availability and pricing inside a Claude conversation and receive a purchase link, without leaving the chat. Framing: "You come up with a great name… then have to switch tabs to check if the domain is available" and "Naming your business shouldn't feel like an interruption. It should feel like inspiration." Roadmap: authenticated domain management, bulk availability checks, contextual product recommendations, and expansion to OpenAI, Google and Perplexity. The registrar is moving its top-of-funnel INTO other people's AI assistants — a distribution move DreamHost should treat as urgent.

findings.title: Airo Plus and Airo All Access exist as separate AI upsell SKUs on top of everything
findings.detail: Airo Plus ($59.88/yr year one, renews $95.88/yr) bundles: Marketing Consultant ("Meet your marketing department" — campaigns, plans, SEO optimization), Site Optimizer ("all-in-one AI optimization tool for MWP sites" for traffic, Google rankings, accessibility), Compliance ("create terms of service and a privacy policy"), a customizable 3D logo, and AI product photography ("create pro-level photos without an expensive shoot"). Airo All Access is a 14-day trial bundle renewing at $323.88. Three AI SKUs stacked on four builders is the upsell density trap in its purest form.

standout_ux.name: The glowing prompt pill
standout_ux.what_it_is: A pure-white, full-radius input floating inside a large multi-layer lavender bloom on a near-black violet ground, with a mic and a circular violet send button inside it. Everything else on the entry screen is deliberately muted.
standout_ux.why_it_works: The halo — not a border, not a gradient fill — is what makes the page read as expensive. It puts light behind the one thing the user must touch, so the composition has exactly one focal point and zero competing chrome. It is cheap to build (layered box-shadows) and disproportionately effective.

standout_ux.name: Zero-credit action list, published as documentation
standout_ux.what_it_is: GoDaddy publishes an explicit list of what never costs credits: Preview, Code, Edit (non-AI changes), uploading via Menu, Media management, and restoring a version via History. Publishing is not listed as billable at all.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Metered products create a background hum of anxiety that suppresses exploration. Naming the free surface converts the meter from a threat into a boundary, and it lets users work confidently in direct-manipulation mode. Directly relevant to us: Remixer bills credits on publishing, GoDaddy appears not to.

standout_ux.name: "Use Edit instead of typing a prompt"
standout_ux.what_it_is: Official docs steer users away from the AI for simple changes: "It's free, and Airo AI Builder can't make unintended changes when you're editing directly. Save the AI chat for complex tasks."
standout_ux.why_it_works: It sets an honest expectation about agent blast radius, positions direct manipulation as the precision tool and chat as the power tool, and reduces both credit burn and restore events. Counter-intuitively, telling people to use your AI less increases trust in it.

standout_ux.name: Restore never auto-publishes
standout_ux.what_it_is: Both the History restore and the Backups restore end with the same instruction: "Once restored, select Publish to make it live." Every version can be previewed before restoring.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Rollback is done in panic. Decoupling restore from go-live means a wrong restore is recoverable and the public never sees the thrash. It also keeps one mental model — nothing is live until you press Publish — consistent across editing and recovery.

standout_ux.name: Site Summary as a pre-generation brief you can amend
standout_ux.what_it_is: On the Websites+Marketing Airo path, before generating, a right-hand panel shows Site name, full business description, Industry, Site style (Organic / Modern / Bold) and Writing style (Neutral / Professional / Casual), with three buttons to adjust each and a "Create Preview" button top-right of the panel.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It externalises the AI's interpretation of the brief and makes creative direction editable before any compute is spent. As the reviewer put it, you are shaping the direction "before it commits to a design" — which is far cheaper than fixing a wrong render, and it makes the AI feel like it listened.

standout_ux.name: Named colour theme and font pairing in the build log
standout_ux.what_it_is: The generation checklist reports decisions in plain language: "Applied gelato color theme — Paired with bubblegum fonts," plus per-page section manifests like "Home — Hero, Menu, Gallery, Testimonials, and Contact," all under an elapsed timer ("Worked for 45s").
standout_ux.why_it_works: It turns waiting into reading, and it gives non-designers vocabulary for what they got — so their next instruction is "warmer than gelato" instead of "I don't like it." The elapsed counter also reframes latency as effort rather than lag.

standout_ux.name: "On click" in the inline element toolbar
standout_ux.what_it_is: The floating white toolbar on a selected element reads Replace | Modify | On click | bookmark | AI sparkle — assigning link or interaction behaviour directly on the canvas.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Most click-to-edit toolbars only cover appearance. Exposing behaviour at the same level as content is what makes this an app builder rather than a page editor, and it removes a whole class of prompts ("make the logo link to the homepage") from the credit-metered chat.

standout_ux.name: Screenshot-as-context in the attachment menu
standout_ux.what_it_is: The chat "+ Add" menu offers Attach a file, reference a file, and take a screenshot — with the explicit caveat that screenshots and referenced files inform the request but are not inserted into the site.
standout_ux.why_it_works: A built-in capture tool means the user can point at the problem instead of describing it, which is the highest-leverage input any visual agent can receive. The caveat is equally good: it kills the obvious misinterpretation before support has to.

standout_ux.name: Prompt-first, wall-second
standout_ux.what_it_is: The user writes their idea into the hero box and presses "Start building" before any account exists; SSO appears only after the prompt is committed.
standout_ux.why_it_works: The prompt is the emotional investment. Collecting it first means the signup screen interrupts a story already in motion rather than a stranger at the door. GoDaddy's own legacy product does the opposite, which makes the direction of travel unambiguous.

standout_ux.name: Discord in the top-right, beside the account menu
standout_ux.what_it_is: The builder entry screen's chrome is exactly two icons: Discord and account.
standout_ux.why_it_works: For a 25-year-old registrar, putting community above docs and help is a strong cultural signal to the developer and indie-builder audience it is trying to win — and community answers scale support for a product whose interface is largely undocumented prompts.

weaknesses.issue: Four overlapping builders under one brand, one of them being killed mid-2026
weaknesses.evidence: GoDaddy maintains a help article titled "Which GoDaddy website builder do I have?" comparing Classic Websites+Marketing, GoDaddy AI Website Builder, Airo AI Builder and Airo for WordPress. It states GoDaddy AI Website Builder "is being discontinued on July 31, 2026, and customers are being moved to the Websites + Marketing classic Website Builder," and warns that "Although Airo AI Builder and Airo for WordPress share the Airo brand, they're separate products that build different things." Third-party 2026 reviews routinely conflate them — top10.com's "vibe-coding" review of Airo AI Builder actually lists Websites+Marketing tiers ($9.99–$49.99) and complains it "can't add custom code," which is false for Airo AI Builder.

weaknesses.issue: Credit balance is hidden on a separate page, forcing constant navigation
weaknesses.evidence: Checking your balance requires User menu → "Manage my plan" → "Total AI Credit Usage". A 2026 hands-on reviewer: "unlike other AI builders that display a running tally of your AI credit use somewhere on the dashboard, GoDaddy keeps Airo's tucked away on a separate screen" — described as "a nuisance" and listed as a top complaint alongside the free tier's inability to publish.

weaknesses.issue: Free tier's 50 credits are exhausted by a single project
weaknesses.evidence: "Users on the Free plan only get 50 AI credits per month; these will likely be used up quickly on a single website project." A reviewer testing a cosmetics store "maxed out as soon as our website was finished" and could not send further prompts. Measured burn on a real build was ~8 credits per prompt (314 credits / 39 prompts), which puts the free tier at roughly six prompts.

weaknesses.issue: Configuration by copy-pasted prompt instead of settings UI
weaknesses.evidence: The official contact-form article instructs users to paste literal strings into chat: "Can we update our contact form and use the new email skill to see if we need to make any changes? Let me know if you need any information from me.", "CC [your email address here] to my email contact form.", "Change my To email address to [your GoDaddy Conversations email here]." Non-discoverable, brittle, and it spends metered credits to change a setting.

weaknesses.issue: Preview desyncs, and the documented fix leaks dev-server internals
weaknesses.evidence: The build article ships a manual control: "(Optional) If you don't see your edits updating, select Refresh Preview." The prompt best-practices table lists "Preview isn't working" with recommended prompt "Restart dev server" — a developer concept surfaced to a no-code audience as the official remedy.

weaknesses.issue: No inline diffs, file chips or per-message rollback
weaknesses.evidence: Across the entire get-started series, credits FAQ, backup/restore doc and every 2026 hands-on, no diff view, changed-file indicator, per-message revert or chat-vs-agent mode is described. Recovery is only via the separate History list and day-granularity Backups. Users cannot see what the agent changed in code without manually opening Code themselves.

weaknesses.issue: App deletion is irreversible in-product with a support-only 30-day window
weaknesses.evidence: Verbatim: "There is no undo button for deletion. Recovery requires contacting support, and is not guaranteed." GoDaddy retains records "up to 30 days" and asks users to supply the domain, account email and approximate deletion time by phone. "Recovery is not guaranteed — it depends on how recently the app was deleted and whether the data is still within the retention timeframe."

weaknesses.issue: AI-generated images and logos are not retained between sessions or in backups
weaknesses.evidence: Verbatim backup limitation: "Only the images and files you upload will be retained in Backups. Airo AI Builder does not permanently store images or logos between sessions unless you upload them yourself." Users are told to keep their own copies of anything the AI generated.

weaknesses.issue: Generic AI copy and unpolished AI imagery
weaknesses.evidence: Multiple independent 2026 reviews: business.com found "AI-generated copy described as 'very generic'" and imagery "unpolished, requiring human refinement"; aitoolspolice calls the output "template-grade" — "a template selector with AI prompts, not true generative design." The WP Minute found the sibling Airo Site Designer "asked for our preferred colors, then ignored our answer when building the preview."

weaknesses.issue: Renewal price cliff is the single most-cited GoDaddy complaint
weaknesses.evidence: "GoDaddy advertises the first-year price and renews materially higher, so the number that matters for a budget is the two-year total, not the promo." Airo Plus $59.88 → $95.88/yr. Airo All Access renews at $323.88 after a 14-day trial. Commerce tier "widely reported renewing from around $11.99... to roughly $20.99 a month or more." Reddit threads on r/smallbusiness and r/web_hosting cite renewal sticker-shock of roughly $200–275/yr after year one.

weaknesses.issue: Aggressive upselling and cluttered cross-sell surfaces
weaknesses.evidence: "The interface can sometimes feel cluttered with upsells, promotions, and add-on suggestions during normal use." A heavily-upvoted Reddit thread claimed an agent added $900+ of products to an account without consent. Even help-centre articles render behind the full commercial mega-nav (Domains / Websites / Email / Hosting / Marketing / Commerce / SSL / Pricing / Deals), so documentation is wrapped in storefront.

weaknesses.issue: Support experience contradicts the "award-winning human support" claim
weaknesses.evidence: GoDaddy's own comparison tables score itself "Phone + chat (award-winning support)" against competitors' "chat only." Against that: one customer described a chat loop that repeatedly asked if they were "still there" and pushed wait time from 6 to 8 to 11 minutes, which they read as running out the refund window. Another review cites "being left on the phone hold for hours, not talking to an actual person, and limited assistance" — though that source (hoot.host) is a competitor marketing an alternative and should be discounted accordingly.

weaknesses.issue: Geographic restriction on the AI features
weaknesses.evidence: Multiple 2026 reviews report "GoDaddy Airo is currently only available in the US and Canada" and that "everyone else gets the older legacy GoDaddy Website Builder, not the Airo AI features." GoDaddy marketing simultaneously claims 150+ countries with multi-language support, and the AI Builder page says "Type your idea in any language." This contradiction is unresolved and should be treated as unverified in either direction.

weaknesses.issue: No keyboard shortcuts or command palette despite courting developers
weaknesses.evidence: The pricing page dedicates an entire audience rail to "Developers" ("Customize to your heart's content. Edit code, copy, visuals, and style yourself"). No shortcut, hotkey or command palette appears anywhere in GoDaddy's documentation or in any 2026 hands-on; a review of the sibling builder lists "lacks keyboard shortcuts" as an explicit limitation.

weaknesses.issue: Buying a domain requires leaving the builder — even at the world's largest registrar
weaknesses.evidence: The documented "Buy a domain" flow is: "Go to GoDaddy domains, search for a desired domain, and then purchase it," then return to the Airo apps page, select the app, select Domain, select Settings, Connect Domain, Yes Continue. The registrar advantage is real but the in-flow purchase experience is unbuilt — the highest-value unclaimed ground in this category.

pricing_2026:
AIRO AI BUILDER (airo-builder.godaddy.com) — verified from GoDaddy's own pricing section, Aug 2026. Pricing page has an Annual/Monthly toggle and shows the monthly price struck through above the annual price.
• Free — "Best for simple apps and sites". 50 AI credits/mo. "Get building immediately". "No credit card required". Unlimited building, ZERO publishing.
• Starter — "Best for increased editing power". 150 AI credits/mo. SAVE 33%. $14.99 struck through → $9.99/mo billed annually. "Powerful core build features". 1 published app or site.
• Professional — "Most Popular", "Best for collaborative projects". 300 AI credits/mo. SAVE 32%. $36.99 → $24.99/mo billed annually. "Advanced build capabilities". Bullets verbatim: "Create unlimited apps or sites / 10 published apps or sites / Connect a domain / Download your code / Share access".
• Ultimate — "Best for scaling fast". 750 AI credits/mo. SAVE 33%. $149.99 → $99.99/mo billed annually. "Full feature access". 50 published apps or sites.
(The 1 / 10 / 50 published-project ladder is corroborated by two independent 2026 reviews; the Ultimate credit figure of 750 is corroborated but not read directly off the GoDaddy tier card — medium confidence on 750 specifically.)

CREDIT MECHANICS — verbatim from GoDaddy help:
• "Credits are used when you perform an action that uses Airo AI Builder's agents (for example, using the Airo AI Builder chat). Credits are not used for non-agent actions."
• Free (no-credit) actions, published list: Preview; Code (editing code/files); Edit (non-AI changes); uploading images/videos/files via Menu; Media management; "Restore your app to a previous version using History."
• Publishing is NOT listed as a credit-consuming action anywhere in GoDaddy's documentation. (Absence of evidence, not explicit confirmation — but notable given Remixer bills credits on publish.)
• Monthly free credits do NOT roll over. "Purchased credits expire 1 year from the time of purchase." Spend order: "Airo Builder uses credits in order of expiration, starting with those expiring soonest. This includes both free and paid credits."
• Top-ups: Manage My Plan → "Buy AI Credits" (one-time) or "Upgrade" (higher monthly limit). EXACT TOP-UP PACK SIZES AND PRICES: UNVERIFIED — GoDaddy does not publish them and the purchase screen is behind auth.
• Measured burn rate (one reviewer, Professional plan): 314 credits across 39 prompts ≈ 8 credits/prompt.
• Credits are account-scoped: "Credits can only be used for Airo AI Builder in the GoDaddy account they were purchased from."
• Downgrade behaviour: takes effect at the start of the next billing period; site goes offline but content is preserved and restorable.

TRIAL: No time-boxed trial on Airo AI Builder — the Free tier is perpetual, no credit card, but cannot publish. (Distinct from Websites+Marketing, which runs a 7-day premium trial that silently downgrades: "After those 7 days, the account automatically downgrades to the free tier without a proactive warning.")

SURROUNDING GODADDY AI SKUs:
• Airo (core) — free with any new domain purchase. Includes 12 AI logo options, One-Page Site, social handle suggestions, campaign content, free LLC setup.
• Airo Plus — $59.88/yr first year, renews $95.88/yr (≈$4.99/mo → ≈$7.99/mo). Marketing Consultant, Site Optimizer, Compliance (ToS + privacy policy), 3D logo, AI product photography. Medium confidence (third-party sourced; GoDaddy's own Airo Plus page is JS-gated).
• Airo All Access — 14-day trial bundle, renews at $323.88. Medium confidence.

WEBSITES + MARKETING (the legacy builder, separate product): Basic $16.99/mo list (intro ≈$9.99 annual); Premium $26.99 (intro ≈$14.99); Commerce $29.99 (intro ≈$16.99); Commerce Plus $49.99 (intro ≈$29.99). 7-day free trial, no card. Free plan publishes to yourbusinessname.godaddysites.com. Medium confidence — third-party sourced, and intro vs renewal figures vary across reviews.

ADJACENT COSTS: professional email $2.99/user/mo; Microsoft 365 $7.99/mo; payment processing ≈2.7% + $0.30/transaction. Domains: .co $11.99 first year; .ai $59.99 first year on a 2-year term. Medium confidence (third-party, and GoDaddy domain pricing is highly promotional).

UNVERIFIED / DO NOT ASSUME: exact credit top-up pack prices; per-action credit costs (GoDaddy publishes none — "The search results don't specify how many credits each individual action uses"); Ultimate's published-project count read directly from GoDaddy; whether publishing consumes credits (documented as agent-only billing, but never stated explicitly for publish); current geographic availability (GoDaddy claims 150+ countries, multiple 2026 reviews say US/Canada only).
