one_line_positioning: An agentic full-stack build tool for the React/Next.js/Tailwind/shadcn stack that turns a prompt into production-ready code in a real sandbox, self-QAs its own output in a headless browser, and deploys straight to Vercel — priced by raw token consumption rather than by site.
summary:
v0 is Vercel's AI build product, positioned not as a website builder but as "an AI agent that helps anyone create real code and full-stack apps and agents." Its hero headline is "What do you want to create?" and its three-word product promise is "Prompt. Build. Publish." The target user is a React-literate builder — designer-who-codes, PM prototyping, or engineer scaffolding — not a small-business owner. Everything about the funnel assumes you will eventually look at the code.

**Funnel.** The landing page is pure black (`oklch(0 0 0)`) with a single 690×108px composer, 12px radius, `oklch(0.182 0 0)` fill, placeholder "Ask v0 to build…". A model chip sits bottom-left ("v0 Max" default, aria-label `Select model, current model: v0-max`), a mic icon bottom-right that swaps to a white 28×28px up-arrow submit once you type. Four rotating starter chips (Contact Form, Image Editor, Mini Game, Finance Calculator) sit below with a shuffle button. Critically, **there is no signup wall before generation** — I submitted "a simple landing page for a coffee shop" anonymously and it built the entire site. The model picker even exposes third-party frontier models pre-login under "More models": Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 5 Fast, GPT-5.6 Sol. The wall lands *after* the build completes, as a centered modal: "Create your own app / Sign up to build your idea or duplicate this chat. Free users get $5 in credits per month." This is the inverse of most competitors — maximum proof before any ask.

**Generation.** First render took **6 minutes 21 seconds** ("Worked for 6m 21s"), far slower than Remixer's 2–3 min. The right pane holds an empty state ("Your v0 generation will show here.") the entire time — no live preview assembly. All the drama is in the left chat, which alternates streaming prose with dimmed, shimmering step rows that solidify when done: "Generated design direction", "Scanned project", "Explore • 3 Files", "Generated beans image", "Updated theme colors", "Added font tokens", "Created header", "Created hero". Queued steps appear pre-dimmed in batches of three, so you see the plan before it executes.

**The anti-generic mechanism.** Two things stop v0 producing AI slop. First, it *commits to an art direction out loud* before writing code: "I'll commit to a warm, editorial craft-coffee direction with a deep espresso palette and amber accents." Then it sets theme colors and font tokens *first*, before components. Second — and this is the real differentiator — it runs a **visual self-QA loop**. It loaded an "agent-browser skill", screenshotted its own page ("$ agent-browser screenshot /tmp/agent-browser/full.png --full" shown as a literal terminal line), posted desktop *and* mobile screenshots back into the chat, read debug logs, found a genuine bug ("the Button component doesn't support asChild"), diagnosed it ("The Button uses base-ui, which needs a render prop"), fixed all four call sites, re-verified, and chased a false-positive console error to ground. The output was a genuinely designed page: invented brand "Ember & Oak", Fraunces/Inter pairing, espresso/cream/amber palette, letterspaced eyebrow, AI-generated barista photography, and an overlapping pull-quote card. Not a template.

**Design systems.** This is v0's strongest moat. Legacy v0 grounds on a **shadcn registry** — a `registry.json` exposing `/r/{component}.json` endpoints, with an "Open in v0" button that deep-links with the registry URL as context, plus an MCP server so the same design system grounds Cursor and Windsurf. **Design Systems 2.0** goes further: a design system becomes a *skill* saved at v0.app/design-systems, imported from GitHub repos, Figma frame/node links, Storybook, npm/`.tgz` packages, notes, and `NPM_TOKEN` env vars. It emits a `v0.json` with up to three read-only reference sources, then runs a verification chat that builds a starter app and *pauses for approval before saving*. Attached from the prompt toolbar or set as team default ("Set as Default", "Default" badge). The agent then "refuses to use components, props, or tokens it cannot verify from the provided sources."

**Builder shell.** Left chat (~200px at my viewport, roughly 25%), right canvas. Top bar: v0 mark, favorite star, auto-generated chat title with chevron, then a five-icon cluster (comments, preview/eye, design mode, code, database), then a browser chrome strip — back, forward, device toggle, URL field showing "/", open-in-new, refresh. The code view is a full VS Code clone: file tree headed "V0-PROJECT", explorer/search/git tabs, and an empty-editor state listing shortcuts with keycaps — Go to File ⌘P, Find in Files ⇧⌘F, Command Palette ⇧⌘P, Terminal ^`.

**Publish.** Publish → "Publish to Production", ~30s to live, "Publish Changes" for updates, "Inspect on Vercel" to escape to the dashboard, "Fix with v0" on failed builds, and a "Built with v0" badge on free accounts. Crucially, **Vercel is itself a registrar**: Publish → Customize → "Buy a Domain" purchases in-flow, then Configure → Connect to Project. That directly contests DreamHost's assumed structural advantage — the one thing Vercel cannot do is mailboxes.

**Money.** Free ($0, $5 credits, 7 messages/day), Plus ($30/user/mo), Business ($100/user/mo), Enterprise. Billing is raw token metering — v0 Mini at $0.20/1M in to v0 Max Fast at $50/1M out, a 40× output spread. This is the product's biggest wound: users pay for the agent's own mistakes, and my anonymous run spent minutes of tokens fixing a bug in v0's own scaffolding.

findings.title: No signup wall before generation — anonymous users get a complete build
findings.detail: Submitted 'a simple landing page for a coffee shop' at v0.app while logged out. The app immediately transitioned to the full builder shell and ran the entire agentic build to completion (6m 21s), producing a finished, styled, multi-section page. At no point before or during generation was auth requested. This is the most permissive try-before-signup funnel in the category — more permissive than Remixer's 30-day no-card trial, because it requires literally zero commitment.

findings.title: Signup wall is a post-generation modal, verbatim copy captured
findings.detail: After the build finished, a centered modal appeared over a dark blurred scrim. Bespoke illustration: two interlocking rings forming a chain-link, containing the Vercel triangle and the v0 wordmark. Title 'Create your own app'. Body: 'Sign up to build your idea or duplicate this chat. Free users get $5 in credits per month.' Two full-width stacked buttons: 'Sign Up' (light/white fill) then 'Log In' (dark fill with border). Dismissible via an X at top-right. Note the two distinct offers in one sentence — build your own, or duplicate this one.

findings.title: Zero pre-generation questions — no style chooser, no template picker, no clarifying questions
findings.detail: v0 asks the user nothing before building. There is no industry selector, no palette chooser, no page-count question, no brand upload step. The only pre-flight controls are the model chip and (per Vercel Academy) an 'Enhance prompt' toggle that expands the input into a detailed brief. Design direction is decided by the agent, not elicited from the user — the opposite of a wizard.

findings.title: Composer geometry and tokens, measured
findings.detail: Landing composer: <form> 690×108px, background oklch(0.182 0 0) (~#1c1c1c), border-radius 12px, 1px border oklch(0.39 0 0). Placeholder 'Ask v0 to build…' at 14px/400. Model button 100×28px, 6px radius, transparent fill, aria-label 'Select model, current model: v0-max'. Submit button 28×28px, 6px radius, fill oklch(0.946 0 0) (near-white). Drag-and-drop hint string in the DOM: 'Drop to attach'.

findings.title: Mic-to-arrow submit swap is the composer's only state animation
findings.detail: With the composer empty, the bottom-right control is a microphone icon (voice input). The instant text is entered it becomes an upward arrow submit button. After submission, in the follow-up composer, it becomes a filled circle stop button during generation. Three states on one 28px target — cheap, legible, and it makes voice input discoverable without a separate affordance.

findings.title: Four v0 models plus a 'More models' submenu exposing third-party frontier models — available pre-login
findings.detail: Model dropdown, opened while logged out, listed: v0 Mini, v0 Pro, v0 Max (checked, default), v0 Max Fast, then 'More models ›'. The submenu contained Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 5 Fast, GPT-5.6 Sol — each with its own vendor glyph. v0 therefore resells frontier models through its AI Gateway inside the builder, which is why billing is token-metered rather than per-message.

findings.title: Verbatim model descriptions position the tiers by speed/intelligence tradeoff
findings.detail: From the live pricing page: v0 Mini — 'Lightning-fast speed with near-frontier intelligence'; v0 Pro — 'Balanced speed and intelligence, with superior performance for most tasks'; v0 Max — 'Maximum intelligence for complex work and demanding users'; v0 Max Fast — 'Maximum intelligence with 2.5x faster output speed for rapid iteration'. Note that v0 Max is the DEFAULT, i.e. the most expensive non-Fast tier is preselected for every new anonymous user.

findings.title: The agent commits to a named art direction out loud before writing any code
findings.detail: Verbatim from the run: 'I have what I need. Let me generate a few images and build the page. I'll commit to a warm, editorial craft-coffee direction with a deep espresso palette and amber accents.' This is preceded by a discrete step row labelled 'Generated design direction'. Declaring and naming a direction — rather than defaulting to a neutral shadcn look — is the single most copyable anti-slop mechanism observed, and it costs nothing but a prompt-chain step.

findings.title: Tokens and fonts are written before components, in that exact order
findings.detail: Observed build order: Generated design direction → Scanned project → Explore • 3 Files → Generated beans image → 'Updated theme colors' → 'Added font tokens' → 'Updated auto dark block' → 'Set up fonts and metadata' → 'Applied fonts to html' → 'Updated theme color' → then components (header, hero, menu, roast, visit, footer) → 'Assembled page'. Theme and type are locked in before a single section exists, which is why the output reads as a coherent system rather than a pile of sections.

findings.title: AI image generation is part of the build, not an afterthought
findings.detail: A step row read 'Generated beans image', and the finished hero contained a photorealistic barista espresso-pour image plus a photographed interior in the visit section. The agent generates bespoke imagery inline rather than pulling stock or leaving grey placeholder boxes — which is a large part of why the result does not read as a template.

findings.title: First generation took 6 minutes 21 seconds — badged in the UI
findings.detail: The completed assistant message footer read 'Worked for 6m 21s' next to an activity/pulse icon, with the wall-clock timestamp '4:57 PM' and a '…' overflow menu. v0 surfaces its own slowness as a badge of effort rather than hiding it. For comparison this is roughly 2–3× Remixer's stated 2–3 minute first render.

findings.title: The preview pane stays EMPTY for the entire build — no live assembly
findings.detail: Throughout all 6m21s the right canvas showed only the v0 logomark (outlined square with a diagonal slash) and the string 'Your v0 generation will show here.' The page appeared fully-formed only at the end. v0 deliberately spends the wait on chat narrative rather than on a progressively-building preview — the opposite bet from builders that stream the page in section by section.

findings.title: Step rows use semantic human labels, never file paths, and pre-dim queued work
findings.detail: Completed steps render as a small icon plus grey label: 'Scanned project', 'Explore • 3 Files', 'Checked dependencies', 'Created hero', 'Assembled page', 'Thought for a moment', 'Thought for 1s', 'Thought for 3s'. Steps not yet executed appear simultaneously in a dimmer, shimmering state — typically three at a time — so the user sees the immediate plan before it runs. Labels are past-tense when done, present-participle when running ('Fixing header button semantics').

findings.title: Streaming prose is interleaved between step groups as narration, not dumped up front
findings.detail: Prose appears in short 1–2 sentence bursts that explain the next batch: 'Now let me set up the theme, fonts, and build the page components.' / 'lucide-react is available. Now the hero:' / 'Now the page that assembles everything:' / 'Let me verify it renders correctly in the browser.' The rhythm is narrate → execute → narrate, which keeps a six-minute wait legible.

findings.title: The agent loads a headless browser and visually QAs its own output
findings.detail: Step rows read 'Loaded agent-browser skill' then 'Verified page in browser', then 'Checked debug logs', then 'Screenshotted full page'. The chat displayed the literal shell invocation as a terminal line: '$ agent-browser screenshot /tmp/agent-browser/full.png --full'. This is a closed visual feedback loop — the agent looks at what it built before claiming it is done.

findings.title: The agent posts its own desktop AND mobile screenshots back into the chat as inline thumbnails
findings.detail: After 'Verified page in browser' a desktop render of the hero appeared as a thumbnail card in the chat stream; after 'Now let me verify the error is gone and check mobile responsiveness' → 'Re-verified page', a narrow mobile-width render appeared showing the responsive stat row ('Weekly / 12 Lots / 2016'). The user gets visual proof of responsive correctness without ever touching a device toggle.

findings.title: Self-diagnosis and self-repair of a real code defect, narrated in engineering language
findings.detail: Verbatim chain: 'The page looks great, but there's a real error: the Button component doesn't support asChild. Let me check it.' → 'Read button component' → 'The Button uses base-ui, which needs a render prop instead of asChild. Let me fix all usages.' → four fix steps → 'Base-ui needs nativeButton={false} when rendering as a link. Let me add that to each link button.' → four more fix steps. Inline code identifiers render as monospace chips with a raised background inside the prose.

findings.title: The agent distinguishes real errors from stale console noise — and says so
findings.detail: After fixes it kept probing: 'Now let me verify the console is clean and test the mobile menu toggle.' → 'Verified clean console' → 'The mobile menu works well. Those console errors are stale history from before my fix. Let me reload fresh to confirm a clean console.' → 'Confirmed clean reload' → 'Console history is accumulating across navigations. Let me close the browser fully to clear the buffer, then reopen and check.' → 'Cleared and rechecked console' → 'The console is now clean — the earlier errors were stale history.' It also interactively tested the mobile menu toggle.

findings.title: Closing summary names the design decisions explicitly, in design vocabulary
findings.detail: Verbatim: 'I built Ember & Oak, a warm, editorial craft-coffee landing page with a deep espresso + cream + amber palette and a Fraunces/Inter type pairing. It includes a sticky header with a working mobile menu, a hero with a barista pour image and a pull-quote card, a three-column menu, an "our roast" process section, a visit section with location/hours/contact over a photographed interior, and a footer. Everything is responsive, uses semantic design tokens in globals.css, and the base-ui buttons render as proper anchor links for smooth in-page navigation.' Note it invented a brand name and named the exact typefaces.

findings.title: Two-pane shell with a narrow chat rail — roughly 25/75 split
findings.detail: At a 1280px viewport the chat occupies the left ~200px of an 800px-scaled screenshot (≈25% of width, ~320px CSS) and the canvas takes the rest. Chat is a single scrolling column with the composer docked at the bottom; there is no right-hand icon rail (unlike Remixer). Panel switching happens entirely through the top toolbar icon cluster.

findings.title: Top toolbar anatomy, left to right
findings.detail: v0 logomark (links to New Chat) → favourite star (aria-label 'Add to favorites') → auto-generated chat title as a button with chevron ('Coffee shop landing page') → collapse-chat chevron → a five-icon cluster (comments, eye/preview, design mode, code </>, database) → browser chrome strip: back ‹, forward ›, device/viewport toggle, URL field showing '/' → open-in-new-tab, refresh, chevron → 'Log In' / 'Sign Up' (which is where Publish sits once authenticated). Toolbar icons are 16px custom Geist icons and carry NO aria-labels or title attributes — an accessibility gap.

findings.title: Chat title and URL slug are auto-derived from the first prompt
findings.detail: Prompt 'a simple landing page for a coffee shop' produced title 'Coffee shop landing page' and URL https://v0.app/chat/coffee-shop-landing-page-mxUh28K2l4e — i.e. slugified-title + 11-character chat ID. Document title becomes 'Coffee shop landing page - v0 by Vercel'. Titles are editable via the chevron dropdown.

findings.title: The code view is a full VS Code clone with explorer, search and source-control tabs
findings.detail: Clicking the </> icon opens a three-tab left rail (file icon / magnifier / git branch) above a file tree headed 'V0-PROJECT' with its own toolbar (new file, new folder, refresh, collapse-all, '…'). Tree contents from my run: folders app, components, lib, public; files .gitignore, components.json, next-env.d.ts, next.config.mjs, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, postcss.config.mjs, tsconfig.json.

findings.title: Empty-editor state teaches four keyboard shortcuts with rendered keycaps
findings.detail: With no file open, the editor pane shows the v0 logomark, the line 'Describe what you want to build and let the agent help', and a shortcut list with individual key-cap chips: Go to File ⌘P · Find in Files ⇧⌘F · Command Palette ⇧⌘P · Terminal ^` . This confirms v0 has a command palette and an integrated terminal, and it teaches them at the exact moment of idleness.

findings.title: File chips and a Console tab expose the full-stack runtime
findings.detail: During the build a file chip rendered in the chat showing filename plus dimmed path on two lines ('site-header.tsx' / 'components/site-header.tsx'), with the status line 'Loading file changes' beneath. Vercel Academy documents a Console tab showing 'real server requests and responses' as you interact with the preview, and a Code tab showing 'every file the agent wrote: server files, API routes, frontend components'.

findings.title: Design Mode is a full property inspector overlaid on the live preview
findings.detail: Enabled from the prompt-form toolbar. Cursor becomes a selection tool; hover highlights elements, click selects and shows selection handles plus the design panel. Property groups: Typography (font family, size, weight, line height, letter spacing, alignment, text decoration), Color, Background, Layout (margin/padding all sides), Border (color, style, width), Appearance (opacity, corner radius), Shadow, Content (direct text editing). Side panels include a Layers view of the component hierarchy and an Inspector surfacing metadata like links and element IDs.

findings.title: Design Mode has Undo/Redo/Reset plus a Before/After comparison toggle, and Cmd+I to switch modes
findings.detail: The panel carries Undo, Redo and Reset buttons and a Before/After preview toggle to compare against the original. The 'Inspect' control — or Cmd+I / Ctrl+I — toggles between selecting elements and interacting with the app normally; Escape deselects. The Before/After toggle in particular is a detail most visual editors lack.

findings.title: Design Mode edits are batched and committed via 'Apply', creating a real chat version
findings.detail: Clicking Apply 'serializes your edits (and any instructions / screenshots), sends them to the chat, and generates an updated version of your project that reflects the changes in your source code.' Applied edits create new chat versions supporting diffs, iteration and reversion. Crucially you can also type natural-language instructions at a selected element, and 'v0 automatically attaches a screenshot of the selected element along with your instructions' — visual selection becomes multimodal context. The panel surfaces Tailwind-compatible values where applicable.

findings.title: Design Mode is free-tier, but unavailable on mobile viewports and read-only chats
findings.detail: The Free plan bullet reads verbatim 'Edit visually with Design Mode' — it is not paywalled. Docs state it requires the latest preview runtime and latest chat version, and is unavailable on read-only chats or mobile viewports.

findings.title: Version chips appear inline in the chat stream with a Restore action attached
findings.detail: A 'v1' chip rendered inline in the message flow immediately after 'Assembled page', and the accessibility text showed 'v1' followed by 'Restore'. Separately, a version dropdown sits in the top-right showing the current version count (e.g. 'v2'), and users can scroll the chat and click a '↩' icon to restore an earlier generation. Versions are created only when v0 updates a code block from a message — 'Non-message actions (such as editing code or modifying files directly) do not generate new versions.'

findings.title: Restore is linear, not branching — it creates a NEW latest version from old code
findings.detail: Docs: restoring a previous version creates 'a new, most recent version using the restored code', maintaining linear history rather than branching. Deployment always uses the latest version, so shipping an older build requires restoring it first. This avoids a version tree but means the history grows monotonically.

findings.title: Forking is a first-class primitive — including in the public API
findings.detail: You can create a new chat fork (duplicate) from a specific version within an existing chat, for branching alternate directions without touching the original conversation. There is a documented API endpoint for it (Fork Chat, v0.app/docs/api/platform/reference/chats/fork). Reviewers describe the resulting workflow as forking several directions at once rather than re-prompting one linear thread. Deleted chats are recoverable for 30 days from an archive view.

findings.title: Design Systems 2.0: a design system is saved as a reusable 'skill'
findings.detail: Docs define it as 'a small, focused set of instructions v0 keeps with your work and pulls in when relevant' — an adapter pointing v0 at component sources, safe-to-use tokens and integration patterns, rather than pasted documentation. Saved systems live at v0.app/design-systems under the heading 'Your Design Systems'.

findings.title: Design system import accepts seven source types including Figma node links and private npm tokens
findings.detail: The import form accepts: GitHub repositories (source or consumer apps); Figma frame/node URLs (v0 extracts screenshots and context); external links (Storybook, docs, guidelines); file attachments (screenshots, ZIPs, .tgz archives, exported packages); a Notes field for things that cannot be inferred (global styles, deprecated components, conventions); and an Environment Variables section for credentials such as NPM_TOKEN via 'shared environment variables'. Consumer apps are explicitly encouraged as a source because they demonstrate real global setup.

findings.title: Import produces a v0.json config with a hard cap of three reference sources
findings.detail: Generated config carries version, referenceWorkspace.sources (each with id like 'github-repo:owner/repo:main', type, repo org/name, ref, and a mountPath under /vercel/share/v0-reference-workspace-sources/...), environment.providers (shared-env-vars or vercel-project), and starter (source: skill-directory | v0-default | empty). Docs state a v0.json can include 'up to three reference sources', mounted read-only.

findings.title: Import runs a verification chat that builds a starter app and PAUSES for approval before saving
findings.detail: After submitting the form, v0 opens a dedicated chat that: discovers sources and design system primitives; builds a starter app and previews it; pauses for user approval before saving; saves the skill on approval; then validates and returns verified links. During review v0 checks 'how it looks and how it's wired up: components and tokens, providers, theme setup, fonts, and global styles.' The human-in-the-loop pause before persistence is the detail worth stealing.

findings.title: Grounded generation explicitly refuses unverifiable components
findings.detail: Once a skill is attached, v0 applies its instructions, references and starter app, grounding itself 'in the real source', and refuses to use components, props, or tokens it cannot verify from the provided sources. This refusal behaviour — rather than hallucinating a plausible prop — is what makes registry grounding trustworthy enough to ship.

findings.title: Attach from prompt toolbar, or set a team default with a 'Default' badge
findings.detail: A menu in the prompt toolbar shows an attached design system skill and lets users pick one per chat. Team owners open a skill card's actions menu and choose 'Set as Default'; the chosen skill then shows a 'Default' badge, removable from the same menu. Manual per-chat selection overrides the team default. Skills can also be invoked by naming them in the prompt ('Update Acme UI to v2.3…').

findings.title: Updating a skill deliberately does NOT rewrite existing projects
findings.detail: Docs: 'Updating a design system skill changes the shared instructions… Existing chats… don't automatically rewrite code they've already generated.' Users must ask v0 per-project to adopt the update. Skills are updated conversationally — you tell v0 what changed (release notes, migration guides, new package versions, updated GitHub sources) and it edits the skill and re-validates the starter app.

findings.title: Legacy registry path: shadcn registry.json + /r/{component}.json + 'Open in v0' deep link + MCP
findings.detail: A registry is 'a distribution specification designed to pass context from your design system to AI Models.' registry.json exposes components/blocks per the shadcn spec; the build emits per-item endpoints at /r/${component_name}.json containing file content and metadata. Registry pages at /registry/[name] expose an 'Open in v0' button that redirects to v0 with a prepopulated prompt plus the JSON endpoint URL. The first registry item MUST be named 'theme' and carries Tailwind config plus design tokens/CSS variables — this is required for MCP. Private registries gate /r/:path with REGISTRY_AUTH_TOKEN passed as a token= search param.

findings.title: MCP makes the design system portable to competing editors — deliberately
findings.detail: Registries support the Model Context Protocol, which 'keeps model generations grounded'; Vercel states the design system 'will not only work in v0, but in tools like Cursor and Windsurf too.' Configuration is a JSON block specifying REGISTRY_URL. Vercel is betting that owning the design-system format is more valuable than locking generation to v0 — a notable strategic choice.

findings.title: Preview is real browser chrome, not a device-frame mock
findings.detail: The canvas top strip is a functioning browser bar: back and forward arrows, a device/viewport toggle icon, an editable URL field showing the current route ('/'), plus open-in-new-tab, refresh and a chevron menu. Because the app runs in a real sandbox, navigating routes in the preview behaves like a real site rather than a static render.

findings.title: Preview runs on a per-chat sandbox domain: {24-char-id}.v0.build
findings.detail: The preview iframe src was https://v0.app/chat/api/vm/open?vmUrl=https%3A%2F%2F73qx9a7279h0x9j9qkbclmxp.v0.build%2F&chatId=mxUh28K2l4e&scope= . So the staging/sandbox host is *.v0.build with an opaque 24-character subdomain, proxied through a /chat/api/vm/open endpoint. Unlike Remixer's editable *.remixer.app subdomain, the v0 sandbox host is machine-generated and not presented as a user-facing address.

findings.title: Publish is a menu, not a one-shot button: Publish → 'Publish to Production'
findings.detail: The Publish button sits top-right. Clicking it opens a menu where you select 'Publish to Production'; Vercel builds and hosts, live in roughly 30 seconds. In the publish menu you name the project and set visibility (e.g. 'Team only') before confirming. Subsequent updates use 'Publish Changes' to update production 'instantly with zero downtime'. Each project has exactly one production URL.

findings.title: 'Inspect on Vercel' is the deliberate escape hatch to the real dashboard
findings.detail: An 'Inspect on Vercel' button in the Publish card opens the Vercel dashboard for environment variables, custom domains, analytics, deployment protection and monitoring. v0 does not attempt to reimplement hosting settings inside the builder — it hands off. Failed deployments get a 'Fix with v0' button that diagnoses and applies fixes; the documented fallback is to 'go back one version'.

findings.title: Free deployments carry a 'Built with v0' badge
findings.detail: Deployed apps show a 'Built with v0' badge by default for free users, toggled via Project Menu '…' → Vercel Project. A visible attribution tax on the free tier — worth noting as a conversion lever Remixer does not currently use.

findings.title: Vercel sells domains IN-FLOW — Publish → Customize → 'Buy a Domain'
findings.detail: Vercel Academy documents: click 'Customize', then 'Buy a Domain' to search for and purchase a custom domain through Vercel's own registrar; then 'Configure' → 'Connect to Project'. Vercel has a Domains Registrar API (search, price, buy, renew, transfer, nameserver management) and has cut domain prices 'by up to 50%', pricing at registrar cost. This materially contests the assumed DreamHost registrar advantage: v0 can also sell-and-connect with zero DNS work. What Vercel cannot do is provision @yourdomain mailboxes.

findings.title: Two entry points to domains; free *.vercel.app is offered as the default alternative
findings.detail: Entry points: 'Publish' → 'Customize Domain', or 'Project Menu …' → 'Domains'. Clicking Add presents two options: a free .vercel.app domain described as 'free and instantly available' with automatic HTTPS, or a custom domain. Propagation is messaged as 'custom domains take a few minutes', with Vercel indicating roughly 15 minutes while work continues in the background.

findings.title: External-domain DNS is punted to the Vercel dashboard, not guided in v0
findings.detail: For a domain registered elsewhere, v0 docs direct users to click 'Inspect on Vercel' and follow instructions in the Vercel dashboard and external Vercel docs. The v0-specific documentation does not specify record types, nameserver-vs-CNAME choice, SSL provisioning messaging, or verification UI copy. So v0's in-builder domain experience is strong only for Vercel-registered domains — the same shape of gap Remixer has, just with a different boundary.

findings.title: No email product at any tier — a structural absence, not an oversight
findings.detail: Across the pricing page, docs navigation, integrations messaging and FAQs there is no mailbox, @yourdomain email, or email-hosting offering. Hosting is Vercel's edge platform with automatic HTTPS, edge caching and CDN distribution. Transactional email would come via a third-party integration. This is the one axis where DreamHost's registrar+host+email position cannot be matched by Vercel.

findings.title: 2026 rebuild moved v0 from component generator to full-stack sandbox
findings.detail: The February 2026 'Introducing the new v0' launch added a sandbox-based runtime that can import any GitHub repo and automatically pull environment variables and configurations from Vercel, plus API routes, server actions and database connections. Secure integrations with Snowflake and AWS databases let users 'connect your app directly to the tables you need'. The landing page states 'Agentic by default — v0 plans, creates tasks, and connects to databases as it builds.'

findings.title: Integrations pitch is 'no accounts required' — provisioning is abstracted away
findings.detail: Landing page verbatim: 'Integrate with apps — Build with your favorite tools and APIs. Automatic integration, no accounts required.' The claim is that v0 provisions/wires third-party services without the user creating accounts with each provider. A database icon sits in the builder toolbar cluster as a dedicated panel.

findings.title: Collaboration is a paid-tier gate, and Publish carries visibility controls
findings.detail: 'Share chats and collaborate with your team' appears as a bullet on Plus and Business only, not Free. The publish menu includes a visibility setting (e.g. 'Team only'). Deployment-level access is governed by Vercel Deployment Protection: without protection anyone with the link can view; with Vercel Authentication only team members can, unless individually added, having requested access, or via sharable links. Access requests can be approved, declined and revoked from the share modal on the deployment page.

findings.title: Template gallery uses fork-count and like-count as the primary social proof
findings.detail: Cards show a screenshot thumbnail, title, an author handle (e.g. @estebansuarez), and two numbers — fork/duplicate count and likes (observed: 'Image Generation Playground' 6.4K/714; 'Brillance SaaS Landing Page' 14.1K/2.1K; 'Optimus' 7.8K/1.3K; 'The Orb' 3.5K/81). Card action is 'View Details'; the section CTA is 'Duplicate a Template'. Landing filter chips: Apps and Games, Landing Pages, Components, Dashboards, then 'Browse all ›'. Full category list adds Login & Sign Up, Blog & Portfolio, E-commerce, AI, Animations, Design Systems, Layouts, Website Templates, Agents.

findings.title: Geist Sans on pure black, with an internal v0 gray scale exposed in class names
findings.detail: body font-family is 'GeistSans, GeistSans Fallback, ui-sans-serif, system-ui…'; body background is oklch(0 0 0) — true #000, not a soft charcoal like Remixer's #18181B; body text oklch(0.946 0 0). html carries class 'dark' and color-scheme dark. Utility classes revealed v0's own token scale: text-v0-gray-900, hover:text-v0-gray-1000, bg-v0-background-100 — Tailwind v4 syntax with the '!' important modifier.

findings.title: Marketing type is tight and restrained: 32px/600 headline at -1.28px tracking
findings.detail: The hero h1 'What do you want to create?' computes to 32px, weight 600, letter-spacing -1.28px (exactly -0.04em). It is notably SMALL for a hero — v0 does not shout. The restraint plus true-black ground and near-white text is a large part of why the site reads as expensive rather than loud.

findings.title: A deliberate two-radius system: 12px containers, 6px controls, full-round chips
findings.detail: Measured: composer form 12px radius; model button and submit button 6px; suggestion chips border-radius effectively infinite (fully rounded pill), 32px tall, 14px/500 text, background oklch(0.182 0 0), 1px border oklch(1 0 0 / 0.145), text oklch(0.706 0 0), padding 0 12px. Three radius values total across the whole hero — containers, controls, chips — each mapped to a semantic role.

findings.title: Custom 16px Geist icon set, not Lucide, in the product chrome
findings.detail: Toolbar SVGs use a 16-unit viewBox with bespoke path geometry and no lucide-* class names, unlike the generated output which uses lucide-react. v0 draws its own product iconography while shipping Lucide to users — the chrome and the output are visibly different icon families.

findings.title: Vercel's code syntax palette is a distinct, saturated accent system
findings.detail: CSS custom properties on :root define the code theme: --sh-class #00a7fd, --sh-string #00e7c1, --sh-keyword #ff0078, --sh-identifier #fff, --sh-sign #9b9b9b, --sh-comment #a19595, --sh-jsxliterals #ffff72. These vivid cyan/magenta/mint accents are the only strong colour in an otherwise monochrome interface, which makes code feel like the product's centre of gravity.

findings.title: Three distinct empty states, each with purposeful copy
findings.detail: Preview pane while building: v0 logomark plus 'Your v0 generation will show here.' Code pane while syncing: a centered rounded pill with spinner reading 'Syncing project files…'. Editor with no file open: logomark, 'Describe what you want to build and let the agent help', plus the four shortcut rows. None are generic spinners — each states what is happening or what to do next.

findings.title: Live 2026 tiers: Free $0 / Plus $30 per user / Business $100 per user / Enterprise custom — monthly only
findings.detail: Verified on the live pricing page 13 Aug 2026. Free: '$5 of included monthly credits', 'Deploy apps to Vercel', 'Edit visually with Design Mode', 'Sync with GitHub', '7 message/day limit', CTA 'Start Building'. Plus (badged 'Popular'): 'Access to all models', '$30 of included monthly credits per user', '$2 of free daily credits on login per user', purchasable overage shared across team, 'Centralized billing on vercel.com', 'Share chats and collaborate with your team', CTA 'Select Plan'. Business adds 'Training opt-out by default'. Enterprise adds 'Your data is never used for training', SAML SSO, RBAC, 'Priority access for better performance and no queues', 'Guaranteed customer support SLAs'. No annual toggle is offered — unlike Remixer's yearly discount.

findings.title: Billing is raw token metering with a 40x spread between cheapest and dearest output
findings.detail: Published per-1M-token rates: v0 Mini $0.20 in / $0.25 cache write / $0.02 cache read / $1.20 out. v0 Pro $2 / $2.50 / $0.20 / $10. v0 Max $5 / $6.25 / $0.50 / $25. v0 Max Fast $10 / $12.50 / $1 / $50. Output on Max Fast costs 40x output on Mini. Because v0 Max is the default selection, a naive user is on the second-most-expensive tier by default.

findings.title: Credits roll over but expire at 65 days; purchased credits last a year
findings.detail: Docs: 'Unused monthly credits roll over to the next billing cycle and expire after 65 days.' Purchased additional credits expire one year after purchase and persist if the subscription lapses, though an active paid plan is required to spend them. Premium, Plus and Business can purchase additional credits at any time; Enterprise must contact their Account Executive. Purchased credits are shareable across the team on Team/Enterprise.

findings.title: There is no individual paid plan — the cheapest paid tier is priced per seat
findings.detail: The historical Premium tier at $20/month is documented as 'being sunsetted' and unavailable to new users, and it does not appear on the live pricing page. The pricing FAQ also asks 'What happened to the Ultra plan?'. Net effect in 2026: a solo hobbyist goes from Free ($5 credits, 7 messages/day) straight to $30/user/month. That is a hard cliff, and a direct opening for Remixer's $9.99.

findings.title: The paywall interrupts at exhaustion, mid-task — not at a feature boundary
findings.detail: Free users hit two independent walls: a 7-message/day cap and a $5 credit balance. Community reports describe running out mid-build: one user reported v0 'drained my credits and tried to restart, but just told me that I ran out of credits.' Because failed and self-corrective generations bill the same as successful ones, the interruption lands at the least forgivable moment.

findings.title: Native iOS app built on React Native + Expo, chat-only by design
findings.detail: Vercel explicitly 'did not set out to build a mobile IDE with feature parity with our website' — the centerpiece is the chat. Landing copy: 'Create from your phone — Build anywhere with the v0 iOS app. Design on the go.' with a 'Ship mobile sites' CTA and a dedicated 'iOS' nav item. Positioned as 'the next generation of your Notes app, where your ideas get built in the background.'

findings.title: The iOS app's streaming text animation is pooled and staggered at 32ms, capped at 4 concurrent words
findings.detail: A TextFadeInStaggeredIfStreaming component chunks words into individual nodes and limits concurrent animations to 4 words at a time with 32ms stagger, to hold frame rate during rapid streaming. User messages 'animate in smoothly' and scroll to the top of the screen; assistant responses 'fade in with a staggered transition as they stream'. This is an unusually rigorous approach to making token streaming feel composed rather than jittery.

findings.title: iOS composer is a 'Liquid Glass composer with a progressive blur' over a patched native text view
findings.detail: The floating input toolbar is absolutely positioned at the bottom via KeyboardStickyView, with a progressive-blur glass treatment inspired by iMessage. The team patched native RCTUITextView to kill scroll indicators and bounce, enable interactive keyboard dismissal, and support an upward pan gesture to focus the input. Menus are native UIMenu via Zeego, alerts are native iOS alerts, bottom sheets use presentationStyle='formSheet'. A ~1,000-line useKeyboardAwareMessageList hook handles six keyboard behaviours including deduplicating repeated iOS keyboard events.

findings.title: Paste handling on iOS converts long text to a file attachment automatically
findings.detail: An Expo Module listens to native UIPasteboard events so users can paste images and files straight into the text input; long text pastes automatically convert into .txt file attachments rather than flooding the composer. A small, high-empathy detail that directly reduces a common mobile annoyance.

findings.title: Training opt-out is a paid feature; code ownership is explicit
findings.detail: FAQ: 'Vercel doesn't own the code generated based on your queries and prompts', with the caveat that users must evaluate output for suitability and that it may overlap with other users' work. v0 may use prompts and content to improve products via third-party models EXCEPT for Enterprise customers or those who opted out in Vercel settings. Business gets 'Training opt-out by default'; Enterprise gets 'Your data is never used for training' plus SAML SSO and RBAC. Data deletion is a manual email request to privacy@vercel.com.

findings.title: Post-launch tooling exists but lives on Vercel, not in v0
findings.detail: Deployments include 'automatic HTTPS, edge caching, performance monitoring, and analytics integration', and after going live the Vercel dashboard Settings section provides analytics tracking visitor data, integrations, and domains management. There is no in-builder analytics panel — the user is expected to cross into the Vercel dashboard, which is a meaningful drop-off for non-developer audiences.

findings.title: Self-healing is expensive: a large share of my run was spent fixing v0's own scaffold
findings.detail: Of the ~6m21s build, roughly a third of the visible steps (Read button component, four asChild fixes, four nativeButton fixes, three console re-verification cycles) were spent correcting an incompatibility between v0's own starter Button component and base-ui. Under token metering the user pays for this. It is the mechanistic root of the most common complaint — elliottux measured '20% of this was on corrections where v0 broke stuff.'

findings.title: Public Platform API and SDK let third parties build on v0's generation engine
findings.detail: Package v0-sdk (npm install v0-sdk), base URL https://api.v0.dev, auth via V0_API_KEY env var or createClient() for multiple keys/enterprise URLs, keys issued at v0.app/settings/keys. Documented surface includes v0.chats.create(), v0.chats.init() (seed with existing files), project CRUD, v0.deployments.create(), and a chats fork endpoint. REST paths POST /v1/chats, GET /v1/projects, POST /v1/deployments.

findings.title: Legal/limitation disclaimer sits permanently under the composer
findings.detail: Beneath the follow-up composer in the builder: 'v0 may make mistakes. Please use with discretion.' Persistent rather than a dismissible one-time notice — a calibrated-uncertainty pattern placed at the point of input rather than buried in terms.

standout_ux.name: Generate first, ask for the account second
standout_ux.what_it_is: An anonymous visitor can type a prompt on the homepage and receive a complete, deployed-to-sandbox, self-QA'd site with zero authentication. The signup modal ('Create your own app / Sign up to build your idea or duplicate this chat. Free users get $5 in credits per month.') only appears after the build finishes.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It inverts the usual bargain. The user has already seen 6 minutes of visible competence and a finished artefact they feel ownership of before being asked for anything. The modal's second clause — 'or duplicate this chat' — converts loss-aversion directly: signing up is framed as keeping the thing you already have, not starting something new.

standout_ux.name: Declare the art direction out loud before writing code
standout_ux.what_it_is: A discrete 'Generated design direction' step, followed by a sentence in chat naming the specific aesthetic: 'I'll commit to a warm, editorial craft-coffee direction with a deep espresso palette and amber accents.' Theme colours and font tokens are then written before any component.
standout_ux.why_it_works: This is the cheapest known fix for AI-slop output. Forcing the model to name and commit to a direction prevents regression to the safe-average look, and stating it in chat makes the direction a reviewable artefact — the user can reject 'warm editorial' in one sentence before six minutes of building, instead of after.

standout_ux.name: The agent screenshots its own output and posts the evidence into the chat
standout_ux.what_it_is: v0 loads an 'agent-browser skill', renders the built page in a real headless browser, screenshots it at desktop and mobile widths, and embeds both thumbnails in the conversation — showing even the raw command line: '$ agent-browser screenshot /tmp/agent-browser/full.png --full'.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Two payoffs from one mechanism. Functionally it closes a visual feedback loop so the agent catches layout and responsive failures a text-only model cannot see. Rhetorically it is the single most trust-building moment in the product: the user watches the machine check its own work and shows the receipts.

standout_ux.name: Visible self-diagnosis in real engineering language
standout_ux.what_it_is: On finding a defect the agent narrates the whole loop: 'there's a real error: the Button component doesn't support asChild' → reads the component → 'The Button uses base-ui, which needs a render prop instead of asChild' → fixes all four call sites → re-verifies → then distinguishes genuine errors from stale console history and reloads to prove it.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It converts the most anxious part of AI building — 'did it actually work?' — into a spectator sport with a resolution. The precision of the language ('base-ui needs nativeButton={false} when rendering as a link') signals competence to a technical audience far more effectively than a green success toast.

standout_ux.name: Design-system-as-skill, with a mandatory approval pause before saving
standout_ux.what_it_is: A team imports its design system from GitHub repos, Figma node links, Storybook, npm packages and free-text notes. v0 opens a verification chat that discovers primitives, builds a starter app, previews it, and then PAUSES for human approval before persisting anything. Once saved, the agent refuses to use components, props or tokens it cannot verify from those sources.
standout_ux.why_it_works: The pause is the whole trick. A design system that silently absorbs a wrong inference poisons every future generation, so v0 makes the first save a reviewed artefact rather than a background job. The refusal behaviour then converts grounding from a soft prior into a hard constraint — which is what makes it safe to set as a team default.

standout_ux.name: Empty states that teach shortcuts instead of apologising
standout_ux.what_it_is: The code editor with no file open shows the v0 mark, the line 'Describe what you want to build and let the agent help', and four shortcut rows with rendered keycaps: Go to File ⌘P, Find in Files ⇧⌘F, Command Palette ⇧⌘P, Terminal ^`.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It uses the one moment the user is guaranteed to be idle and looking at nothing to transfer the four highest-leverage skills in the panel. Rendered keycaps rather than prose make them scannable and memorable, and it quietly signals that this is a real IDE.

standout_ux.name: Semantic past-tense step rows with pre-dimmed queued work
standout_ux.what_it_is: Progress renders as short human labels — 'Scanned project', 'Created hero', 'Updated theme colors', 'Fixed visit button semantics' — past tense when complete, present participle while running, with the next batch of roughly three steps shown pre-dimmed and shimmering before execution.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It makes a six-minute wait navigable without a progress bar, which would be a lie anyway. Showing queued steps gives the user a short-horizon forecast so the wait feels bounded, and semantic labels rather than file paths keep it readable to non-engineers while remaining honest about what happened.

standout_ux.name: Mic becomes arrow becomes stop, on one 28px target
standout_ux.what_it_is: The composer's trailing button is a microphone when empty, an upward arrow submit once text exists, and a filled stop circle while the agent is running.
standout_ux.why_it_works: One pixel budget, three affordances, each correct exactly when it is relevant. Voice input becomes discoverable without cluttering the composer, and cancel appears precisely at the only moment it matters — no dead controls at any point in the cycle.

standout_ux.name: Buy the domain inside the publish flow
standout_ux.what_it_is: Publish → Customize → 'Buy a Domain' searches and purchases through Vercel's own registrar (prices at registrar cost, recently cut up to 50%), then Configure → Connect to Project attaches it with no DNS work.
standout_ux.why_it_works: It removes the single biggest drop-off between 'my site is built' and 'my site is real'. Notably this closes the gap Remixer assumes is structural — the registrar+builder combination is not unique to DreamHost, so the durable differentiator is mailboxes, not domains.

standout_ux.name: Worked-for badge as an honesty signal
standout_ux.what_it_is: The completed message footer reads 'Worked for 6m 21s' alongside a wall-clock timestamp and an overflow menu.
standout_ux.why_it_works: Rather than hiding latency, it reframes elapsed time as evidence of thoroughness — consistent with the visible QA loop. It also sets a truthful expectation for the next prompt, which is more durable than an optimistic progress estimate that keeps being wrong.

weaknesses.issue: Token-metered credits burn far faster than users expect, and the model bills for its own mistakes
weaknesses.evidence: Vercel Community thread 'Credits are burning way too fast under the new pricing model'. User Amit: 'I spent 30$ in a single day just to add a couple of category pages. The new pricing model is insanely worse. We are literally paying for all the good/bad codes that v0 generates, it's terrible.' User elliottux quantified it: 'Each iteration is now costing between $0.15 and $0.30 where as previously it was $0.08 and $0.12', with ~20% of iterations being corrections for functionality v0 itself broke. Another user reported paying an extra $30 and finding 'today that 30 dollars ran out! AFTER 2 DAYS!'

weaknesses.issue: The self-healing loop is billable, and I watched it fix a bug in v0's own starter scaffold
weaknesses.evidence: In my anonymous run, roughly a third of visible steps were spent correcting an incompatibility between v0's bundled Button component and base-ui ('the Button component doesn't support asChild'), requiring eight separate fix steps plus three console re-verification cycles across the 6m 21s build. Under token metering a paying user funds that remediation.

weaknesses.issue: No individual paid plan — a hard cliff from Free to $30/user/month
weaknesses.evidence: The live pricing page (13 Aug 2026) shows only Free, Plus $30/user/mo, Business $100/user/mo and Enterprise. The former Premium $20/mo tier is documented as 'being sunsetted' and unavailable to new users, and the pricing FAQ includes 'What happened to the Ultra plan?'. A solo builder exhausting $5 of credits and 7 messages/day has no intermediate option.

weaknesses.issue: Hard stack lock-in to React/Next.js/Tailwind/shadcn
weaknesses.evidence: Reviewers are consistent that v0 'supports one framework' and generates shadcn/ui + Tailwind targeting Next.js regardless of request. Hacker News user _bin_ (March 2025): 'i asked it for some basic svelte code. it spat out react.' For anyone outside the Vercel ecosystem this is disqualifying.

weaknesses.issue: Long sessions degrade into broken project state
weaknesses.evidence: User dasilvacontin (April 2025) reported that after 30+ prompts projects entered a 'broken state' with missing files in exports, abandoning the tool despite liking the output quality. Community threads also exist titled 'Cannot revert to previous working state' and 'Previous Versions and Chat VANISHED'.

weaknesses.issue: Post-March-2026 regressions in prompt adherence and preview stability
weaknesses.evidence: Community reports collected in 2026 reviews: dk-hello reported spending $300 on a single parser bug while the tool 'won't listen' to prompts; luobo1689-5678 cited connection errors and preview failures. A Vercel Community thread is titled 'Huge issue with v0 wasting credits and not doing the prompt'.

weaknesses.issue: Six minutes to first render, with an empty preview pane the whole time
weaknesses.evidence: Measured directly: the completion badge read 'Worked for 6m 21s', and the right canvas showed only 'Your v0 generation will show here.' for the entire duration. That is roughly 2–3× Remixer's 2–3 minute first render, and unlike builders that stream the page in progressively, there is nothing to look at but chat.

weaknesses.issue: Builder toolbar icons ship with no accessible names
weaknesses.evidence: Querying every <header> button in the builder returned aria-label and title both null for the entire icon cluster (comments, preview, design mode, code, database) and for the browser-chrome controls. Only 'Add to favorites' carried a label. Icon-only controls without accessible names are unusable via screen reader and undiscoverable without hovering.

weaknesses.issue: Design Mode is unavailable exactly where non-technical users often are
weaknesses.evidence: v0 docs state design mode 'is unavailable on read-only chats or mobile viewports' and requires the latest preview runtime and latest chat version. The visual editing story therefore does not extend to the iOS app or to shared read-only links.

weaknesses.issue: External-domain DNS is handed off to the Vercel dashboard rather than guided in-product
weaknesses.evidence: v0's custom-domain doc instructs users to click 'Inspect on Vercel' and follow instructions in the Vercel dashboard and external docs; it does not specify record types, nameserver-vs-CNAME guidance, SSL provisioning messaging or verification copy. The polished in-flow experience only exists for domains bought from Vercel.

weaknesses.issue: Free deployments are branded
weaknesses.evidence: v0 deployment docs state apps show a 'Built with v0' badge by default for free users, removable via Project Menu … → Vercel Project.

weaknesses.issue: Failed generations are not refunded and support treats them case-by-case
weaknesses.evidence: v0's own FAQ answers 'Why do v0 agents keep failing and consuming my credits?' with 'The v0 agent is constantly improving. If you're experiencing repeated failures, please send us feedback so we can investigate.' — no credit-back policy. In the main pricing complaint thread no Vercel response appeared at all.

weaknesses.issue: No email product at any tier
weaknesses.evidence: No mailbox or @yourdomain email offering appears anywhere across the pricing page, docs navigation, integrations messaging or FAQs. Hosting is edge/CDN only.

pricing_2026:
VERIFIED LIVE on v0.app/pricing, 13 August 2026. Monthly billing only — no annual toggle is offered.

FREE — $0/month. Bullets verbatim: "$5 of included monthly credits" · "Deploy apps to Vercel" · "Edit visually with Design Mode" · "Sync with GitHub" · "7 message/day limit". CTA: "Start Building".

PLUS — $30/user/month, badged "Popular". Bullets verbatim: "Access to all models" · "$30 of included monthly credits per user" · "$2 of free daily credits on login per user" · "Purchase additional credits outside of your monthly usage shared across your team" · "Centralized billing on vercel.com" · "Share chats and collaborate with your team". CTA: "Select Plan".

BUSINESS — $100/user/month. All Plus bullets (still "$30 of included monthly credits per user" — the extra $70/seat buys governance, not credits) PLUS "Training opt-out by default". CTA: "Select Plan".

ENTERPRISE — Custom Pricing. "Access to all models" · "Your data is never used for training" · "SAML SSO" · "Role-based access control" · "Priority access for better performance and no queues" · "Guaranteed customer support SLAs". CTA: "Contact Us".

SUNSET TIERS: A "Premium" plan at $20/month with $20 monthly credits is described in v0 docs as "being sunsetted" and unavailable to new users; it does NOT appear on the live pricing page. The pricing FAQ also asks "What happened to the Ultra plan?". Net effect: as of 2026 there is NO individual paid plan — the cheapest paid tier is per-seat at $30.

CREDIT MODEL: Not messages — raw input/output token metering, converted to credits, introduced 13 May 2025 (Vercel blog "Updated v0 pricing"). Published per-1M-token rates:
· v0 Mini — input $0.20, cache write $0.25, cache read $0.02, output $1.20
· v0 Pro — input $2, cache write $2.50, cache read $0.20, output $10
· v0 Max — input $5, cache write $6.25, cache read $0.50, output $25
· v0 Max Fast — input $10, cache write $12.50, cache read $1, output $50
Output on Max Fast is 40× output on Mini. v0 Max is the DEFAULT model for a new anonymous user.

WHAT BURNS CREDITS: every generation, including chat history and context re-sent as input tokens (the pricing FAQ explicitly addresses "Why do messages use so many input tokens? My prompts are short."), and including failed or self-corrective generations — there is no documented refund for failures. Design Mode edits, when Applied, generate a new version and therefore consume tokens. Third-party models (Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 5 Fast, GPT-5.6 Sol) are selectable and metered the same way; per-token rates for those specific models are UNVERIFIED.

ROLLOVER/EXPIRY: "Unused monthly credits roll over to the next billing cycle and expire after 65 days." Purchased additional credits expire one year after purchase, persist if the subscription lapses but require an active paid plan to spend, and are shareable across the team on Team/Enterprise. Premium, Plus and Business can buy top-ups at any time; Enterprise goes through an Account Executive.

TOP-UP PRICE POINTS: UNVERIFIED — v0 does not publish fixed top-up bundle prices the way Remixer does (+1,000 = $14.99 / +2,500 = $34.99). Overage appears to be purchased as arbitrary dollar amounts of credit rather than fixed packs.

FREE-TIER LIMITS: $5 credits/month AND a hard 7 messages/day cap (two independent ceilings). Free includes Design Mode, GitHub sync and deploy to Vercel, but NOT team collaboration or "all models", and free deployments carry a "Built with v0" badge.

TRIAL: There is no time-limited free trial. The free tier is permanent, and generation is available with no account at all — I generated a complete site logged out, hitting the signup modal only after the build finished.

PUBLISHING: Publishing itself does not appear to consume credits separately (unlike Remixer, where publishing changes burns credits) — the token spend is in generation. Marked medium confidence; not explicitly stated either way in docs.
